📋 ITE Complete System Overview

Enterprise Resource Planning for Manufacturing Operations

🎯 Project Overview

ITE (Integrated Technology Enterprise) is a complete ERP system for manufacturing organizations. It automates the entire order-to-cash and manufacturing lifecycle: from customer order through job requisitioning, procurement, warehouse management, manufacturing execution, quality assurance, completion, and warranty tracking. The system eliminates manual processes, ensures compliance, prevents errors, and provides real-time visibility into all business operations with multi-tenant architecture supporting multiple organizations.

IWT (Integrated Workflow Tracking) is the companion subsystem that handles real-time tracking and monitoring of all procurement and delivery workflows. It provides live visibility into PO status, supplier performance, delivery delays, and material tracking across the entire supply chain.

▶ 🎨 Frontend Stack

Technology Stack: The frontend is built with Thymeleaf 3.x server-side templating engine running on the same Spring Boot application server (NOT a separate React SPA). This approach provides: fast initial page load, server-side rendering (SEO friendly), reduced JavaScript complexity, simpler session management, and integrated form processing.

UI Framework & Libraries: Bootstrap 4/5 for responsive grid layout and component styling. jQuery 3.x for DOM manipulation, AJAX calls to backend APIs, form validation, and event handling. DataTables.js for interactive data grids with sorting, filtering, pagination. Chart.js for dashboard charts and analytics. Select2 for enhanced dropdown selections. Moment.js for date/time formatting and calculations.

Key Frontend Features: 81 Thymeleaf templates covering all modules (requisitions, purchase orders, job management, inventory tracking, reports). Responsive design works on desktop, tablet, mobile. Role-based UI elements (show/hide fields based on user role). Real-time form validation (client-side and server-side). AJAX-based searches and filters (no full page reload). Modal dialogs for inline editing. Toast notifications for user feedback. Print and PDF export capabilities for reports.

Architecture Pattern: MVC model where Thymeleaf processes server-side models and renders HTML. jQuery handles client-side interactivity and communicates with REST APIs via AJAX. Forms submitted via POST to backend controllers with server-side validation. Session management via Spring Security and JWT tokens stored in cookies. No state management library needed (server manages session state).

▶ ⚙️ Backend Stack

Core Framework: Spring Boot 2.6.5 with embedded Tomcat server. Spring MVC for REST endpoint handling. Spring Security 5.x for JWT authentication, authorization, and RBAC enforcement. Spring Data JPA for ORM and database access. Spring Transaction Management (@Transactional) for ACID compliance and data consistency.

Database & ORM: PostgreSQL 14+ as primary database with pgcrypto extension for encryption. Hibernate 5.x as ORM framework mapping Java entities to tables. Hibernate Envers for automatic audit trail creation (versioning and change history). Flyway 7.x for database schema versioning and migrations. Connection pooling via HikariCP for performance.

Architecture & Code Structure: 45+ REST API controllers handling HTTP requests. 55+ service classes implementing business logic (requisition processing, PO generation, budget tracking, supplier selection). 80+ JPA entities representing database tables. Repository pattern using Spring Data repositories for database queries. Exception handling with custom exceptions and global exception handlers. Logging via SLF4J and Logback for debugging and monitoring.

Business Logic Components: BOM explosion algorithm for calculating material requirements. Budget tracking engine that monitors spending in real-time. Approval routing engine that determines approval chains based on amounts. PO auto-generation and supplier grouping logic. Inventory management with location-wise tracking. Automation rules engine for event-driven processes. Warranty calculation and expiration tracking. Report generation and analytics queries.

Complete Module List: (1) User Module - Authentication, authorization, role-based access control, user management. (2) Masters Module - Product catalog, suppliers, manufacturers, units, currencies, locations, departments, designations, job types, hold reasons. (3) Sales Module - Customer management, job creation, budget allocation, shipping addresses.

Modules 4-8: (4) Requisitions - Material requisition creation with BOM explosion, multi-level approval routing, PO generation. (5) Purchasing - Purchase order management, supplier selection, delivery tracking, performance metrics. (6) Stores - Warehouse operations, goods receipt, material issues, inventory tracking, stock management. (7) Job Lifecycle - Job status management, approval workflows, budget tracking, holds, revisions, warranty tracking.

Modules 9-12: (8) Tracking - Real-time PO tracking, delivery monitoring, late parts alerts, supplier performance. (9) Automation - Event-driven rules, automation engine, notifications, email templates. (10) Configurators - Job type customization, workflow builder, automation rules setup, system settings. (11) Database (Technical) - PostgreSQL schema, 95+ tables, multi-tenancy architecture, audit trails. (12) API Collection (Technical) - 200+ REST endpoints, authentication, data formats, error handling.

Module Integration Flow: Sales creates job → Triggers requisition creation → Requisition approved → Auto-generates POs grouped by supplier → POs confirmed to suppliers → Materials received and quality inspected → Materials issued to job → Manufacturing produces → QA review → Job completed → Warranty created and tracked → Final closure. All with real-time budget tracking, approval chains, audit trails, and exception handling throughout.

▶ 📊 System Hierarchy & Architecture

Three-Tier Architecture: Presentation Tier (Thymeleaf + jQuery frontend in browser), Application Tier (Spring Boot REST API processing business logic on server), Data Tier (PostgreSQL database storing all persistent data). Each tier independent and scalable. Frontend communicates with backend only via JSON APIs. Backend enforces all security and business rules.

Organizational Hierarchy: Organization (company/tenant) → Departments (Production, Sales, Finance, Warehouse, HR) → Users (assigned to departments and roles) → Designation/Roles (define permissions and approval limits). Multi-tenancy ensures complete data isolation: Organization A sees only their data, Organization B sees only their data. Database enforces isolation via organization_id filtering on all queries.

Business Process Hierarchy: Customer → Job → Requisition → Purchase Orders → Goods Receipt → Material Issue → Manufacturing → Quality Review → Job Completion → Warranty → Archive. Each level has specific approvals, validation rules, and status transitions. Holds can pause progress at any stage. Revisions allow scope changes. Complete audit trail tracks all changes and transitions.

Technical Hierarchy: API Gateway (Spring Boot REST controllers) → Service Layer (business logic classes) → Repository Layer (database access via JPA) → Database (PostgreSQL tables). This layered approach separates concerns: APIs handle HTTP protocol, Services handle business rules, Repositories handle database queries. Each layer can be tested independently. Changes in one layer don't affect others (loose coupling).

▶ 🔍 Project Algorithms Overview

Core Algorithms (8 Major): (1) BOM Explosion - Recursively expands product Bill of Materials to calculate all leaf-level materials needed for manufacturing. (2) Preferred Supplier Selection - Intelligently chooses optimal supplier based on lead time, price, quality, availability, and minimum order quantity constraints.

Algorithms 3-5: (3) Budget Tracking & Alerts - Real-time calculation of budget remaining and alert triggers at 80%, 95%, 100% thresholds. (4) Job Status Transition Validation - Enforces workflow rules preventing illegal status changes and ensuring prerequisites met (materials available, approvals received). (5) Multi-Level Approval Routing - Routes approvals through management hierarchy based on authorization limits and job type requirements.

Algorithms 6-8: (6) Automatic PO Grouping - Groups requisition items by preferred supplier to minimize purchase orders and shipping costs. (7) Inventory Quantity & Aging - Tracks stock levels across locations using FIFO (first-in-first-out) and calculates stock aging (how long held). (8) Warranty Period Tracking - Calculates warranty start/end dates, tracks claims, auto-closes on expiration, sends alerts before expiry.

Algorithm Complexity & Performance: BOM explosion O(n log n) complexity scales well even with 1000+ item BOMs. Supplier selection O(n) linear scan optimized with database indexes. Budget alerts use pre-calculated running totals (near-instant). Status validation O(1) configuration lookup. Approval routing O(log n) traverses small hierarchy. PO grouping O(n*m) where n=items, m=suppliers (typically m<10 so practical). Inventory aging O(1) per transaction. All algorithms use database-level sorting/filtering to minimize in-memory processing.

▶ 🏗️ Backend System Design for ITE

Request-Response Lifecycle (13 Steps): (1) User submits form in browser (HTML form or AJAX). (2) HTTP request reaches Spring Boot application server. (3) Spring DispatcherServlet routes to appropriate @RestController. (4) Request interceptor extracts JWT token from Authorization header. (5) JwtAuthenticationFilter validates token and extracts user/organization context. (6) TenantContext sets organization_id for this request thread. (7) Controller method calls Service layer business logic. (8) Service queries Repository (DAO) to fetch/update database. (9) Hibernate ORM translates JPA queries to SQL. (10) PostgreSQL executes queries with automatic organization_id filtering. (11) Hibernate Envers creates audit trail records for all changes. (12) Service returns result to Controller. (13) Controller serializes to JSON and returns HTTP response.

Multi-Tenancy Implementation: Shared schema strategy: all tables have organization_id column. Every query automatically includes WHERE organization_id = ? filter. TenantContext interceptor extracts organization_id from JWT token and stores in ThreadLocal. Spring Data JPA repository queries use Spring @Query annotations with organization_id filters. Impossible to query data from other organizations (application-level AND database-level enforcement). Supports 1000s of organizations in single database instance.

Security Architecture: JWT Bearer Token authentication - user logs in with email/password, receives token valid for 24 hours. Token stored in httpOnly cookie (prevents XSS access). Each API request includes Authorization: Bearer {token} header. JwtAuthenticationFilter validates token signature, expiration, and extracts claims (user_id, organization_id, roles). Spring Security uses @PreAuthorize annotations to check roles before executing methods. Role-based access control: ADMIN can manage users, MANAGER can approve requisitions, WORKER can create jobs, QA can review quality, etc. All sensitive operations audited via Hibernate Envers.

Error Handling & Reliability: Global exception handler (@ControllerAdvice) catches all exceptions and returns consistent JSON error responses with HTTP status codes (400=validation error, 401=unauthorized, 403=forbidden, 404=not found, 409=business rule violation). Transactional boundaries ensure data consistency: if any step fails, entire transaction rolled back. Optimistic locking prevents concurrent update conflicts (version field checked before update). Retry logic with exponential backoff for transient failures. Health checks and monitoring via Spring Boot Actuator. Logging at DEBUG/INFO/WARN/ERROR levels with correlation IDs for request tracing.

▶ 🗄️ Database Access & Strategy

Database Technology & Configuration: PostgreSQL 14+ chosen for reliability, ACID compliance, JSON support, and scalability. Connection pooling via HikariCP maintains 10-20 live connections (configurable), reduces connection overhead. SQL query timeout 30 seconds (prevents long-running queries blocking resources). Connection timeout 10 seconds (fast fail vs. hanging). Automatic reconnection on network failures. Connection test query validates health every 5 minutes.

Query Optimization Strategy: Indexes created on all frequently filtered columns: organization_id (every table), job_id/requisition_id/po_id (many joins), status/created_date (filtering and sorting), item_id/supplier_id (lookups). JOIN FETCH used to avoid N+1 query problems (single query with joins vs. multiple queries). Pagination (limit/offset) on large result sets (max 1000 records per page). Lazy loading for optional relationships, eager loading for required relationships. Database-level sorting preferred over application-level sorting (faster). Prepared statements prevent SQL injection.

Data Access Layer (Repositories): Spring Data JPA repositories automatically generate SQL for common operations (findById, findAll, save, delete). Custom @Query annotations for complex queries. Repository pattern provides abstraction: if switching databases (MySQL, Oracle), only repository queries change, business logic unchanged. Soft delete pattern used for data preservation: records marked inactive instead of physically deleted (enables audit trail and recovery). Cascading deletes/updates configured carefully to prevent accidental data loss.

Audit & Compliance: Hibernate Envers automatically creates audit tables for all entities marked @Audited. Every INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE creates history record with revision number, timestamp, and user. Full change history queryable: "show me all changes to Job-001", "who changed customer discount?", "when was this supplier marked inactive?". Regulatory compliance: complete audit trail demonstrates data governance. Immutable audit records (never modified/deleted) for legal evidence. Retention policies: keep 7 years of history, then archive to separate database.

▶ ☁️ Deployment & Infrastructure (Azure/Cloud)

Deployment Architecture: Spring Boot JAR packaged as Docker container for cloud deployment. Deployed to Azure Container Instances (ACI) or Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) for auto-scaling. Fronted by Azure Application Gateway or Traffic Manager for load balancing across multiple instances. PostgreSQL 14 database on Azure Database for PostgreSQL (managed service with automatic backups, failover). All traffic via HTTPS/TLS (encrypted in transit). Secrets (API keys, database passwords) stored in Azure Key Vault, injected at runtime.

Infrastructure Components: Application tier: 3-5 container instances of Spring Boot app (auto-scales based on CPU/memory load). Each instance stateless (no local session storage). Database tier: Azure Database for PostgreSQL with high availability (read replicas in secondary region). Storage tier: Azure Blob Storage for document uploads (requisitions, BOMs, invoices). Cache tier: Azure Cache for Redis caches frequently accessed data (user permissions, master data) to reduce database queries. Message queue: Azure Service Bus for async job processing (email notifications, report generation).

Monitoring & Logging: Spring Boot Actuator endpoints provide health checks (/actuator/health), metrics (/actuator/metrics), environment info (/actuator/env). Azure Monitor collects logs and metrics from all instances. Application Insights tracks performance (response time, error rates, dependency calls). Alerts configured for: CPU > 80%, Memory > 90%, Database connection pool > 15, API error rate > 5%, Deployment failures. Log aggregation via ELK Stack or Azure Log Analytics: centralized search across all instances. Slow query logs capture queries > 1 second for optimization.

Deployment Process & CI/CD: Source code in GitHub, configured with branch protection (main/master requires code review). GitHub Actions workflow triggered on push to main: (1) Run unit tests (JUnit), (2) Run integration tests (TestContainers), (3) Build Docker image, (4) Push to Azure Container Registry, (5) Deploy to staging environment, (6) Run smoke tests, (7) Deploy to production with rolling update (no downtime). Rollback capability: previous Docker image retained, can revert within 15 minutes if issues detected. Database migrations via Flyway run automatically during deployment (no manual SQL). Feature flags enable toggling features on/off without redeployment.

🔄 Core System Modules Overview

12 Integrated Modules Working Together: User Management (authentication & access), Masters (product catalogs & master data), Sales (customer & job creation), Requisitions (material requests with approvals), Purchasing (purchase orders & supplier management), Stores (warehouse & inventory), Job Lifecycle (manufacturing execution), Tracking (real-time monitoring), Automation (event-driven processes), Configurators (system customization), Database (PostgreSQL backend), API Collection (REST endpoints).

Module Integration: Each module passes data to the next in a coordinated workflow. Sales creates job → Requisitions auto-created → Purchasing auto-generates POs → Stores receives materials → Job Lifecycle issues materials → Manufacturing executes → Quality reviewed → Job completed → Warranty tracked. Approval workflows span multiple modules (requisitions need approval before POs created). Budget tracking spans from Job through final Payment. Notifications triggered across all modules.

⚡ Core Algorithms & Workflows

▶ 1️⃣ Approval Workflow Algorithm - Multi-Level Authorization

Algorithm Logic: Multi-level approval routing ensures proper authorization at each spending/authority level before allowing action execution.

approval_chain = GET_APPROVERS(requisition.amount, requisition.job_type) requisition.status = SUBMITTED FOR EACH approver IN approval_chain: 1. CREATE approval_record ( approval_id, requisition_id, approver_id, status = PENDING, created_date = NOW() ) 2. SEND_NOTIFICATION(approver.email, "Approval needed for REQ-001") 3. WAIT_FOR_RESPONSE(approval_id) IF RESPONSE = REJECTED: - UPDATE approval_record.status = REJECTED - UPDATE requisition.status = REJECTED - SEND_NOTIFICATION(requester, "REQ-001 rejected by {approver}") - RETURN FAILURE IF RESPONSE = APPROVED: - UPDATE approval_record.status = APPROVED - UPDATE approval_record.approved_date = NOW() - CONTINUE to next approver ELSE (HOLD): - UPDATE approval_record.status = HELD - WAIT_FOR_RESOLUTION - Continue when released AFTER all approvers approved: 7. UPDATE requisition.status = APPROVED 8. UPDATE requisition.approved_date = NOW() 9. TRIGGER_EVENT: PO_GENERATION 10. SEND_NOTIFICATION(procurement, "REQ-001 approved, generate POs") 11. CREATE_AUDIT_LOG("Requisition approved through all levels")

Business Example: Requisition ₹500,000 needs approval. Step 1: Department Manager (₹100K limit) can't approve, routes to Head. Step 2: Department Head (₹500K limit) approves. Step 3: Finance Manager approves. Step 4: Procurement generates POs. Without this algorithm, requisition stuck or wrong person approves (financial control loss).

Business Impact: Ensures proper authorization control preventing unauthorized spending. Eliminates approval delays by parallel notifications. Creates complete approval audit trail. Prevents bottlenecks (holds can be used for issues). Reduces time from requisition to PO creation from days to hours. Automatically routes to correct approver based on amount (no manual routing).

▶ 2️⃣ PO Generation Algorithm - Automatic Purchase Order Creation

Algorithm Logic: Automatically creates purchase orders from approved requisitions, grouping items by preferred supplier to optimize logistics.

TRIGGER: requisition.status = APPROVED 1. VALIDATE: - requisition.status = APPROVED ✓ - all_items_have_supplier = TRUE ✓ - total_amount within_budget = TRUE ✓ 2. EXTRACT requisition_items = [ {item_id, qty, unit_price, preferred_supplier}, {item_id, qty, unit_price, preferred_supplier}, ... ] 3. GROUP items by preferred_supplier: supplier_A_items = [item_1, item_5, item_8] supplier_B_items = [item_2, item_6] supplier_C_items = [item_3, item_4, item_7, item_9] 4. FOR EACH supplier_group: a. CREATE po_number = "PO-2026-{SEQUENCE}" b. CALCULATE delivery_date: delivery_date = TODAY + supplier.lead_time c. CREATE purchase_order: po = { po_id, po_number, supplier_id, status = DRAFT, total_amount = SUM(qty * unit_price), delivery_date = delivery_date, created_date = NOW() } d. FOR EACH item IN supplier_group: CREATE po_item = { po_item_id, po_id, item_id, qty_ordered, unit_price, line_total = qty * unit_price } e. SEND_EMAIL(supplier.email, po, attachment=PO PDF) f. UPDATE po.status = SENT_TO_SUPPLIER 5. AFTER all POs created: - UPDATE requisition.status = CONVERTED_TO_PO - CREATE_AUDIT_LOG("Created {n} POs from requisition") - SEND_NOTIFICATION(procurement, "POs created and sent") - SEND_NOTIFICATION(warehouse, "POs expected delivery on {dates}") - TRIGGER_AUTOMATION_RULES

Business Example: Requisition with 8 items: Motor (Supplier-A), Bearing (Supplier-B), Shaft (Supplier-A), Oil Seal (Supplier-C), Fastener (Supplier-D), Lubricant (Supplier-C), Paint (Supplier-B), Gasket (Supplier-A). Algorithm groups into 4 POs: PO-001 (Supplier-A: Motor, Shaft, Gasket), PO-002 (Supplier-B: Bearing, Paint), PO-003 (Supplier-C: Oil Seal, Lubricant), PO-004 (Supplier-D: Fastener). Each PO sent to supplier. Requisition automatically converted to PO status.

Business Impact: Eliminates manual PO creation (reduces time from hours to seconds). Groups items by supplier (reduces shipping costs, simplifies logistics). Automatically sends to suppliers (no manual emailing). Calculates delivery dates (enables accurate job scheduling). Prevents PO creation mistakes (system enforces supplier validation). Enables early warning of supply issues (delivery dates known immediately).

▶ 3️⃣ Goods Receipt Algorithm - Receive & Quality Inspection

Algorithm Logic: Validates received materials against PO, performs quality inspection, and updates inventory with accepted goods.

TRIGGER: Materials arrive from supplier 1. SCAN po_number OR enter PO details po = FIND_PO(po_number) 2. VALIDATE: - po.status IN [CONFIRMED, IN_TRANSIT] ✓ - po.supplier matches packaging_label ✓ - po.items list available ✓ 3. CREATE grn_number = "GRN-2026-{SEQUENCE}" grn = { grn_id, grn_number, po_id, received_date = TODAY, received_by = current_user, status = IN_PROGRESS } 4. FOR EACH item IN po.items: a. SCAN item_barcode OR enter manually b. COUNT actual_qty_received c. QUALITY_INSPECTION: - Visual check (damage, defects, packaging) - Label verification (correct item, expiry date) - Specification check (samples tested) d. IF INSPECTION = PASS: - Create grn_item ACCEPTED - UPDATE stock: stock.qty_available += received_qty stock.location_id = receiving_location stock.received_date = TODAY - Store quality metadata (batch number, serial, test results) e. IF INSPECTION = FAIL: - Create grn_item REJECTED - Create return_record (initiate return to supplier) - UPDATE po_item.qty_received_rejected += failed_qty - SEND_EMAIL(supplier, return_details) - Update supplier.quality_issues_count++ f. IF RECEIVED_QTY != PO_QTY: - Create discrepancy_record - IF short_qty: Notify procurement to follow up - IF excess_qty: Note for supplier clarification 5. AFTER all items processed: - UPDATE grn.status = COMPLETED - UPDATE po.status = RECEIVED - UPDATE po.delivery_actual_date = TODAY - CALCULATE po.on_time = (delivery_actual <= delivery_expected) - TRIGGER_AUTOMATION: INVOICE_MATCHING_PROCESS - SEND_NOTIFICATION(Finance, "GRN ready for invoice matching" ) - CREATE_AUDIT_LOG("GRN created: {n} accepted, {m} rejected")

Business Example: PO-001 (Steel & Parts) arrives. Receiving staff scans PO. System shows expected: Motor 1, Shaft 1. Receives Motor (1) - passes inspection ✓. Receives Shaft (1) - fails inspection (rust detected) ⚠. Creates GRN-001: 1 accepted (Motor), 1 rejected (Shaft). Stock updates: Motor +1. Quality team notified of Shaft issue. Return initiated with Supplier-A. PO status changes to RECEIVED. Finance can now match invoice to GRN.

Business Impact: Prevents defective goods entering manufacturing (quality gate). Eliminates quantity discrepancies (verified at receipt). Reduces cycle time from delivery to inventory available (hours vs. days). Creates quality metrics (what % of Supplier-A's shipments are defect-free?). Enables accurate cost tracking (only accepted goods charged). Prevents duplicate invoicing (GRN validates PO delivery).

▶ 4️⃣ Supplier Rating Algorithm - Performance Scoring

Algorithm Logic: Calculates supplier performance scores based on delivery timeliness, quality acceptance rate, and pricing competitiveness.

CALCULATE_SUPPLIER_RATING(supplier_id, period = "last 3 months"): 1. FETCH supplier metrics for period: total_pos = COUNT(po WHERE supplier_id AND status=RECEIVED) pos_on_time = COUNT(po WHERE delivery_actual <= delivery_expected) total_grns=COUNT(grn WHERE po.supplier_id) grns_accepted=COUNT(grn WHERE status=ACCEPTED) 2. CALCULATE component scores: a. ON_TIME_RATE: on_time_rate=(pos_on_time / total_pos) * 100 Example: 95 POs on-time / 100 total=95% on-time b. QUALITY_RATE: quality_rate=(grns_accepted / total_grns) * 100 Example: 380 items accepted / 400 total=95% quality c. COST_COMPETITIVENESS: supplier_avg_price=AVG(po_item.unit_price) market_avg_price=AVG(all_suppliers.unit_price for same item) cost_score=(supplier_avg_price / market_avg_price) * 100 Example: Supplier price ₹520 vs market avg ₹500 cost_score=(520/500)*100=104 (slightly expensive) IF cost_score> 100: penalize for expensive IF cost_score < 100: reward for competitive pricing 3. CALCULATE weighted overall score: overall_score=(on_time_rate * 0.35) + // 35% weight for delivery (quality_rate * 0.35) + // 35% weight for quality ((100 - cost_score) * 0.30) // 30% weight for value Example calculation: overall=(95 * 0.35) + (95 * 0.35) + (0 * 0.30) overall=33.25 + 33.25 + 0=66.5 4. ASSIGN RATING TIER: IF overall_score>= 90: rating = 5 STARS "Excellent" ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ IF overall_score >= 75: rating = 4 STARS "Good" ⭐⭐⭐⭐ IF overall_score >= 60: rating = 3 STARS "Fair" ⭐⭐⭐ IF overall_score >= 45: rating = 2 STARS "Poor" ⭐⭐ IF overall_score < 45: rating=1 STAR "Unacceptable" ⭐ 5. UPDATE supplier master: UPDATE supplier SET on_time_rate={95%}, quality_rate={95%}, cost_score={104}, overall_rating={4 STARS}, last_rating_date=TODAY, rating_trend=IMPROVING/STABLE/DECLINING 6. STORE historical record: INSERT supplier_rating_history Track rating changes over time (shows trends) 7. TRIGGER actions based on rating: IF rating=1 STAR: - FLAG for procurement review - REDUCE order volume - SEND corrective action request to supplier IF rating=5 STARS: - INCREASE preferred status - OFFER volume discounts (negotiate better terms) - HIGHLIGHT as preferred supplier

Business Example: Supplier-A metrics (last 3 months): 100 POs, 95 on-time (95%), 400 items, 380 accepted (95%), average price ₹520 vs market ₹500 (cost_score=104). Overall score = (95×0.35) + (95×0.35) + (0×0.30) = 66.5 = 3 STARS "Fair". Trend: Excellent delivery, good quality, slightly expensive. Procurement recommends: Use for critical items (reliable delivery), negotiate price reduction, or find cheaper alternative for non-critical items.

Business Impact: Provides data-driven supplier selection (use best performers). Identifies underperformers (who needs corrective action?). Negotiation leverage (use rating to request improvements). Supplier development (rating improvement shows success). Risk management (avoid unreliable suppliers for critical items). Continuous improvement (measure and track performance over time). Competitive bidding (ratings guide which suppliers to invite for bids).

▶ 🔄 End-to-End Order Workflow

Complete Business Process Flow: From customer order through final payment closure, tracking all data transformations and system events.

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ ITE END-TO-END ORDER WORKFLOW │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ 1. CUSTOMER ORDER RECEIVED ↓ 2. SALES CREATES JOB job = {job_number, customer, description, budget, job_type} Status: DRAFT → QUOTE → APPROVED ↓ 3. JOB APPROVED → MATERIAL REQUISITION CREATED (AUTO) System performs BOM explosion requisition = {req_number, job_id, items[], total_amount} Status: DRAFT ↓ 4. REQUISITION SUBMITTED FOR APPROVAL Multi-level approval chain Routing: Manager → Head → Finance → Procurement Each level: APPROVE / REJECT / HOLD Status: SUBMITTED → (Under Review) → APPROVED ↓ 5. PURCHASE ORDERS AUTO-GENERATED (when requisition APPROVED) Supplier grouping algorithm creates POs po1 = {Supplier-A, items[], amount, delivery_date} po2 = {Supplier-B, items[], amount, delivery_date} po3 = {Supplier-C, items[], amount, delivery_date} Status: DRAFT → CONFIRMED → SENT_TO_SUPPLIER ↓ 6. MATERIALS ORDERED FROM SUPPLIERS POs sent via email/API to suppliers Supplier confirms delivery schedule Tracking begins (expected delivery dates known) ↓ 7. GOODS RECEIVED & QUALITY INSPECTED Supplier shipments arrive at warehouse For each shipment: - Count items vs. PO - Inspect quality (visual, labels, specs) - Accept good items → Update inventory - Reject defects → Create return records Status: PO marked RECEIVED ↓ 8. MATERIAL ISSUED TO JOB Manufacturing starts (job status: IN_PROGRESS) Warehouse issues materials to job Stock decreases Job cost increases (material cost added) Status: Material Issue created ↓ 9. MANUFACTURING EXECUTION Job status: IN_PROGRESS Real-time tracking: - Labor time logged - Resources consumed tracked - Quality checkpoints monitored Budget remaining: tracked in real-time If budget 80% spent → ALERT Finance ↓ 10. QUALITY ASSURANCE REVIEW Job status: REVIEW QA checks: specifications met, defects, compliance If issues found: Create hold, document defects If approved: Ready for delivery Status: REVIEW → COMPLETED ↓ 11. DELIVERY TO CUSTOMER Job status: COMPLETED Job packaged, shipped to customer Delivery date recorded Final cost calculated (material + labor + overhead) ↓ 12. INVOICE GENERATED & SENT Invoice created based on job completion Amount = Final Cost + Markup/Profit Sent to customer for payment Status: INVOICED ↓ 13. PAYMENT RECEIVED Customer pays invoice (cash/check/wire) Payment recorded, matched to invoice Cash flow impact recorded Status: PAID ↓ 14. WARRANTY PERIOD STARTS Warranty created automatically (12 months typical) Warranty claims tracked if defects found Customer can raise claims within period ↓ 15. FINAL CLOSURE Warranty period expires Job archived All data preserved (historical record) Status: CLOSED Financial closure: - Revenue recognized - All costs settled - Profitability calculated - Supplier ratings updated ↓ WORKFLOW COMPLETE - JOB CYCLE FINISHED

Timeline Example: Job-001 created July 20 (budget ₹100K). Requisition submitted July 21, approved July 22. POs generated/sent July 23 (expected delivery July 30). Materials received July 29-30. Manufacturing July 31-Aug 4 (5 days). QA review Aug 4. Delivered Aug 5. Invoice sent Aug 6. Customer pays Aug 20. Warranty starts Aug 5, expires Aug 4 next year. Total calendar cycle: 16 days from order to delivery.

Business Impact: Provides complete visibility from order to payment. Eliminates manual handoffs between departments. Prevents workflow bottlenecks (status tracking identifies delays). Enables accurate costing (labor, material tracked at each step). Creates audit trail for compliance (every step recorded). Enables profitability analysis (know cost and revenue per job). Risk management (identify issues early via holds). Customer satisfaction (customer can track delivery status).

▶ 📋 10+ Core Algorithms Summary

Complete Algorithm Suite: ITE implements 10+ core algorithms covering all critical business processes. Each algorithm optimized for accuracy, performance, and reliability to ensure smooth manufacturing operations without manual intervention.

1. Approval Workflow - Multi-level authorizations ensuring proper spending control
2. PO Generation - Auto-create purchase orders from requisitions, group by supplier
3. Goods Receipt - Receive materials, quality inspect, update inventory
4. Material Issue - Allocate materials to manufacturing jobs, track costs
5. Material Return - Handle returns from manufacturing, reverse transactions
6. Stock Management - Track inventory levels, reorder points, location-wise tracking
7. Job Cost Calculation - Calculate labor + material + overhead costs per job
8. Supplier Rating - Score suppliers on delivery, quality, cost (weighted 35/35/30%)
9. Notification System - Multi-channel alerts (email, SMS, in-app) for all events
10. Payment Processing - Vendor payment workflows, invoice matching, reconciliation
11. BOM Explosion - Recursively expand products to leaf-level materials
12. Budget Tracking - Real-time spending with alerts at 80%, 95%, 100% thresholds

Algorithm Performance: All algorithms optimized for production use. Execution times: Approval workflow (< 1 sec), PO generation (< 5 sec even for 100 items), Goods receipt (< 3 sec per item), Supplier rating (< 1 sec), Stock management (< 100ms), Budget tracking (real-time, < 10ms). Algorithms handle edge cases: supplier unavailable (fallback to secondary), quality issues (hold for resolution), budget overrun (alert escalation), delivery delays (supplier rating impact).

Reliability & Failsafes: All algorithms transactional (ACID guarantees). Partial failures handled gracefully (if PO generation fails for Supplier-B, Supplier-A POs still created). Audit trail captures every decision (why was PO created for this supplier?). Retry logic for transient failures (network timeouts automatically retry). Manual overrides allowed for exceptions (bypass supplier validation if needed, with approval). Monitoring tracks algorithm execution (alerts if unusually slow or failing frequently).

Business Value & Benefits

  • ✅ Quality Enforcement - Approval gates at each stage, QA checkpoints, defect tracking

👤 User Module - Access Control & Security

Authentication and Role-Based Access Management

Module Summary

Purpose: Controls who accesses the system and what they can do. Ensures each employee has appropriate access based on role and responsibilities.

User Module Hierarchy

▶ 🔐 Authentication - User Login & JWT Tokens

What It Is: Authentication verifies the user's identity (proves they are who they claim). Uses JWT (JSON Web Tokens) for stateless, secure token-based authentication instead of session cookies.

Authentication Flow (10 Steps):

Step Action Details
1 User navigates to login page Browser loads /login endpoint, renders login form
2 User enters email & password Form submits to POST /authenticate endpoint via HTTPS
3 System finds user by email Database query: SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = 'user@company.com'
4 System verifies password Compares submitted password hash with stored Argon2 hash using Spring Security
5 Password matches → Load user data Fetch: user_id, email, roles, organization_id, department_id from database
6 Generate JWT token Token payload: {user_id, email, roles[], organization_id, exp: now+24hrs}
7 Sign token with secret key HMACSHA256(payload, secret_key) = signature
8 Return token to client Response includes: {token, user_id, email, roles, organization_id}
9 Store token in httpOnly cookie Browser stores in secure httpOnly cookie (prevents XSS access)
10 Redirect to dashboard User logged in, can now make authenticated API calls

JWT Token Structure: Header.Payload.Signature format. Example: eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjoxMjMsIm9yZ19pZCI6NDUsImV4cCI6MTczMjMwOTAwMH0.KL1BPH9CcOKmkebl8H7YqJQVHh2dMYo7Z9Q3W8Z5pZs. Payload contains: user_id, organization_id, roles[], exp (expiration timestamp in Unix seconds). Token valid for 24 hours, then user must log in again.

Token Usage in Requests: Every API call includes Authorization header: Authorization: Bearer {token}. Server extracts token, validates signature using secret key (ensures not tampered), checks expiration (not expired), extracts organization_id and user_id. If valid, request allowed. If invalid/expired, returns 401 Unauthorized. TenantContext.set(organization_id) stores org for this request thread.

Security Features: Passwords stored as Argon2 hashes (industry standard, slow hash prevents brute force). HTTPS enforced (tokens encrypted in transit). httpOnly cookies prevent JavaScript access (XSS protection). CSRF tokens prevent cross-site attacks. Token expiration (24 hours) limits damage if token stolen. Refresh token mechanism allows extending session without re-entering password. Failed login attempts tracked (throttle after 5 failures, temporary lockout).

▶ 🔑 Authorization - Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)

What It Is: Authorization controls what authenticated users can do (access control). After login verified, system checks: does this user have permission to view this job? Can they approve requisition? Can they delete customer? Uses Spring Security @PreAuthorize annotations.

Authorization Implementation: Spring Security @PreAuthorize("hasRole('MANAGER')") on controller methods ensures only MANAGER role users access endpoint. If user lacks role, Spring Security returns 403 Forbidden. Example: @PreAuthorize("hasRole('MANAGER') or hasRole('ADMIN')") allows MANAGER or ADMIN. @PreAuthorize("hasPermission(#jobId, 'EDIT')") fine-grained permission checking (can this user edit job #123?).

Method-Level Security: Service methods decorated with @Secured({"ROLE_MANAGER", "ROLE_FINANCE"}) restrict to specific roles. Transactional methods (@Transactional) maintain authorization context throughout database operations. Audit interceptor logs which role performed what action (user_id, role, action, timestamp, resource_id). Prevents privilege escalation (user can't change own role via API).

Field-Level Access Control: Sensitive fields (salary, customer_credit_limit, supplier_cost) hidden from non-authorized roles. Serialization filters in REST responses remove restricted fields. Example: WORKER sees job status/deadline but not job profit/cost breakdown (visible only to MANAGER/FINANCE). Database queries include row-level security (WHERE user_id = ? AND role IN (...)). Multi-layer security: if field filter missed, database query filters prevent access.

Complete Role Permission Matrix (7 Roles × 12 Core Permissions):

Quality Inspection (accept/reject) ✅ Yes ❌ No ❌ No ❌ No ✅ Yes ❌ No ❌ No

Role Descriptions with Approval Limits:

Role Title Approval Limit Responsibilities
ADMIN System Administrator Unlimited System configuration, user management, role assignment, organization settings, audit trail access, system backups, security policies
MANAGER Department Manager ₹100,000 Approve requisitions up to ₹100K, approve POs, manage team, modify job status, create/delete jobs, view department budgets and reports
FINANCE Finance/Procurement Head ₹500,000 Approve high-value requisitions (₹100K-₹500K), approve POs, manage invoices/payments, budget tracking, financial reports, supplier management
WORKER Manufacturing Worker None (No approval) Receive goods (GRN), issue materials to jobs, update job status, view assigned job details, time logging for labor tracking
QA Quality Assurance Lead None (No approval) Quality inspection on goods receipt, accept/reject materials, update QA status on jobs, create defect records, quality reports, warranty claim review
CLERK Warehouse Clerk None (No approval) Receive goods and create GRN, issue materials, manage inventory, track stock levels, create material returns, warehouse reports
SALES Sales Executive None (No approval) Create jobs/sales orders, manage customer accounts, track job status, generate sales reports, customer communication, delivery coordination

Role Hierarchy & Escalation: ADMIN > FINANCE > MANAGER > WORKER/CLERK/QA/SALES (horizontal, not hierarchical). Users can have MULTIPLE roles simultaneously (Manager + Finance role = combined permissions). Approval chain follows: Requisition ₹50K approved by Manager → Requisition ₹500K requires Manager + Finance approval → Requisition ₹2M requires CFO approval. Each step in chain notified, each must approve before proceeding to next.

Permission Combination Examples: User with [MANAGER + WORKER] roles: Can approve requisitions (Manager) AND issue materials (Worker) AND receive goods (Worker). User with [QA + CLERK] roles: Can inspect quality (QA) AND receive goods (Clerk) AND manage inventory (Clerk). This flexible combination supports cross-functional team members. Permissions are additive (having more roles = more access, never removes permissions).

▶ 🏢 Multi-Tenant System - Organization Isolation

What Is Multi-Tenancy: Single ITE instance serves 1000s of organizations (companies) with complete data isolation. Organization A cannot see Organization B's data. No data cross-contamination. Reduces infrastructure costs (1 database instead of 1000 databases). Simplifies management (1 codebase, many customers).

Implementation Strategy: Shared Schema Approach - All tables have organization_id column. Every query automatically filters by organization_id. Example: SELECT * FROM jobs WHERE organization_id = 45 ensures Organization-45 sees only their jobs. TenantContext interceptor extracts organization_id from JWT token and adds to every query (automatic, transparent). Spring Data JPA repositories use @Query with organization_id filter. Direct SQL queries include WHERE organization_id = %. Database-level AND application-level filtering (defense in depth).

Aspect Implementation Detail Security Level
Data Isolation organization_id in EVERY table (users, jobs, requisitions, pos, customers, suppliers, stock, etc.). Row-level filtering on all queries. WHERE organization_id = ? mandatory. 🔒 Strong
User Association Each user belongs to exactly ONE organization. User record: user_id, email, password_hash, organization_id, department_id, status. Cannot change own organization. 🔒 Strong
JWT Token Token payload includes: user_id, organization_id, roles[], email. Server extracts organization_id from token, no possibility of mismatch or fraud. 🔒 Strong
TenantContext Spring interceptor stores organization_id in ThreadLocal for request duration. All services access via TenantContext.getOrganizationId(). Automatic, impossible to bypass. 🔒 Strong
Query Filtering Spring Data JPA repositories auto-add WHERE organization_id = {tenantId} to all queries. Custom @Query annotations must include organization_id filter. Code review enforces compliance. 🔒 Strong
Cross-Organization Check If user from Org-A tries to access resource from Org-B, system returns 404 (not found) or 403 (forbidden). Audit logged: "Unauthorized access attempt by user_id". 🔒 Strong
Organization Configuration Each organization has master record: org_id, org_name, tax_id, country, industry, subscription_level, admin_contact. Billing tracked per organization (SaaS model). 💰 Commercial

Real-World Example: Organization A and Organization B both use ITE. User-A (works at Org-A) logs in → JWT token contains org_id=45. User-B (works at Org-B) logs in → JWT token contains org_id=89. User-A queries jobs → System adds WHERE organization_id=45 → Sees only Org-A's 50 jobs. User-B queries same endpoint → WHERE organization_id=89 → Sees only Org-B's 200 jobs. Even if User-A tries SQL injection or parameter tampering to access Org-B data, database has CHECK constraint organization_id IN (SELECT org_id WHERE user_id=?) preventing cross-org access.

Data Isolation Guarantees: Application-Level: @PreAuthorize checks user's organization_id, repository filters by organization_id. Database-Level: Foreign key constraints, CHECK constraints, permissions (user roles have org_id scope). Network-Level: HTTPS encryption, no plaintext data transmission. If all layers bypassed, audit log captures suspicious access, alerts security team. Enterprise-grade: SOC2/ISO27001 compliant, designed for healthcare/finance data handling.

▶ 👥 User Account Lifecycle

User Creation Process: Admin creates user via /user/submit endpoint. System generates: user_id, validates email unique across organization, creates user record. Password: temporary random password generated (e.g., "Temp@12345x"), hashed with Argon2, stored. Welcome email sent: "Welcome to ITE! Your temporary password is..." User logs in with email + temp password. System forces password change on first login (must create personal password). Account status set to ACTIVE. Audit log: "User created by admin_id, assigned roles [MANAGER], organization_id=45".

Role Assignment: Admin assigns one or more roles via /user/{userId}/role endpoint. Example: Assign MANAGER role to user-123. System creates roleaccess junction record: user_id=123, role_id=MANAGER, assigned_date=NOW(). Can assign MULTIPLE roles: MANAGER + FINANCE role on same user. Immediate effect: Next login, user has combined permissions from both roles. Audit log: "MANAGER role assigned to user_id by admin_id".

Account Deactivation (Soft Delete): Admin deactivates user via /user/{userId}/status endpoint. System sets user.status = INACTIVE. User cannot login (authentication fails). All historical data preserved (no deletion, soft delete). Job assignments remain (shows "completed by INACTIVE user" with name). Audit trail intact. Can reactivate later (status = ACTIVE). Deactivation reason captured: "Employee resigned", "On leave", "Role changed".

Password Reset & Security: User forgets password → Click "Forgot Password" → Enters email. System generates reset token (32-char random), valid for 1 hour, stores in database. Email sent with reset link: "https://app.com/reset?token={token}". User clicks link → Page asks for new password. System validates token (not expired, not used), updates password hash. Reset token marked as used (can't reuse). Audit log: "Password reset for user_id, initiated from IP_address". Maximum 5 reset attempts per hour (prevent spam).

▶ 🔒 Security Best Practices in User Module

Password Security: Stored as Argon2 hash (never plain text). Argon2 is memory-hard algorithm, takes ~1 second to hash single password (prevents brute force attacks, even with stolen database). Password requirements enforced: minimum 8 characters, 1 uppercase, 1 number, 1 special character. Previous password history tracked (can't reuse last 3 passwords). Automatic expiration: users must change password every 90 days (configurable).

Session & Token Security: JWT tokens valid for 24 hours (short-lived, limits token theft window). httpOnly cookies prevent JavaScript XSS access. Secure flag on cookies (HTTPS only, not transmitted over HTTP). Refresh token mechanism: separate long-lived token (7 days) for refreshing session without password. Token revocation list: logged-out tokens added to Redis cache, checked on each request (prevents reuse after logout).

Audit & Compliance: Every login logged: user_id, timestamp, IP address, browser, success/failure. Failed login attempts logged: email, timestamp, IP address, failure reason. Suspicious patterns trigger alerts: 5 failed attempts → temporary account lockout (15 min). User activity logged: what user did, when, from which IP. Audit logs retained for 7 years (compliance requirement). Reports: "Who accessed customer data on July 20?" "Who modified this PO?" "All changes made by user_id".

Admin Oversight: ADMIN role requires second factor: password + security question or TOTP app. Cannot bulk assign admin role (prevents accidental mass privilege escalation). Admin actions logged separately with enhanced detail. Admin login notifications sent to backup admin (if primary compromised). Admin can view all user activity, reset passwords, disable accounts. Regular access reviews: quarterly audit of who has admin access (ensure still needed).
