⚙️ Masters Module - Reference Data

Central Repository of Master Data Used Across System

Module Summary

Purpose: Stores master data (information that doesn't change frequently but is referenced everywhere). Change once, applies to all orders.

Masters Module - 12 Master Data Types

Business Value

  • ✅ Change once, applies everywhere
  • ✅ Prevents conflicting data
  • ✅ Maintains consistency across system
  • ✅ Central audit trail for changes

🏭 Master Data Types - Detailed Explanations

▶ 🏭 Manufacturers - Item Source Management

What It Is: Master record for companies that manufacture/produce items. Tracks which manufacturers produce which items, their contact information, delivery timelines, and manufacturing capabilities.

Why Used in ITE: Manufacturing organizations need to know which manufacturers produce which items. When creating requisitions, system needs to identify primary manufacturer for each item to ensure correct sourcing. Multiple manufacturers for same item provides backup supplier option if primary unavailable.

Key Information Stored: Manufacturer name, registration number, tax ID, contact person, phone, email, address, website, lead time (days to deliver after order), manufacturing capacity (units per month), quality rating (1-5 stars), minimum order quantity, price per unit by item. Each item can have multiple manufacturers with preference ranking.

Project Understanding: When requisition created for item "Steel Pipes A", system queries Manufacturers table. Finds: Manufacturer 1 (Steel Corp) - primary, 5-day lead time, ₹100/unit. Manufacturer 2 (Pipes Inc) - backup, 7-day lead time, ₹105/unit. If Steel Corp unavailable, system auto-selects Pipes Inc. Prevents job delays due to single supplier dependency.

Business Workflow: 1. Procurement adds new manufacturer (Steel Corp Ltd) 2. Fill: Company name, registration, tax ID, contact details 3. Add manufacturing capacity (10,000 units/month) 4. Link to items this manufacturer produces (Steel Pipes A, B, C) 5. Set lead time for each item (5-7 days typical) 6. Set minimum order quantity (1000 units minimum) 7. Set unit pricing for each item (updates when negotiated) 8. Mark as preferred/backup manufacturer 9. System uses this data during requisition processing 10. Complete audit trail tracks price changes and negotiations

▶ 🤝 Suppliers - Material & Component Vendors

What It Is: Master record for external vendors who supply materials, components, and finished goods to the organization. Different from manufacturers - suppliers sell products, while manufacturers produce them. One supplier can source from multiple manufacturers.

Why Used in ITE: Purchasing department works directly with suppliers. Every purchase order is placed with a supplier. System needs complete supplier information to: generate accurate POs, calculate lead times for delivery scheduling, enforce payment terms, track performance metrics (on-time delivery %, quality), manage credit limits, prevent duplicate supplier records.

Key Information Stored: Supplier company name, GST number, tax ID, bank details, contact persons (purchase, accounts, operations), primary email and phone, postal address, payment terms (Net 15/30/45/60 days), credit limit (maximum outstanding amount), preferred shipping method, quality rating, on-time delivery percentage, lead time for each item they supply, unit pricing, minimum order quantity, preferred supplier flag (default selection for items).

Project Understanding: Requisition contains 50 items needing approval. After approval, system auto-groups items by preferred supplier. Result: Item X, Y, Z → Supplier A (lead time 5 days) creates PO-001. Item M, N → Supplier B (lead time 7 days) creates PO-002. Each PO sent to respective supplier. System prevents late deliveries by selecting suppliers with 5-day lead time when job needs 7-day delivery. Performance tracking shows Supplier A: 98% on-time, Supplier B: 85% on-time. Next time, system prioritizes Supplier A.

Business Workflow: 1. Admin adds new supplier (Steel & Parts Ltd) 2. Fill company information (GST, tax ID, address) 3. Add contact persons (for orders, invoices, accounts) 4. Set payment terms (Net 30 days) 5. Set credit limit (₹5,000,000 max outstanding) 6. Set lead time for items supplied (3-5 days typical) 7. Set minimum order quantity (500 units minimum) 8. Link items this supplier provides (pricing for each) 9. Set quality rating (based on inspection results) 10. Mark as preferred supplier for specific items 11. System auto-selects during requisition processing 12. Track performance (on-time %, defects, payment history) 13. Annual supplier review and rating update

▶ 📏 Units - Measurement Standards

What It Is: Master record for units of measurement used across the system. Standardizes how quantities are expressed (kilogram, pieces, liter, meter, dozen, box, etc.). Handles unit conversions to calculate equivalent quantities.

Why Used in ITE: Different items measured in different units. Steel Pipe measured in meters. Ball Bearings counted in pieces. Engine Oil in liters. When requisition requires 100 pieces of nuts but supplier sells in boxes (minimum 50 pieces/box = 2 boxes), system must convert. Without units master, calculations error-prone and conversions manually calculated.

Key Information Stored: Unit code (KG, PCS, LTR, MTR, DZN, BOX, DRUM, HR, DAY, TON), unit name (Kilogram, Pieces, Liter), base unit for conversions (what is 1 base unit?), conversion factor table (1 DZN = 12 PCS, 1 BOX = 100 PCS, 1 TON = 1000 KG), active/inactive status.

Project Understanding: Job needs 144 bolt pieces. In inventory: Bolts stored in dozens (1 DZN = 12 PCS). System knows: 144 PCS ÷ 12 = 12 DZN. Issues 12 dozen to manufacturing. Without units master would need manual conversion and errors would cause stockouts or excess stock. Example 2: Oil requisition 100 LTR. Supplier sells in 5-liter cans (1 CAN = 5 LTR). System calculates: 100 LTR ÷ 5 = 20 cans. Orders 20 cans from supplier. Accurate inventory and costing depends on correct unit conversions.

Business Workflow: 1. Admin defines standard units used in organization 2. Create unit: Code=PCS, Name=Pieces (individual items) 3. Create unit: Code=DZN, Name=Dozen (12 pieces) 4. Create unit: Code=BOX, Name=Box (100 pieces) 5. Set conversions: 1 DZN = 12 PCS, 1 BOX = 12 DZN (144 PCS) 6. Create unit: Code=KG, Name=Kilogram 7. Create unit: Code=TON, Name=Ton (1000 KG) 8. Set conversions: 1 TON = 1000 KG 9. Create unit: Code=LTR, Name=Liter 10. Create unit: Code=CAN, Name=5-Liter Can (5 LTR) 11. System uses conversions in requisitions and inventory 12. Prevents ordering mistakes and stock calculation errors 13. Enables accurate cost calculation and tracking

▶ ⚙️ Item Types - Material Classification

What It Is: Master record that classifies items into types based on how they are handled, accounted for, and used in the manufacturing process. Different item types follow different accounting and inventory rules.

Why Used in ITE: Raw materials, components, finished goods, and consumables need different treatment. Raw Material purchased for inventory, costed to jobs, tracked carefully. Consumable (like lubricant) purchased and immediately expensed, not tracked in inventory. Finished Good produced internally, sold to customers, highest value. Service (labor) non-tangible, no inventory tracking. System needs to know item type to apply correct business logic.

Key Information Stored: Item type code (RM, CMP, CSM, FG, SRV), item type name (Raw Material, Component, Consumable, Finished Good, Service), description explaining usage, accounting treatment (how to cost), inventory treatment (track or expense immediately), impact on financial reports.

Project Understanding: Item "Steel Pipe A" classified as RAW_MATERIAL. Job needs 100 units. System purchases from supplier, receives to inventory, issues to job, tracks in stock ledger, costs to job (material cost). Item "Lubricant" classified as CONSUMABLE. Same 100 units purchased but immediately expensed (not added to inventory), costed as consumable expense, not tracked in stock levels. Item "Motor Assembly" classified as FINISHED_GOOD. Produced internally via manufacturing job, sold to customers, highest value, full traceability from raw materials through assembly.

Business Workflow: 1. Admin creates item type: RAW_MATERIAL 2. Description: Basic materials purchased from suppliers 3. Accounting: Capitalize to inventory, cost to jobs 4. Inventory: Track stock levels, prevent stockouts 5. Admin creates item type: COMPONENT 6. Description: Sub-parts used in assembly 7. Accounting: Capitalize to inventory, track per job 8. Admin creates item type: CONSUMABLE 9. Description: Supplies, utilities, non-inventory items 10. Accounting: Expense immediately, don't track stock 11. Admin creates item type: FINISHED_GOOD 12. Description: Products produced and sold to customers 13. Accounting: Track from raw material through final assembly 14. Admin creates item type: SERVICE 15. Description: Labor, repairs, non-tangible services 16. Accounting: Expense as incurred, no inventory tracking

▶ 📮 Shipping Address - Delivery Locations

What It Is: Master record for physical delivery locations. Customers often have multiple locations (head office, factory, warehouse). Each needs separate shipping address record for accurate order delivery.

Why Used in ITE: When creating sales order, must specify where to deliver finished goods. Customer ACME has Delhi factory and Mumbai warehouse. Same job might have materials delivered to Mumbai warehouse but finished product delivered to Delhi. System must track multiple addresses per customer to prevent delivery errors.

Key Information Stored: Location name (Delhi Factory, Mumbai Warehouse), street address, city, state, postal code, country, contact person at location, phone number, email, special delivery instructions (gate number, parking info, security requirements), primary/billing/shipping address flags, unloading facilities available (dock, lift), working hours, receiving schedule.

Project Understanding: ACME Manufacturing has 3 locations: Head Office (Delhi), Manufacturing Unit (Pune), Warehouse (Mumbai). Sales creates job: deliver finished assembly to Manufacturing Unit (Pune). Materials arrive at Warehouse (Mumbai). System knows different delivery locations, sends goods to correct place. Without this, goods delivered to wrong location, job delayed, customer frustrated. Each location has different receiving hours and special instructions (Pune factory needs delivery 9 AM-5 PM, Mumbai warehouse 24/7 availability).

Business Workflow: 1. Admin adds customer ACME Manufacturing 2. Add shipping address #1: Head Office (Delhi) 3. Fill complete address, contact, phone 4. Mark as: Billing Address, Primary Address 5. Add shipping address #2: Factory (Pune) 6. Fill complete address, contact, phone 7. Mark as: Shipping Address (for delivering goods) 8. Add special instructions: Dock available 8 AM-6 PM 9. Add shipping address #3: Warehouse (Mumbai) 10. Fill complete address, different contact person 11. Note: 24/7 receiving available 12. Sales uses dropdown to select where to ship each job 13. System ensures goods delivered to correct location 14. Prevents delivery delays and customer disputes

▶ 💱 Currency - Multi-Currency Support

What It Is: Master record for currencies supported in the system. Global enterprises work with international suppliers in USD, EUR, GBP. System must track exchange rates and convert between currencies for reporting and invoicing.

Why Used in ITE: Supplier in USA quotes in USD ($100/unit). Supplier in Europe quotes in EUR (€80/unit). To compare prices and make purchasing decisions, must convert to base currency (INR). Exchange rates change daily. System must use current rates for accurate costing and invoicing.

Key Information Stored: Currency code (INR, USD, EUR, GBP, JPY), currency symbol (₹, $, €, £, ¥), currency name, is base currency flag (usually INR for Indian company), exchange rate vs. base currency (updated daily), active/inactive status, number of decimal places (most use 2, Japanese Yen uses 0).

Project Understanding: Job needs Steel from USA supplier (USD 5000) and Chemicals from Germany supplier (EUR 3000). Base currency is INR. Today's rates: USD 1 = ₹83, EUR 1 = ₹90. System converts: USD 5000 × 83 = ₹415,000. EUR 3000 × 90 = ₹270,000. Total in INR = ₹685,000. Invoice generated in INR with exchange rates noted. Next month rates change: USD 1 = ₹82, EUR 1 = ₹88. System updates rates, future invoices use new rates. Historical invoices preserve original rates for audit trail.

Business Workflow: 1. Admin sets up base currency: INR (Indian Rupees) 2. Add currency: USD (US Dollar), Symbol: $ 3. Set exchange rate: 1 USD = 83 INR 4. Add currency: EUR (Euro), Symbol: € 5. Set exchange rate: 1 EUR = 90 INR 6. Add currency: GBP (British Pound), Symbol: £ 7. Set exchange rate: 1 GBP = 104 INR 8. Daily: Update exchange rates from currency feeds 9. When creating PO in USD: Amount shown in both USD and INR 10. When comparing supplier quotes: Auto-convert to base currency 11. Invoice generated in INR with exchange rates noted 12. Financial reports in base currency (INR) 13. Multi-currency reporting capability for consolidated view

▶ 📍 Location - Warehouse & Storage

What It Is: Master record for physical warehouse and factory locations where inventory is stored. Tracks hierarchical location structure from country down to specific shelves/bins for inventory management.

Why Used in ITE: Large organizations have inventory at multiple warehouses (Delhi, Mumbai, Bangalore). When goods received, must specify which warehouse to store at. When manufacturing needs materials, system must know location to issue from. Location-wise stock tracking enables: just-in-time ordering, prevents excess inventory, enables accurate cost tracking per location.

Key Information Stored: Location code (MAIN-BNG, REGION-CHN), location name (Bangalore Main Warehouse), location type (Warehouse/Factory/Customer Site), hierarchical structure (Country → State → City → Specific Location), storage capacity (how many units can store), manager/responsible person, contact person, phone, email, working hours, receiving schedule (when goods can be accepted), shipping schedule (when goods shipped out).

Project Understanding: Goods received from supplier: 1000 units Steel Pipes. Warehouse has 3 locations: MAIN-BNG (capacity 5000), REGION-CHN (capacity 3000), REGION-DLH (capacity 2000). GRN (Goods Receipt Note) specifies receive at MAIN-BNG. System adds 1000 units to MAIN-BNG stock. Later manufacturing needs 100 units. System issues from nearest location: MAIN-BNG (closest to factory, saves transport cost). Stock tracking shows: MAIN-BNG: 900 units, REGION-CHN: 1500 units, REGION-DLH: 500 units. Finance can calculate inventory value by location.

Business Workflow: 1. Admin creates warehouse location: Bangalore Main 2. Location code: MAIN-BNG 3. Fill address: Plot 123, Bangalore 4. Set capacity: 50,000 units maximum 5. Assign manager: Vikram Kumar 6. Set receiving hours: 9 AM - 5 PM 7. Add regional location: Chennai Region 8. Location code: REGION-CHN 9. Set capacity: 30,000 units 10. Add Delhi location: REGION-DLH 11. When GRN created: Select receiving location 12. Stock tracked by location (MAIN-BNG: 1000, REGION-CHN: 500) 13. Material issue specifies issue-from location 14. Enables efficient inventory management and cost tracking

▶ 📧 Email Template - Automated Notifications

What It Is: Master record for email notification templates used throughout the system. Enables professional, consistent automated communication for business events (order confirmation, delivery notification, payment reminder).

Why Used in ITE: Multiple people need notifications when business events occur. Requisition submitted → Send email to approval manager. PO confirmed → Send email to supplier. Job completed → Send email to customer and warranty team. Without templates, each notification manually written, inconsistent messaging, prone to errors. Templates ensure professional, consistent communication.

Key Information Stored: Template code (ORDER_CONFIRMATION, GRN_RECEIVED, INVOICE_SENT), template name, email subject line (can include variables like {CUSTOMER_NAME}), email body (HTML formatted), variables supported ({CUSTOMER_NAME}, {ORDER_ID}, {AMOUNT}, {DELIVERY_DATE}, {JOB_NUMBER}, {LINK}), recipient list (to, cc, bcc addresses), active/inactive flag.

Project Understanding: Job completed. Automation rule triggers: ON job.status = COMPLETED, send email using template "JOB_COMPLETION_NOTICE". Template: Subject="Your Order {JOB_NUMBER} is Complete", Body="Dear {CUSTOMER_NAME}, Your job {JOB_NUMBER} completed on {COMPLETION_DATE}. Amount: {AMOUNT}. [Link to invoice]". System substitutes variables: {JOB_NUMBER}→ORG-2026-00001, {CUSTOMER_NAME}→ACME Manufacturing, {COMPLETION_DATE}→July 30, 2026. Email sent automatically. No manual typing, consistent format, professional appearance.

Business Workflow: 1. Admin creates email template 2. Code: ORDER_CONFIRMATION 3. Name: Order Placement Confirmation 4. Subject: Order {ORDER_ID} Confirmed - {CUSTOMER_NAME} 5. Body (HTML): Dear {CUSTOMER_NAME}, Thank you for order... 6. Include variables: {ORDER_ID}, {AMOUNT}, {DELIVERY_DATE} 7. Add link: Click here to view order status 8. Create template: GRN_RECEIVED 9. Subject: Materials Received for Job {JOB_NUMBER} 10. Body: Goods receipt completed. Received {QUANTITY} units 11. Create template: JOB_COMPLETION 12. Subject: Job {JOB_NUMBER} Completed 13. Body: Your job completed successfully on {DATE} 14. Create template: INVOICE_SENT 15. Subject: Invoice {INVOICE_ID} for Job {JOB_NUMBER} 16. Body: Please find attached invoice. Amount: {AMOUNT} 17. Automation rules trigger emails using these templates 18. Professional, consistent communication via email

▶ 🏢 Department - Organizational Departments

What It Is: Master record for organizational departments (Production, Sales, Finance, Warehouse, HR). Groups employees by function. Used for organizational hierarchy, reporting structure, and access control.

Why Used in ITE: Organization divided into departments with different responsibilities. Production builds jobs. Sales creates orders. Finance approves spending. Warehouse manages inventory. System must know which department user belongs to for: access control (production worker sees only production jobs), approval routing (requisition routed to department head), cost tracking (identify department spending), organizational reporting.

Key Information Stored: Department code (PROD, SALES, FIN, WH, HR), department name, description of responsibilities, department manager (user ID), parent department (reporting structure), cost center (for accounting allocation), budget allocated (annual budget), approval authority (can approve up to amount).

Project Understanding: Requisition created by Production department. Amount: ₹500,000. System routes for approval: Production Manager (local approval, limit ₹100K) → Department Head (limit ₹500K) → Finance Manager (limit ₹1M) → Procurement. Each step knows department and approval authority. Finance tracks: Production spent ₹500K, Sales spent ₹200K this month. Organization sees department-wise spending. Year-end: Production department used 80% of ₹800K budget. Report sent to department manager showing spending vs. budget.

Business Workflow: 1. Admin creates department: Production 2. Code: PROD 3. Description: Manufacturing and job execution 4. Assign manager: Rajesh Kumar (user ID) 5. Set approval authority: Can approve up to ₹100,000 6. Set budget: ₹800,000 annual 7. Create department: Finance 8. Code: FIN 9. Description: Financial planning and approval 10. Assign manager: Sunita Sharma 11. Set approval authority: Can approve up to ₹1,000,000 12. Create department: Sales 13. Create department: Warehouse 14. Users assigned to departments during user creation 15. Requisitions routed by department for approval 16. Cost tracking and reporting by department 17. Organizational hierarchy and accountability

▶ 👔 Designation - Job Titles & Positions

What It Is: Master record for job titles/positions within organization (Manager, Supervisor, Technician, Operator). Defines role hierarchy and authority levels within each department.

Why Used in ITE: Different positions have different authority and responsibilities. Manager can approve up to ₹500K. Supervisor can approve up to ₹100K. Technician cannot approve. System must know designation to enforce approval limits and route workflows correctly. Also used for organizational hierarchy and salary/compensation grading.

Key Information Stored: Designation code (MGR, SUP, TECH), designation name, description of role, department (which department, optional), approval authority (can approve up to amount), can manage users flag, salary grade, reporting structure (who supervises this role).

Project Understanding: Requisition for ₹300,000. Submitted by Technician (Ajay). System checks: Technician designation cannot approve. Routes to Supervisor (Priya). Supervisor can approve up to ₹100K but this is ₹300K, so routes to Manager (Rajesh). Manager can approve up to ₹500K, so Rajesh can approve. Without designation master, system wouldn't know approval limits and might block legitimate approvals or allow unauthorized ones.

Business Workflow: 1. Admin creates designation: Manager 2. Code: MGR 3. Description: Department-level leadership 4. Can approve up to: ₹500,000 5. Can manage users: Yes 6. Salary grade: Grade 5 7. Create designation: Supervisor 8. Code: SUP 9. Can approve up to: ₹100,000 10. Can manage users: No (cannot manage) 11. Salary grade: Grade 3 12. Create designation: Technician 13. Code: TECH 14. Can approve up to: ₹0 (cannot approve) 15. Can manage users: No 16. Salary grade: Grade 1 17. Users assigned designations during user creation 18. System enforces approval limits based on designation 19. Organizational hierarchy and authority levels

▶ 📂 Job Belongs To - Job Type Categories

What It Is: Master record for job type categories (Custom Manufacturing, Standard Production, Repair, Assembly). Classifies jobs by type to apply different workflows and business rules.

Why Used in ITE: Different job types follow different processes. Custom job needs detailed specifications and multiple approvals. Standard job has predefined workflow. Repair job tracks defect analysis. Assembly-only job doesn't need raw materials. System must know job type to apply correct workflow, skip unnecessary steps, and calculate accurate timelines.

Key Information Stored: Job type code (CUSTOM, STANDARD, REPAIR, ASSEMBLY), job type name, description of job type, default lead time (days typical), costing method (material, labor, overhead), required approvals (how many levels), workflow route (which team handles), required documentation (quality plan, design, drawings).

Project Understanding: Sales creates job: Type=CUSTOM. System knows: Requires 2-level approval, needs quality plan documentation, typical lead time 30 days, labor-intensive costing. Routes to Production Manager and Quality Lead. Another job: Type=ASSEMBLY. System knows: Requires 1-level approval, no quality plan (standard), lead time 7 days, material-intensive. Routes only to Warehouse Manager. Different workflows, different lead times, different approvals.

Business Workflow: 1. Admin creates job type: Custom Manufacturing 2. Code: CUSTOM 3. Description: Customized products built per specifications 4. Default lead time: 30 days 5. Requires approvals: 2 levels (Manager + Quality Lead) 6. Costing: Labor-intensive (40% material, 60% labor) 7. Create job type: Standard Production 8. Code: STANDARD 9. Default lead time: 14 days 10. Requires approvals: 1 level (Manager only) 11. Costing: Mixed (50% material, 50% labor) 12. Create job type: Repair 13. Code: REPAIR 14. Default lead time: 5 days 15. Requires approvals: Warranty team 16. Create job type: Assembly 17. Code: ASSEMBLY 18. Default lead time: 7 days 19. Costing: Minimal labor (90% material, 10% labor) 20. When creating job: Select job type 21. System applies correct workflow and rules

▶ ⏸️ Hold Type - Job Hold Reasons

What It Is: Master record for reasons why jobs or orders are placed on hold. Documents why manufacturing paused and what needs to be resolved before resuming.

Why Used in ITE: Jobs frequently need to pause (materials not arrived, quality issues found, customer request, payment pending). System must document why job on hold, who authorized the hold, when it started, target resolution date. Critical for: traceability (why was job delayed?), SLA tracking (don't count hold time against deadline), resume decisions (when can production restart?).

Key Information Stored: Hold type code (MAT_SHORT, QA_ISSUE, CUST_REQ, PAYMENT, EQUIP_DOWN), hold type name, description of hold reason, severity (high/medium/low), estimated resolution time (hours to resolve typically), auto-notify flag (send alert when placed on hold), resolution instructions (how to resolve this hold).

Project Understanding: Job in manufacturing. Materials not received from supplier (expected today, but delayed). Production manager places hold: Type=MATERIAL_SHORTAGE, Reason="Steel pipes not received from Steel Corp, expected July 31". System sends alert to procurement: resolve hold. Procurement tracks supplier, notifies manager July 31 when received. Manager removes hold (Type=MATERIAL_SHORTAGE). Job resumes. While on hold, SLA clock stops (deadline not affected). After job completion, report shows: 2 days on hold (materials), 1 day on hold (QA rework). Explains why 5-day job took 8 calendar days.

Business Workflow: 1. Admin creates hold type: Material Shortage 2. Code: MAT_SHORT 3. Description: Required materials not received 4. Severity: High 5. Estimated resolution: 2-3 days 6. Auto-notify: Yes (alert procurement) 7. Create hold type: Quality Issue 8. Code: QA_ISSUE 9. Description: Quality inspection failed 10. Severity: High 11. Estimated resolution: 1-2 days 12. Create hold type: Customer Request 13. Code: CUST_REQ 14. Description: Customer requested hold 15. Severity: Medium 16. Create hold type: Payment Pending 17. Code: PAYMENT 18. Description: Customer payment not received 19. Severity: High 20. Create hold type: Equipment Down 21. Code: EQUIP_DOWN 22. Description: Required equipment/machine unavailable 23. Severity: High 24. Estimated resolution: 1 day 25. When job needs pause: Place hold with reason 26. SLA tracking excludes hold time 27. Complete traceability of job delays

⚙️ Configurators Module

System-Wide Configuration & Automation Setup

Module Purpose: System-wide configuration and automation setup. This module allows administrators to customize workflows, define automation rules, setup notifications, and configure system behavior without coding.

Business Value:

  • ✅ Customize workflows by job type
  • ✅ Automate repetitive business processes
  • ✅ Ensure consistent notifications
  • ✅ No-code business process configuration
  • ✅ Real-time automation monitoring

⚙️ Configuration Types - Detailed Explanations

▶ 📋 Job Type Configuration - Workflow Customization

What It Is: Configuration that defines job type-specific workflows, required fields, approval levels, and business rules. Each job type (Custom, Standard, Repair) can have unique workflow steps and requirements.

Why Used in ITE: Different job types follow different processes. Custom manufacturing jobs need detailed specifications, design approval, and quality planning. Standard jobs follow predefined quick workflow. Repair jobs need warranty tracking. System must enforce these differences. Without job type configuration, all jobs treated identically, losing business-specific control. Configuration enables workflow flexibility without changing code.

Key Information Stored: Job type name (Custom Manufacturing, Standard Production), workflow steps (Draft → Approved → InProduction → InQC → Completed), required approvals for each step (Manager approval, Quality Lead review), required documentation (Design drawings, Quality plan, Test results), field requirements (Which fields mandatory for this job type?), budget category rules (labor/material split), timeline defaults (typical days to complete).

Project Understanding: Admin configures CUSTOM job type: Requires Manager approval (0-2 days), Quality Lead approval (2-5 days), then can start production. Each step has mandatory fields (Design document, Specifications, Quality plan). System enforces this workflow. Sales creates custom job → System requires design doc before Manager can approve. Admin later adds Finance approval requirement → All future custom jobs now require Finance sign-off. This changes behavior system-wide without code deployment.

Business Workflow: 1. Admin navigates to Job Type Configuration 2. Select job type: CUSTOM (Custom Manufacturing) 3. Define workflow steps: DRAFT → APPROVED → INPRODUCTION → INQUALITY → COMPLETED 4. For APPROVED step: Require Manager approval 5. Set approval deadline: 2 days 6. Mark fields as required: Description, Design drawings, Specifications 7. For INQUALITY step: Require Quality Lead sign-off 8. Define mandatory quality checklist items 9. Set completion timeline: 30 days typical 10. Configure notifications at each step 11. Save configuration → Applies to all new custom jobs 12. Admin can modify workflow anytime (affects pending jobs too) 13. System logs all configuration changes for audit trail

▶ 🤖 Automation Rules - Business Process Automation

What It Is: Event-driven rules that automatically trigger actions when specific business conditions occur. Eliminates manual processes and ensures consistent execution of business rules.

Why Used in ITE: Manufacturing has repetitive manual tasks: when requisition submitted → group by supplier and create POs (manual work). When job completed → create warranty record (manual). When budget 80% spent → alert finance (manual). Automation eliminates manual intervention, prevents errors, ensures immediate action, reduces processing time from days to seconds.

Key Information Stored: Rule name (e.g., "Auto-Create PO from Requisition"), trigger event (requisition.status = SUBMITTED), trigger condition (additional filters: if amount > 100K, etc.), action to perform (CREATE purchase_order, SEND email, UPDATE budget), action parameters (email recipients, PO prefix), rule enabled flag (active/inactive), execution log (track rule runs, success/failures), scheduled execution (immediate or batch).

Project Understanding: Rule: "ON requisition.status=SUBMITTED, AUTO-GROUP items by preferred supplier and CREATE draft POs". Requisition submitted with 50 items. System fires rule immediately. Groups: Supplier A (items 1-15), Supplier B (items 16-30), Supplier C (items 31-50). Creates 3 draft POs automatically. Without rule, procurement manager manually groups and creates POs (2-4 hours work). With rule, done in seconds. Finance gets second rule: "ON jobBudgetActual.spent > (job.budget × 0.80), CREATE alert". Spending hits 80% threshold → Finance notified automatically. Manager can adjust without waiting for scheduler.

Business Workflow: 1. Admin navigates to Automation Rules configuration 2. Create new rule: Name="Auto-Create PO from Requisition" 3. Set trigger: Event="Requisition Status Change", Status="SUBMITTED" 4. Set condition: Amount > ₹100,000 (optional filter) 5. Define action: CREATE purchase order items 6. Set action detail: Group by preferred supplier 7. Enable rule: Active=Yes 8. Set execution: Immediate (no delay) 9. Create second rule: "Budget Alert" 10. Trigger: job.budget_spent > 80% of allocation 11. Action: SEND EMAIL to finance team 12. Email template: "Budget Alert for Job {JOB_NUMBER}" 13. Create third rule: "Warranty Creation" 14. Trigger: job.status = COMPLETED 15. Action: CREATE warranty record for 12 months 16. System automatically executes all active rules 17. Monitor rule execution logs for success/failures 18. Disable rules if causing issues, review before re-enabling

▶ 📧 Notification Groups - Distribution List Management

What It Is: Master configuration for email distribution lists. Groups employees by role/function to receive business notifications about events (orders, approvals, issues).

Why Used in ITE: When purchase order confirmed, multiple people need notification: Procurement manager, Warehouse manager, Finance. When requisition submitted, Approvers need notification. Manually adding email addresses to each notification is error-prone and scattered. Notification groups centralize email lists. Change warehouse manager email once, all notifications automatically go to new person.

Key Information Stored: Group name (Procurement Team, Finance Approvers, Warehouse Team), description of group purpose, list of email addresses (or user IDs who auto-populate email), group type (role-based or functional), group active/inactive flag, notification preferences (email only, SMS, in-app), do-not-disturb settings (quiet hours), escalation rules (if manager unavailable, send to their manager).

Project Understanding: Group: "PROCUREMENT_TEAM" contains 3 people: (Raj, Priya, Sunita). Automation rule triggers: "ON requisition.status=SUBMITTED, SEND email to PROCUREMENT_TEAM". Requisition submitted → Email sent to Raj, Priya, Sunita simultaneously (within seconds). If Sunita leaves company and replaced by Vikram, Admin updates group: Remove Sunita, Add Vikram. All future emails automatically go to Vikram. Without groups, would need to update 50+ individual notifications/rules. With groups, update once.

Business Workflow: 1. Admin navigates to Notification Groups configuration 2. Create group: "PROCUREMENT_TEAM" 3. Description: "Team responsible for PO creation and approval" 4. Add members: Raj Kumar, Priya Sharma, Sunita Singh 5. Create group: "FINANCE_APPROVERS" 6. Add members: Vikram Iyer, Sunita Desai (Finance Lead) 7. Create group: "WAREHOUSE_TEAM" 8. Add members: Ajay Patel (Warehouse Manager), Lakshmi Reddy 9. Create group: "QUALITY_TEAM" 10. Add members: Arjun Verma (QA Lead), Neha Malhotra 11. Set notification preference: Email + In-App 12. Set do-not-disturb: 6 PM - 8 AM 13. Automation rules reference these groups 14. When PO confirmed: Notification to WAREHOUSE_TEAM 15. When QC issue: Notification to QUALITY_TEAM 16. When approval needed: Notification to FINANCE_APPROVERS 17. Admin can add/remove members anytime (effective immediately)

▶ 📊 Report Configuration - Custom Report Templates

What It Is: Configuration for building custom reports without coding. Users can select data sources, columns, filters, and sorting to create custom dashboards and reports.

Why Used in ITE: Finance needs report: "Top 10 suppliers by spending this month". Procurement needs: "Overdue materials not yet received". Operations needs: "Jobs completing this week". Each report different, specialized needs. Without report configuration, developers write custom SQL for each report (weeks of work). With configuration, users build reports in minutes.

Key Information Stored: Report name (Monthly Supplier Spending), report type (List/Dashboard/Chart), data source (Purchase Orders, Requisitions, Jobs), columns to display (Supplier name, Amount, Date), filters (date range, supplier region, PO status), sorting (by amount descending), refresh interval (real-time, hourly, daily), who can access (departments/roles), export format (PDF, Excel, CSV).

Project Understanding: Finance admin creates report: "Supplier Payment Report". Data source: Purchase Orders. Columns: Supplier, Total PO Amount, Total Paid, Balance, Payment Due Date. Filter: Date range (last 90 days), Status=Confirmed. Sort by: Balance (highest first). Refresh: Daily at 8 AM. Access: Finance Department only. Automatically generates daily, shows: Steel Corp (₹500K balance due), Pipes Inc (₹200K balance due). Finance can drill-down, see individual POs, payment history. Without config, Finance manager manually queries database monthly (4 hours work). With config, automated daily report emailed automatically.

Business Workflow: 1. Admin navigates to Report Configuration 2. Create report: Name="Monthly Supplier Analysis" 3. Select data source: Purchase Orders 4. Add columns: Supplier, Amount, Delivery Date, Received Date, Status 5. Add filter: Date Range (Last 30 Days) 6. Add filter: Status = Confirmed 7. Add sorting: Amount (Highest First) 8. Set schedule: Run daily at 8 AM 9. Set recipients: Finance Manager, CFO 10. Set format: Email as PDF + Link to dashboard 11. Create second report: "Overdue Materials" 12. Data source: Purchase Order Items 13. Filter: Expected Delivery Date < Today AND Received=0 14. Add columns: PO Number, Item, Expected Delivery, Days Late, Supplier 15. Sort by: Days Late (highest first) 16. Run on demand and email to Procurement 17. Create dashboard: Job Completion Status 18. Charts: % Complete by Job Type, Avg Days to Complete, On-Time Delivery % 19. Refresh: Real-time (updates as data changes) 20. Access: Operations department dashboard

▶ 🔧 System Settings - Global Configuration

What It Is: Global system configuration for organization defaults, business rules, and system behavior. Controls how system operates across all modules.

Why Used in ITE: System needs organization-wide defaults: Budget approval limits by designation, Default job completion timeline, Financial year start date, Document numbering format (PO-2026-00001), Tax percentage to apply, Currency for reporting. These settings referenced everywhere. Centralized configuration ensures consistency and enables easy changes without code deployment.

Key Information Stored: Company name and registration, fiscal year start/end dates, default currency (INR, USD), tax settings (GST %, tax number), document numbering format (prefix, sequence), approval authority matrix (designation/amount), default lead times (manufacturing, delivery), accounting periods (months, quarters), system behavior (auto-lock old records, retention policies), integration settings (API keys for external systems).

Project Understanding: System setting: "Default Requisition Lead Time = 7 days". When requisition created, system defaults to 7-day delivery. If supplier has 5-day lead time, 2 days buffer added. If supplier needs 10 days, system marks as risk (exceeds default). Year-end fiscal closing: System configured "Fiscal Year = Apr-Mar". April 1 start signals new financial year. April 15, system auto-locks all previous year's records (read-only), prevents accidental changes. Billing: Tax rate setting = 18% GST. Invoices automatically calculate 18% tax on all amounts. If tax rate changes to 20%, change setting once, all future invoices use 20%. Past invoices preserve original 18%.

Business Workflow: 1. Admin navigates to System Settings 2. Set company name: "ACME Manufacturing Ltd" 3. Set GST number: "27AABCT1234H1Z0" 4. Set default currency: INR (Indian Rupees) 5. Set tax rate: 18% GST 6. Set fiscal year: April 1 - March 31 7. Set document numbering: - PO Format: "PO-{YYYY}-{SEQUENCE}" (e.g., PO-2026-00001) - Requisition Format: "REQ-{YYYY}-{SEQUENCE}" - Invoice Format: "INV-{YYYY}-{SEQUENCE}" 8. Set approval authorities: - Manager: Can approve up to ₹500,000 - Finance Head: Can approve up to ₹2,000,000 - CFO: Unlimited approval 9. Set default timelines: - Standard job completion: 14 days - Custom job completion: 30 days - Repair completion: 5 days 10. Set business rules: - Auto-lock records after 6 months - Archive old audit records after 2 years - Calculate bonus on cost savings > 10% 11. Integration settings: - Bank gateway API key for payment - Email service credentials - External accounting system API 12. System applies settings system-wide 13. Admin can change settings anytime (effective immediately)

▶ 🔗 Integration Configuration - External System Connections

What It Is: Configuration for connecting ITE to external systems (banking, accounting, CRM, EDI). Enables data exchange between systems without manual data entry.

Why Used in ITE: Organization uses external systems: Accounting software (Tally, SAP), Banking system (payment processing), Customer CRM (customer records), Shipping software (tracking). Manual data entry between systems: duplicate data, errors, delays. Integration configuration automates data sync: when job completed → automatically send invoice to accounting, payment due date → auto-initiate bank transfer, order completed → send shipment data to tracking system.

Key Information Stored: Integration name (Accounting Software, Bank Gateway, CRM Sync), external system type (API, FTP, EDI), connection URL/credentials, sync direction (one-way or two-way), data entities to sync (Customers, Invoices, Payments), sync frequency (real-time, hourly, daily), error handling (retry, alert, skip), field mapping (ITE field → External system field).

Project Understanding: Integration: "Accounting Software Sync". Connects to Tally accounting. When job completed and invoice issued in ITE: System automatically sends invoice details to Tally (amount, GL codes, customer). Tally receives data, creates accounting entry automatically. Finance doesn't manually enter invoices into Tally (saves 2 hours per day). Second integration: "Bank Payment Processing". ITE configured to send payment requests to bank API at 5 PM daily. Finance approves payments in ITE, system batches them, sends to bank API, payments processed. Without integration, Finance prints checks, manual bank upload (3 days delay). With integration, payments processed same day.

Business Workflow: 1. Admin navigates to Integration Configuration 2. Create integration: "Accounting Software Sync" 3. External system type: REST API 4. Connection URL: https://accounting.company.com/api/ 5. Authentication: API Key (stored encrypted) 6. Sync direction: One-way (ITE → Accounting) 7. Data entities: Invoices, Customers, Payment 8. Sync frequency: Real-time (immediate) 9. Field mapping: - ITE.invoice_number → Accounting.voucher_number - ITE.job_description → Accounting.particulars - ITE.total_amount → Accounting.amount - ITE.customer_id → Accounting.customer_id 10. Error handling: Retry 3 times, then alert admin 11. Create second integration: "Bank Payment Gateway" 12. External system: HTTPS API (secure) 13. Connection: bank.company.com/payments 14. Authentication: Digital certificate + API key 15. Sync direction: Two-way 16. Data: Payment requests sent, payment confirmation received 17. Sync frequency: On-demand + daily batch (5 PM) 18. Create integration: "Customer CRM Sync" 19. Sync: Customer records from CRM updated in ITE 20. Frequency: Hourly (keep customer data fresh) 21. Admin can test connection before enabling 22. System monitors integration health (success rate, delays) 23. Audit trail tracks all synced data for compliance

📋 Requisitions Module

Material Request Processing with Multi-Level Approval & PO Generation

Module Purpose: When job is approved and transitions to OPEN status, system automatically creates material requisition by exploding Bill of Materials. Routes through multi-level approval chain. After approval, auto-generates purchase orders grouped by preferred supplier.

Business Value:

  • ✅ Automatic BOM explosion eliminates manual calculation
  • ✅ Multi-level approval ensures authorization control
  • ✅ Auto-PO generation eliminates procurement delay
  • ✅ Budget tracking prevents overspending
  • ✅ Supplier grouping optimizes logistics and costs

📋 Requisition Features - Detailed Explanations

▶ ➕ Add Requisitions - Material Request Creation

What It Is: Process of creating new material requisition from approved job. System auto-calculates required materials based on Bill of Materials for job components.

Why Used in ITE: When manufacturing job approved, production needs materials. Manually calculating each material needed is time-consuming and error-prone. Requisition auto-created from BOM ensures: all materials identified, no forgotten items, standardized process, speeds up procurement.

Key Information Stored: Requisition number (auto-generated), Job reference, Job total budget allocated, Requisition status (DRAFT), Items list with quantity (auto-calculated from BOM), Unit of measurement, Preferred supplier recommendation, Estimated cost for each item, Total requisition amount, Created date and user.

Project Understanding: Job-001 approved for manufacturing Motor Assembly. BOM defines: Motor (1 unit), Bearing (4 units), Shaft (1 unit), Oil Seal (4 units), Fasteners (20 pieces). Auto-created requisition lists all 5 items with quantities. System calculates: Motor ₹5000, Bearing ₹500 each (4 = ₹2000), Shaft ₹1000, Oil Seal ₹100 each (4 = ₹400), Fasteners ₹200 total = ₹8600 total requisition. Requisition routed for approval. Without auto-creation, procurement manager manually enters each item (1 hour work, error risk).

Business Workflow: 1. Sales creates job with job type = CUSTOM_MANUFACTURING 2. Job includes BOM: Motor (1), Bearing (4), Shaft (1), Oil Seal (4), Fasteners (20) 3. Job status changes to APPROVED and then OPEN 4. System automatically triggers: Create Requisition 5. Requisition populated with BOM items and quantities 6. System looks up preferred supplier for each item 7. Requisition number generated: REQ-2026-00042 8. Status set to DRAFT (editable if needed) 9. Requisition routed to Department Manager for review 10. Manager verifies quantities, can modify if needed 11. Manager submits for approval (status → SUBMITTED) 12. System calculates total cost and checks against job budget 13. Requisition ready for approval chain

▶ ✏️ Modify/Process PR - Requisition Editing

What It Is: Ability to modify requisition items, quantities, and supplier preferences before approval or during approval cycle.

Why Used in ITE: BOM calculated quantities might need adjustment based on actual manufacturing conditions. Supplier might be unavailable for specific item, need to change. Quantities might exceed budget, need to prioritize. System must allow controlled modifications with audit trail tracking who changed what and why.

Key Information Stored: Original quantity vs. modified quantity (with change reason), original preferred supplier vs. new supplier selection, cost impact of modifications, approval status of modifications, change log showing: who changed, when, what changed, reason for change.

Project Understanding: Requisition REQ-2026-00042 created with 4 bearings. Manufacturing engineer reviews, determines: bearing availability low, can substitute with alternative bearing (same spec, ₹600 instead of ₹500). Modifies requisition: Quantity stays 4, but supplier changed from Supplier-A to Supplier-B, new cost ₹600 each (₹2400 vs ₹2000, difference ₹400). System tracks change: "Changed by Rajesh Kumar on July 30, 2026, 3:15 PM. Reason: Better availability and same specifications." Change requires re-approval if amount exceeds limit.

Business Workflow: 1. Requisition REQ-2026-00042 in DRAFT status 2. Manager opens requisition to review 3. Checks each item's quantity and supplier 4. Reviews: Bearing (4 units) from Steel Corp 5. Realizes: Steel Corp lead time 7 days (exceeds 5-day requirement) 6. Changes Bearing supplier to Pipes Inc (5-day lead time) 7. Updates cost: ₹500 → ₹520 per unit 8. Updates reason: "Faster delivery to meet timeline" 9. System recalculates total: ₹8600 → ₹8620 10. Updates quantity of Fasteners from 20 to 25 (actual need) 11. Updates Fastener cost: ₹200 → ₹250 12. New total: ₹8870 (within ₹10K budget) 13. System logs all changes with timestamps 14. Saves requisition (still in DRAFT) 15. Submits for approval with modified content

▶ 👁️ View PR - Requisition Status & Details

What It Is: Read-only view showing full requisition details, current status, approval history, and fulfillment tracking (how many items received vs. ordered).

Why Used in ITE: Multiple users need to track requisition progress: Manager checking approval status, Procurement tracking what ordered, Finance checking costs, Warehouse monitoring receipts. View provides complete visibility without allowing accidental modifications.

Key Information Stored: Requisition number, Job reference, Status timeline (when SUBMITTED, APPROVED, PO_CREATED), Approval history (who approved, when, comments), All items with quantities and pricing, Fulfillment status (Ordered 100 items, Received 75, Pending 25), Linked purchase orders (PO-001, PO-002), Budget vs. actual spending.

Project Understanding: Warehouse manager views REQ-2026-00042. Sees: 4 bearings ordered (linked to PO-001), 3 received so far, 1 pending delivery July 31. Shaft: 1 ordered (PO-001), 0 received, delivery expected August 2. Fasteners: 25 ordered, all 25 received from Supplier-C. Can see approval chain: Manager approved July 30, Finance approved July 30, Procurement created PO-001 & PO-002 on July 30. Total cost: ₹8870, Budget: ₹10000, Remaining: ₹1130.

Business Workflow: 1. User navigates to View Requisition 2. Searches/selects: REQ-2026-00042 3. Views header: Job-001, Status=PO_CREATED, Total=₹8870 4. Views approval history: - SUBMITTED by Manager (Rajesh) on July 30, 2:30 PM - APPROVED by Finance Head on July 30, 2:50 PM (Comment: "Within budget") - POs CREATED by Procurement on July 30, 3:00 PM 5. Views items section: - Motor (1): ₹5000 from Supplier-A, PO-001, Received 1/1 - Bearing (4): ₹520 each from Supplier-B, PO-001, Received 3/4 - Shaft (1): ₹1000 from Supplier-A, PO-001, Received 0/1 - Oil Seal (4): ₹100 each from Supplier-C, PO-002, Received 4/4 - Fasteners (25): ₹10 each from Supplier-D, PO-002, Received 25/25 6. Views PO links: Click to see PO-001, PO-002 details 7. Views budget tracking: Used ₹8870, Budget ₹10000, Remaining ₹1130 8. Views change history: All modifications tracked with reasons

▶ 🔍 PO Check - Purchase Order Validation

What It Is: Verification that purchase orders were correctly created from approved requisition. Checks if all requisition items have corresponding POs with correct quantities and pricing.

Why Used in ITE: After requisition approved, system auto-creates POs. Need to verify: all items got POs, quantities match, pricing matches, no duplicate POs. Missing or incorrect POs would delay manufacturing. PO Check ensures integrity before manufacturing starts.

Key Information Stored: Requisition reference, PO numbers generated, Item-to-PO mapping (which item in which PO), Quantity match (requisition qty = PO qty), Price match (requisition unit price = PO unit price), Supplier match (preferred supplier matches PO supplier), Status (All matched, Mismatches found).

Project Understanding: REQ-2026-00042 approved, auto-created PO-001 and PO-002. PO Check verifies: Requisition item Motor (1 unit, ₹5000) → PO-001 has Motor (1 unit, ₹5000) ✓. Bearing (4 units, ₹520 each) → PO-001 has Bearing (4 units, ₹520 each) ✓. Shaft (1 unit, ₹1000) → PO-001 has Shaft (1 unit, ₹1000) ✓. Oil Seal (4 units, ₹100 each) → PO-002 has Oil Seal (4 units, ₹100 each) ✓. Fasteners (25 pieces, ₹10 each) → PO-002 has Fasteners (25 pieces, ₹10 each) ✓. All items matched correctly, no issues.

Business Workflow: 1. Procurement staff navigates to PO Check 2. Selects Requisition: REQ-2026-00042 3. System shows: "Checking 5 items for PO coverage" 4. Checks Motor: - Requisition: 1 unit, ₹5000 from Supplier-A - Found in: PO-001, 1 unit, ₹5000 from Supplier-A ✓ Match 5. Checks Bearing: - Requisition: 4 units, ₹520 each from Supplier-B - Found in: PO-001, 4 units, ₹520 each from Supplier-B ✓ Match 6. Checks Shaft: - Requisition: 1 unit, ₹1000 from Supplier-A - Found in: PO-001, 1 unit, ₹1000 from Supplier-A ✓ Match 7. Checks Oil Seal: - Requisition: 4 units, ₹100 each from Supplier-C - Found in: PO-002, 4 units, ₹100 each from Supplier-C ✓ Match 8. Checks Fasteners: - Requisition: 25 pieces, ₹10 each from Supplier-D - Found in: PO-002, 25 pieces, ₹10 each from Supplier-D ✓ Match 9. Summary: 5/5 items verified, No mismatches, Status: PASSED 10. Procurement can proceed with PO processing confident all covered

▶ 📊 PR By Items - Item-Level Requisition Analysis

What It Is: Report/view showing all requisitions grouped by item. Shows which jobs need which items, aggregated quantities, total costs, and fulfillment status for each item.

Why Used in ITE: Helps with demand planning and bulk ordering. Example: 3 different jobs need Motor, total quantity 6 units needed. Bulk purchasing 6 units together cheaper than individual orders. Item-level view helps identify consolidation opportunities and supplier negotiations.

Key Information Stored: Item name, Total quantity needed across all requisitions, Jobs requiring this item (list), Total cost for this item, Suppliers supplying this item, Fulfillment status (total ordered, total received, total pending), Consolidation opportunities (can combine requisitions).

Project Understanding: Report shows: Motor needed by Job-001 (1 unit, ₹5000), Job-002 (1 unit, ₹5000), Job-003 (2 units, ₹10000). Total: 4 Motors needed, ₹20000 total. Currently in 3 separate requisitions/POs. Could consolidate to 1 PO of 4 Motors with Supplier-A, negotiate bulk discount (₹4900 per unit instead of ₹5000 = saves ₹400). Item report identifies these opportunities automatically.

Business Workflow: 1. Procurement manager navigates to PR By Items 2. Views aggregated item analysis 3. Motor: Appears in 3 active requisitions - REQ-2026-00042: Job-001, 1 unit, ₹5000 - REQ-2026-00043: Job-002, 1 unit, ₹5000 - REQ-2026-00044: Job-003, 2 units, ₹10000 - Total: 4 units needed, ₹20000 - Supplier: All from Supplier-A - Consolidation: Can order 4 units together, negotiate bulk rate 4. Bearing: Appears in 4 requisitions - Total: 16 units needed, ₹8320 - Suppliers: Supplier-B (12 units), Supplier-C (4 units) - Issue: Split suppliers for same item - Recommendation: Consolidate with primary supplier 5. Can filter by: Item type, Date range, Supplier, Status 6. Can export report for supplier negotiations 7. Helps identify volume discount opportunities 8. Supports demand forecasting for planning

🛒 Purchasing Module

Purchase Order Management & Supplier Tracking

Module Purpose: After requisition approved, system auto-generates Purchase Orders to suppliers. Tracks PO status from DRAFT to CONFIRMED to RECEIVED to CLOSED. Monitors supplier delivery performance, tracks pricing, and manages PO-to-receiving reconciliation.

Business Value:

  • ✅ Auto-generates POs from requisition (no manual creation)
  • ✅ Groups requisition items by supplier (optimizes logistics)
  • ✅ Tracks supplier performance (on-time %, quality)
  • ✅ Reconciles goods received vs. ordered
  • ✅ Monitors delivery delays and exceptions

🛒 Purchase Order Features - Detailed Explanations

▶ 📄 Generate PO - Purchase Order Creation

What It Is: Automatic process of creating purchase orders from approved requisition. System groups requisition items by preferred supplier and generates draft POs ready for confirmation.

Why Used in ITE: Manual PO creation from requisition: procurement manager reads requisition, groups items by supplier, fills in supplier details, calculates totals, numbers the PO (2-3 hours work, error-prone). Auto-generation: all done instantly, correctly, with supplier details auto-populated from master data.

Key Information Stored: PO number (auto-generated: PO-2026-00123), Supplier name and details, Items and quantities (from requisition), Unit pricing (from supplier master), Total amount, Expected delivery date (based on supplier lead time), PO creation date, Created by user ID, Status (DRAFT), PO reference to requisition (REQ-2026-00042).

Project Understanding: Requisition REQ-2026-00042 approved with 5 items. Auto-generation groups: Motor + Bearing + Shaft → Supplier-A (3 items), Oil Seal → Supplier-C (1 item), Fasteners → Supplier-D (1 item). Creates 3 POs: PO-001 (Supplier-A, 3 items, ₹7520), PO-002 (Supplier-C, 1 item, ₹400), PO-003 (Supplier-D, 1 item, ₹250). Each PO has supplier details auto-filled, delivery dates calculated (Supplier-A: 5-day lead time → July 35 expected delivery).

Business Workflow: 1. Requisition REQ-2026-00042 reaches APPROVED status 2. System triggers: Generate Purchase Orders 3. Analyzes requisition items: - Motor (1 unit): Preferred supplier = Supplier-A - Bearing (4 units): Preferred supplier = Supplier-B - Shaft (1 unit): Preferred supplier = Supplier-A - Oil Seal (4 units): Preferred supplier = Supplier-C - Fasteners (25 pieces): Preferred supplier = Supplier-D 4. Groups by supplier: - Supplier-A: Motor (1), Shaft (1) - Supplier-B: Bearing (4) - Supplier-C: Oil Seal (4) - Supplier-D: Fasteners (25) 5. Creates draft POs: - PO-2026-001: Supplier-A, 2 items, ₹6000 - PO-2026-002: Supplier-B, 1 item, ₹2080 - PO-2026-003: Supplier-C, 1 item, ₹400 - PO-2026-004: Supplier-D, 1 item, ₹250 6. Auto-populates supplier details: Address, phone, email, tax ID 7. Calculates delivery dates: - PO-2026-001: Expected July 35 (5-day lead time) - PO-2026-002: Expected July 37 (7-day lead time) - PO-2026-003: Expected July 36 (6-day lead time) - PO-2026-004: Expected July 35 (5-day lead time) 8. Sets status: DRAFT (ready for review and confirmation) 9. Sends to Procurement for review before sending to suppliers

▶ ⚙️ Process/Modify PO - PO Editing & Confirmation

What It Is: Ability to review, modify, and confirm draft POs before sending to suppliers. Can change quantities, delivery dates, or cancel POs if needed.

Why Used in ITE: Auto-generated POs might need adjustments: supplier unavailable, quantity insufficient, delivery date unrealistic. System allows controlled modifications with full audit trail before PO sent to supplier (can't change after sent).

Key Information Stored: Original PO details vs. modified details, Modification reason, Approval for modifications (if amount changes significantly), PO confirmation date and user, Notification sent to supplier flag.

Project Understanding: PO-2026-002 (Bearing from Supplier-B) generated with 7-day lead time (delivery July 37). Procurement realizes: Job needs materials by July 35. Calls Supplier-B for expedited delivery. Supplier agrees to 5-day lead time (July 35) but charges ₹50 extra per unit. Modifies PO: Qty stays 4, unit price changes from ₹520 to ₹570 (extra ₹200 cost). Updates reason: "Expedited delivery to meet manufacturing timeline." Recalculates total: ₹2080 → ₹2280. Checks: Total requisition cost now ₹8870 + ₹200 = ₹9070 (still within ₹10K budget). Approves modification and confirms PO (status → CONFIRMED).

Business Workflow: 1. Draft POs created, shown to Procurement Manager 2. Manager opens PO-2026-002 for review 3. Sees: 4 Bearings from Supplier-B, ₹520 each, delivery July 37 4. Realizes: Manufacturing needs materials by July 35 (2 days earlier) 5. Calls Supplier-B to check expedited delivery 6. Supplier agrees: 5-day lead time (July 35) for ₹580 per unit (₹60 premium) 7. Modifies PO in system: - Quantity: 4 (no change) - Unit price: ₹520 → ₹580 - Delivery date: July 37 → July 35 - Modification reason: "Expedited delivery to meet job timeline" 8. System recalculates: 4 × ₹580 = ₹2320 (was ₹2080, difference +₹240) 9. System checks budget impact: Total job requisition now ₹9110 (was ₹8870) 10. Checks: Still within ₹10K budget ✓ 11. Approves modification in system 12. Reviews all other POs: - PO-2026-001: 2 items, ₹6000, delivery July 35 ✓ OK - PO-2026-003: 1 item, ₹400, delivery July 36 ✓ OK - PO-2026-004: 1 item, ₹250, delivery July 35 ✓ OK 13. Confirms all POs (status → CONFIRMED) 14. System sends POs to suppliers via email and system notification 15. POs locked (can't modify after confirmed)

▶ 👁️ View PO - Purchase Order Details & Tracking

What It Is: Read-only view showing complete PO details, delivery tracking, received quantities vs. ordered, and payment status.

Why Used in ITE: Multiple teams need to track POs: Procurement checking status and delivery, Warehouse monitoring receipts, Finance tracking invoices and payments, Management monitoring supplier performance.

Key Information Stored: PO number, Supplier details, All items with quantities and pricing, Total amount, Expected delivery date, Actual delivery date, Received quantity for each item, Invoice status (received, matched with GRN, approved for payment), Payment status (pending, partial, fully paid), Change history (all modifications tracked).

Project Understanding: View PO-2026-001 (Supplier-A). Shows: Order date July 30, Expected delivery July 35. Items: Motor (1, ₹5000), Shaft (1, ₹1000). Total: ₹6000. Received portion: Motor received July 34 ✓, Shaft pending (expected July 35). Invoice status: Not yet received. Payment status: Pending invoice. Manager can see: PO created July 30 by Rajesh Kumar, Confirmed July 30 by Vikram (Procurement), Invoice expected within 30 days of delivery, Payment due 30 days after invoice receipt. All changes logged (if any).

Business Workflow: 1. User navigates to View Purchase Order 2. Searches: PO-2026-001 3. Views header section: - PO Number: PO-2026-001 - Supplier: Steel & Parts Ltd (Supplier-A) - Status: CONFIRMED - Order Date: July 30, 2026 - Ordered By: Rajesh Kumar (Manager) - Confirmed By: Vikram Iyer (Procurement) 4. Views supplier details: - Name: Steel & Parts Ltd - Address: Plot 123, Bangalore - Phone: 9876543210 - Email: sales@steelparts.com - GST: 27AABCS1234H1Z0 5. Views items section: - Motor: 1 unit @ ₹5000 - Shaft: 1 unit @ ₹1000 - Total: ₹6000 6. Views delivery tracking: - Expected Delivery: July 35, 2026 - Motor: Received July 34, 2026 (1/1) ✓ - Shaft: Expected July 35, 2026 (0/1) Pending 7. Views financial tracking: - Invoice: Not received - Payment: Pending invoice - Terms: Net 30 days (due August 30) 8. Views change history: - July 30, 2:50 PM: Created by system from REQ-2026-00042 - July 30, 3:00 PM: Confirmed by Vikram Iyer 9. Can link to related documents: Requisition, GRN, Invoice

▶ 💰 Item Price History - Pricing Tracking & Analysis

What It Is: Historical record of prices paid for each item across different POs and suppliers. Shows price trends, supplier pricing comparison, and helps with cost analysis and future negotiations.

Why Used in ITE: Procurement needs to track if prices going up or down. Example: Motor costing ₹5000 last month, ₹5200 this month. Need to understand trends and negotiate better rates. Price history enables: supplier comparison, trend analysis, budget forecasting, cost reduction initiatives.

Key Information Stored: Item name, Date of purchase (PO date), Supplier name, Unit price paid, Quantity, Total cost for that PO, Cumulative quantity from supplier, Supplier pricing trend (average, highest, lowest), Price comparison across suppliers.

Project Understanding: Item "Motor" price history: July 2026: ₹5000 (Supplier-A, 2 units), ₹5100 (Supplier-B, 1 unit). June 2026: ₹4900 (Supplier-A, 3 units), ₹5000 (Supplier-B, 2 units). May 2026: ₹4800 (Supplier-A, 1 unit). Trend: Supplier-A average ₹4950, Supplier-B average ₹5050. Supplier-A cheaper by ₹100. Procurement can negotiate: "Supplier-A offered ₹4800 in May, why ₹5000 in July? Need to return to ₹4800 rate." Historical data supports negotiation.

Business Workflow: 1. Procurement manager navigates to Item Price History 2. Searches for: Motor 3. Views price history table: | Date | Supplier | PO # | Unit Price | Quantity | Total | Status | |------|----------|------|-----------|----------|-------|--------| | Jul 30, 2026 | Supplier-A | PO-2026-001 | ₹5000 | 1 | ₹5000 | Partial Received | | Jul 29, 2026 | Supplier-B | PO-2026-005 | ₹5100 | 1 | ₹5100 | Pending | | Jun 28, 2026 | Supplier-A | PO-2026-xxx | ₹4900 | 3 | ₹14700 | Received | | Jun 27, 2026 | Supplier-B | PO-2026-yyy | ₹5000 | 2 | ₹10000 | Received | | May 15, 2026 | Supplier-A | PO-2026-zzz | ₹4800 | 1 | ₹4800 | Received | 4. Views pricing analysis: - Average Price: ₹4960 - Highest Price: ₹5100 (Supplier-B, Jul 2026) - Lowest Price: ₹4800 (Supplier-A, May 2026) - Price Trend: Increasing (May ₹4800 → Jul ₹5000-5100) 5. Views supplier comparison: - Supplier-A: Avg ₹4900 (3 purchases), Total ₹24500 - Supplier-B: Avg ₹5050 (2 purchases), Total ₹15100 - Best Price: Supplier-A by ₹150 avg 6. Can export to Excel for detailed analysis 7. Identifies negotiation opportunity: Return Supplier-A to May rate (₹4800) 8. Forecasts cost savings: If all future at ₹4800 vs ₹5000, saves ₹200 per unit

▶ 📊 PO Report - Purchase Order Analysis & Insights

What It Is: Comprehensive report showing all purchase orders grouped by various dimensions: supplier, status, job, date range. Includes metrics like on-time delivery %, average cost per item, payment status.

Why Used in ITE: Management needs visibility on: Total spending with each supplier, How many POs pending delivery, How much outstanding payment, Which suppliers delivering on time vs. late. Reports enable: supplier performance evaluation, budget tracking, cash flow forecasting, operational decisions.

Key Information Stored: PO summary data: Total POs created, Total PO value, Breakdown by supplier (top suppliers, total spending), Breakdown by status (DRAFT, CONFIRMED, RECEIVED, CLOSED), Breakdown by job (which jobs have pending orders), Payment summary (outstanding, paid, partially paid), On-time delivery % (received on time vs. late), Average price trends per item.

Project Understanding: Monthly PO report shows: Total POs created (42), Total value (₹4.2M), Top suppliers: Supplier-A (₹800K, 10% of total), Supplier-C (₹650K, 15% of total), Supplier-D (₹600K, 14% of total). PO status: CONFIRMED (28 POs, ₹1.8M pending delivery), RECEIVED (10 POs, ₹1.5M awaiting invoice), CLOSED (4 POs, ₹900K paid). Payment: Outstanding (₹1.8M), Paid (₹900K), Outstanding days > 30 (₹200K overdue). On-time delivery: Supplier-A (95% on-time), Supplier-C (78% on-time), Supplier-D (82% on-time). Shows: Supplier-A most reliable, Supplier-C needs improvement.

Business Workflow: 1. Finance manager navigates to PO Report 2. Selects report type: Monthly PO Analysis 3. Selects date range: July 2026 4. Generates report showing: - Total POs: 42 - Total Value: ₹4,200,000 - Average PO Value: ₹100,000 5.
