📦 Stores Module

Warehouse & Inventory Management Operations

Module Purpose: Manages complete warehouse operations from receiving goods from suppliers through issuing materials to manufacturing. Tracks inventory levels, handles quality inspections, processes returns, and maintains stock accuracy across multiple warehouse locations.

Business Value:

  • ✅ Accurate inventory tracking prevents stockouts
  • ✅ Quality inspection catches defects before manufacturing use
  • ✅ Location-wise stock management optimizes storage
  • ✅ Material issue automation speeds manufacturing
  • ✅ Stock aging reports identify obsolete inventory

📦 Warehouse Operations - Detailed Explanations

▶ 📥 Receive Order - Goods Receipt Processing

What It Is: Process of receiving goods from supplier against purchase order. Warehouse receives shipment, verifies against PO, inspects quality, creates GRN (Goods Receipt Note), and updates inventory.

Why Used in ITE: Goods received from supplier must be verified before adding to inventory. Need to check: Does shipment match PO? Are quantities correct? Are items in good condition? Without verification, defective goods mixed with good stock, wrong quantities received go unnoticed, inventory counts become inaccurate.

Key Information Stored: GRN number (auto-generated), Supplier name, PO reference, Received date and time, Received by (warehouse staff name), Items received (quantity for each item), Quality status (accepted, rejected, partial accepted), Discrepancies noted (missing items, damaged items, quantity mismatch), Location assigned (which warehouse location to store), Receiving notes and photos.

Project Understanding: PO-2026-001 (Steel & Parts, Motor 1 + Shaft 1, total ₹6000) scheduled delivery July 35. Goods arrive July 34 at warehouse. Warehouse staff: 1. Verifies shipment against PO: Motor (1) ✓, Shaft (1) ✓ 2. Physically counts: Motor (1) ✓, Shaft (1) ✓ 3. Inspects quality: Motor OK ✓, Shaft shows slight rust, requires cleaning 4. Notes in GRN: "Shaft has rust, needs cleaning before use" 5. Accepts both items 6. Creates GRN-2026-001 7. Specifies storage location: MAIN-BNG (Bangalore Main warehouse) 8. System updates inventory: Motor +1 at MAIN-BNG, Shaft +1 at MAIN-BNG.

Business Workflow: 1. Supplier shipment arrives at warehouse 2. Warehouse staff accesses Receive Order module 3. Enters PO number: PO-2026-001 4. System displays: Expected items (Motor 1, Shaft 1), Expected quantity 5. Staff physically counts received items: - Motor: 1 received, 1 expected ✓ - Shaft: 1 received, 1 expected ✓ 6. Staff inspects quality: - Motor: Visual inspection OK ✓ - Shaft: Visual inspection - slight rust detected ⚠ 7. Notes quality issues: "Shaft has rust, needs cleaning" 8. Quality status: Motor (ACCEPTED), Shaft (ACCEPTED WITH NOTE) 9. Selects storage location: MAIN-BNG warehouse 10. Enters receiving notes: "Delivered at 3:30 PM by courier" 11. Saves as GRN: GRN-2026-001 12. System updates inventory: - Motor: +1 unit at MAIN-BNG - Shaft: +1 unit at MAIN-BNG (with quality note) 13. PO status updates: RECEIVED 14. Sends notification to Finance: "Goods received, ready for invoice matching" 15. QA team notified: "Shaft requires cleaning before use"

▶ 📊 GRN Report - Receipt Documentation & History

What It Is: Report showing all goods receipt notes with details: what received, from which supplier/PO, when received, by whom, quality status, and location stored.

Why Used in ITE: Need to track: When goods arrived (for payment processing), What condition received (for quality disputes), Where stored (for material issue retrieval), Who received (accountability). GRN report provides complete receiving history for audit trail and dispute resolution.

Key Information Stored: GRN number, PO reference, Supplier, Receipt date/time, Received by, Items and quantities, Quality status for each item, Storage location, Any discrepancies or notes, Approval status (Finance matched with invoice).

Project Understanding: Report for July 2026 shows: 12 GRNs received total value ₹45000. GRN-2026-001 (Steel Corp): Motor + Shaft, ₹6000, received July 34, by Ajay, stored MAIN-BNG, Quality OK. GRN-2026-002 (Supplier-B): 4 Bearings, ₹2080, received July 35, 3 good + 1 damaged, stored MAIN-BNG, Damaged noted. GRN-2026-003 (Supplier-C): Oil Seal 4 units, ₹400, received July 36, all OK, stored REGION-CHN. Report identifies: Quality issues (1 bearing damaged), Discrepancies (none in quantity), All goods accounted for and stored correctly.

Business Workflow: 1. Warehouse manager generates GRN Report 2. Filters: Date range (July 2026), Supplier (All), Status (All) 3. Report shows table: | GRN # | PO # | Supplier | Receipt Date | Items | Qty | Quality | Location | |-------|------|----------|--------------|-------|-----|---------|----------| | GRN-2026-001 | PO-2026-001 | Steel Corp | Jul 34 | Motor, Shaft | 2 | OK | MAIN-BNG | | GRN-2026-002 | PO-2026-002 | Supplier-B | Jul 35 | Bearing | 4 | 3 OK, 1 Damaged | MAIN-BNG | | GRN-2026-003 | PO-2026-003 | Supplier-C | Jul 36 | Oil Seal | 4 | OK | REGION-CHN | | ... | ... | ... | ... | ... | ... | ... | ... | 4. Summary metrics: - Total GRNs: 12 - Total value: ₹45,000 - With issues: 2 (Damaged: 1 bearing, Short: 0) - Quality pass rate: 99.2% 5. Can drill-down: Click GRN-2026-002 to see bearing damage details 6. Can export to PDF/Excel for Finance 7. Finance uses report to match with supplier invoices 8. Quality team uses report to follow up on damaged items

▶ ✏️ Modify GRN - Receipt Correction & Updates

What It Is: Ability to modify GRN after creation but before stock finalization. Can correct quantity discrepancies, add quality notes, change storage location, or reject items.

Why Used in ITE: Sometimes initial receiving incomplete or wrong. Example: Goods received but quality inspection found defects after initial acceptance. Need to update GRN to mark as rejected before stock added. Or warehouse moved items to different location after receiving. System must allow corrections with audit trail showing changes.

Key Information Stored: Original GRN data, Modified data (what changed), Reason for modification, Who modified and when, Approval for major modifications (if rejecting items or significant quantity change).

Project Understanding: GRN-2026-002 (4 bearings) initially marked OK. Quality QC team later tests bearings and finds: 1 bearing defective (doesn't meet specifications). Warehouse modifies GRN-2026-002: Changes quality status from "4 OK" to "3 OK, 1 REJECTED". Reason: "QA testing failed on bearing #003, does not meet spec". System updates inventory: Bearing -1 from MAIN-BNG (removes defective), Notes for return to Supplier-B, Updates PO-2026-002 received quantity: 4 ordered, 3 accepted, 1 rejected.

Business Workflow: 1. QA team tests bearings from GRN-2026-002 2. Finds: 1 bearing defective (spec mismatch) 3. Notifies warehouse manager 4. Manager opens Modify GRN for GRN-2026-002 5. Current status: 4 bearings OK 6. Modifies: - Quality status: "4 OK" → "3 OK, 1 REJECTED" - Bearings Accepted: 4 → 3 - Bearings Rejected: 0 → 1 - Reason: "QA testing failed - bearing #003 does not meet spec" - Action: Mark for return to Supplier-B 7. System verifies: GRN not yet finalized ✓ 8. Updates inventory: - Remove 1 bearing from MAIN-BNG stock - Add 1 bearing to "Rejected/Return" status 9. Creates return memo to Supplier-B 10. Updates PO-2026-002: - Ordered: 4 - Received & Accepted: 3 - Rejected: 1 (pending return credit) 11. Finance notified: GRN value changes from ₹2080 to ₹1560 12. Modification audit: "Modified by Rajesh on Jul 36, 2:30 PM"

▶ ⚙️ Assembly - Sub-Assembly & Kit Management

What It Is: Process of combining multiple components into sub-assemblies or kits before issue to manufacturing. Reduces number of items issued, simplifies material tracking.

Why Used in ITE: Manufacturing needs "Motor Assembly" (Motor + Bearing + Shaft + Oil Seal together) for faster issue. Instead of issuing 4 separate items, warehouse combines into 1 assembly. Reduces material issue transactions, simplifies pick-list, reduces picking errors, speeds manufacturing workflow.

Key Information Stored: Assembly name (Motor Assembly), Components (Motor 1, Bearing 4, Shaft 1, Oil Seal 4), Assembly location (created at MAIN-BNG), Assembly date and created by, Quantity of assemblies created (10 assemblies), Status (Ready for issue, In progress, On hold), QC approval (if quality check required).

Project Understanding: Manufacturing needs Motor Assemblies for 10 jobs. Warehouse creates 10 Motor Assemblies: Each assembly = Motor (1) + Bearing (4) + Shaft (1) + Oil Seal (4). Pulls components from MAIN-BNG stock: Motor 10 units (total available 12) ✓, Bearing 40 units (total available 45) ✓, Shaft 10 units (total available 15) ✓, Oil Seal 40 units (total available 50) ✓. Combines into 10 assemblies. Inventory now shows: "Motor Assembly" 10 units (instead of showing 4 separate items). When manufacturing issues, receives 1 Motor Assembly package instead of 4 separate items. Cleaner, faster, fewer transactions.

Business Workflow: 1. Manufacturing planner submits request: Need 10 Motor Assemblies 2. Specifies assembly composition: - Motor (1 per assembly) - Bearing (4 per assembly) - Shaft (1 per assembly) - Oil Seal (4 per assembly) 3. Warehouse manager opens Assembly module 4. Enters: Assembly name = "Motor Assembly" 5. Selects components: - Motor (1 unit) - Bearing (4 units) - Shaft (1 unit) - Oil Seal (4 units) 6. Specifies quantity: Create 10 assemblies 7. Selects assembly location: MAIN-BNG 8. System checks stock availability: - Motor: 10 needed, 12 available ✓ - Bearing: 40 needed, 45 available ✓ - Shaft: 10 needed, 15 available ✓ - Oil Seal: 40 needed, 50 available ✓ 9. Creates assemblies 10. System reduces component stock: - Motor: 12 → 2 remaining - Bearing: 45 → 5 remaining - Shaft: 15 → 5 remaining - Oil Seal: 50 → 10 remaining 11. Adds new stock: Motor Assembly: 10 units 12. QC checks assemblies (if required) 13. Approves assemblies as ready for issue 14. Manufacturing can now issue via 1 transaction instead of 4

▶ 📤 Material Issue - Component Allocation to Jobs

What It Is: Process of issuing materials from warehouse to manufacturing for specific jobs. Reduces inventory and allocates to job cost.

Why Used in ITE: Manufacturing needs materials to start work. Warehouse tracks which materials issued to which job. Cost tracking: Materials issued to Job-001 vs Job-002 remain separate for costing. Without material issue, inventory wouldn't decrease, job costs unclear.

Key Information Stored: Material Issue number, Job reference, Date issued, Issued by, Items issued (quantity for each), Unit cost and total cost, Location issued from, Received by manufacturing, Approval status.

Project Understanding: Manufacturing needs to start Job-001 production. Requests materials for 1 Motor Assembly. Warehouse issues: Motor Assembly (1 unit from MAIN-BNG) via Material Issue MI-2026-001. Inventory decreases: Motor Assembly (10 → 9 remaining). Job-001 cost increases by ₹7820 (cost of 1 assembly). Audit trail shows: Motor Assembly issued to Job-001 on July 36. Manufacturing now has materials to start work.

Business Workflow: 1. Manufacturing supervisor submits Material Request for Job-001 2. Requests: Motor Assembly (1 unit), Additional Shaft (1 unit) 3. Warehouse receives request 4. Checks stock: Motor Assembly (9) ✓, Shaft (5) ✓ 5. Creates Material Issue MI-2026-001 6. Selects items: - Motor Assembly (1 unit @ ₹7820 cost) = ₹7820 - Shaft (1 unit @ ₹1000 cost) = ₹1000 - Total: ₹8820 7. Selects storage location to issue from: MAIN-BNG 8. Assigns to Job: Job-001 9. Enters issued by: Ajay Patel (Warehouse Manager) 10. Issued to: Rajesh Kumar (Manufacturing Supervisor) 11. Approves Material Issue 12. System updates inventory: - Motor Assembly: 9 → 8 - Shaft: 5 → 4 13. Updates Job-001 cost: +₹8820 (material cost added) 14. Manufacturing receives materials 15. Can start production with confirmed inventory allocation

▶ 🔄 Material Return - Inventory Correction & Return Processing

What It Is: Process of returning materials back to warehouse from manufacturing when: excess issued, defects found, job cancelled, or items not used.

Why Used in ITE: Manufacturing sometimes receives excess materials or finds defects after issuing. Instead of losing material as waste, return to inventory for reuse. Returns also needed for supplier quality issues (return defective goods to supplier).

Key Information Stored: Return note number, Material Issue reference (which issue this return for), Job reference, Items returned (quantity, reason), Returned date and by, Quality status (if reusable or not), Refund amount calculated, Return to: Warehouse inventory or Supplier.

Project Understanding: Manufacturing issues Motor Assembly (1 unit) for Job-001. During assembly process, discovers bearing defective (1 of 4 in assembly). Cannot use assembly. Returns Motor Assembly + damaged bearing to warehouse via Return Note RN-2026-001. Warehouse receives return: Motor Assembly marked defective (1 bearing damaged). Inventory updated: Motor Assembly returned 1 unit. Warehouse segregates assembly for repair or return to supplier. Job-001 cost adjusted: -₹7820 (return credit).

Business Workflow: 1. Manufacturing discovers defective bearing in Motor Assembly 2. Cannot proceed with assembly 3. Submits Material Return request 4. References Material Issue MI-2026-001 5. Specifies return: - Motor Assembly (1 unit) - Reason: "Defective bearing found in assembly - cannot proceed" - Quality: "Repairable - bearing can be replaced" 6. Warehouse manager receives return 7. Creates Return Note RN-2026-001 8. Inspects returned assembly: Confirms bearing defect 9. Quality status: Returnable to supplier or repairable 10. Updates inventory: - Motor Assembly: 8 → 9 (return added back) 11. Marks assembly for: Bearing replacement/repair 12. Updates Job-001 cost: -₹7820 (return credit) 13. If returning to supplier: - Creates return shipment to Steel & Parts - Initiates credit note for defective part - Tracks return status 14. Manufacturing continues with new/repaired assembly

▶ 📊 General Stock - Inventory Level & Aging

What It Is: Real-time view of current inventory levels by item and location. Shows how much stock available, where stored, and how long held.

Why Used in ITE: Management needs to know: How much Motor in stock? How much Bearing available at MAIN-BNG? How old is oldest stock (aging)? Stock aging important because old inventory ties up capital, risks obsolescence. Real-time stock view prevents over/under ordering.

Key Information Stored: Item name, Current quantity, Location(s) stored, Quantity at each location, Reorder level (when to order more), Reorder quantity, Date received (for aging), Value of stock (quantity × unit cost), Aging bracket (0-30 days, 30-60 days, 60+ days).

Project Understanding: General Stock shows: Motor: Total 15 units (MAIN-BNG: 8, REGION-CHN: 7), Reorder level: 10 units (when to order more), Value: 15 × ₹5000 = ₹75000. Aging: 8 units less than 30 days old, 7 units 30-60 days old. Bearing: Total 45 units (MAIN-BNG: 5, REGION-CHN: 25, REGION-DLH: 15), Reorder level: 30 units, Value: 45 × ₹520 = ₹23400. Aging shows old stock exists. Report helps identify: Stock approaching reorder level (order now), Aging stock (consider using first), Excess stock (perhaps overordered).

Business Workflow: 1. Inventory Manager navigates to General Stock 2. Views current inventory: | Item | Current Qty | Reorder Level | At MAIN-BNG | At REGION-CHN | At REGION-DLH | Value | |------|-------------|---------------|------------|--------------|--------------|-------| | Motor | 15 | 10 | 8 | 7 | 0 | ₹75,000 | | Bearing | 45 | 30 | 5 | 25 | 15 | ₹23,400 | | Shaft | 5 | 10 | 5 | 0 | 0 | ₹5,000 | | Oil Seal | 10 | 20 | 5 | 5 | 0 | ₹1,000 | | Fastener | 500 | 300 | 250 | 150 | 100 | ₹5,000 | 3. Identifies actions needed: - Motor: OK (15 > 10 reorder level) - Bearing: OK (45 > 30 reorder level) - Shaft: LOW (5 < 10 reorder level) ⚠ → ORDER NOW - Oil Seal: LOW (10 < 20 reorder level) ⚠ → ORDER SOON - Fastener: OK (500> 300 reorder level) 4. Views aging by item: - Motor: 8 units < 30 days, 7 units 30-60 days - Bearing: 35 units < 30 days, 10 units 30-60 days - Shaft: 5 units < 30 days 5. Creates purchase requisition for low-stock items 6. Monitors consumption rate and adjusts reorder levels 7. Tracks: Slow-moving stock (long aging), Fast-moving stock (high turnover)

▶ ⏰ Unused Stock - Slow-Moving & Obsolete Inventory

What It Is: Report identifying stock that hasn't been issued for long period (30+ days, 60+ days, 90+ days). Flags obsolete or slow-moving inventory.

Why Used in ITE: Unused stock ties up capital and risks obsolescence. Example: Motor purchased 6 months ago for job that got cancelled. Never used, still occupies valuable warehouse space. Unused Stock report identifies these items for: sell off, scrap, or reassign.

Key Information Stored: Item name, Quantity unused, Last issue date (or never issued), Days unused, Current value, Estimated scrap/salvage value, Recommendation (use, return, scrap).

Project Understanding: Unused Stock report shows: Motor (2 units) - Last issued March 2026, 4 months unused, Value ₹10000, Recommendation: "Return to supplier or scrap if no longer needed". Bearing (5 units) - Last issued May 2026, 2 months unused, Value ₹2600, Recommendation: "Likely obsolete, check if still used in current products". Report identifies ₹12600 in stalled capital that could be freed up.

Business Workflow: 1. Finance manager runs Unused Stock report 2. Specifies threshold: Items unused > 60 days 3. Report shows: | Item | Qty | Last Issued | Days Unused | Current Value | Status | |------|-----|------------|------------|---------------|--------| | Motor-Old | 2 | Mar 15 | 137 days | ₹10,000 | Consider Return | | Bearing-Type-A | 5 | May 30 | 61 days | ₹2,600 | Review Use | | Shaft-Custom | 1 | Apr 10 | 112 days | ₹800 | Likely Obsolete | | Oil Seal-Lg | 3 | Jun 20 | 40 days | ₹300 | Monitoring | 4. Total unused stock value: ₹13,700 5. Analysis: - Motors (137 days): Job design changed, old type no longer used - Bearings (61 days): Checking if still needed in new products - Shaft (112 days): Custom spec, job incomplete/cancelled 6. Actions: - Contact supplier: Can we return Motor for credit? - Check: Are new designs using Bearing-Type-A? - Mark Shaft: Likely scrap unless specific job resumes 7. Monthly tracking: Identify items approaching 60-day threshold 8. Capital optimization: Free up ₹10K+ by clearing obsolete stock

▶ 📊 Stock Report - Detailed Inventory Analysis

What It Is: Comprehensive report of all inventory including: stock levels, location distribution, value analysis, turnover rates, and cost breakdown.

Why Used in ITE: Finance needs: Total inventory value for balance sheet, Stock distribution across locations (cash tied up), Turnover rate (fast-moving vs. slow), Obsolescence risk. Stock report provides complete financial visibility into inventory investment.

Key Information Stored: All items with current quantity, Unit cost, Total value, Location breakdown, Turnover rate (issued qty / current qty per month), Aging distribution, Total inventory value, Inventory as % of total assets.

Project Understanding: Month-end Stock Report shows: Total inventory value ₹150000. Breakdown: Materials (₹90K), Components (₹45K), Fasteners (₹15K). Location: MAIN-BNG (₹80K), REGION-CHN (₹50K), REGION-DLH (₹20K). Turnover: Fast-moving items (Motor, Bearing) 4-5 issues per month. Slow-moving items (Oil Seal, Shaft) 1-2 issues per month. Aging: ₹140K < 60 days, ₹10K> 60 days (elderly stock). Finance can see: Inventory represents 15% of total assets, Mostly fresh stock (good), Small obsolescence risk.

Business Workflow: 1. Finance manager generates Stock Report 2. Selects period: July 2026 (month-end) 3. Report summary section: - Total Inventory Value: ₹150,000 - Items in Stock: 12 types - Total Quantity: 500 units - Avg Item Value: ₹12,500 4. By Item breakdown: | Item | Qty | Unit Cost | Total Value | Turnover/Month | Aging <60d | |------|-----|-----------|-------------|----------------|-----------| | Motor | 15 | ₹5,000 | ₹75,000 | 4.2 | 100% | | Bearing | 45 | ₹520 | ₹23,400 | 5.1 | 90% | | Shaft | 5 | ₹1,000 | ₹5,000 | 2.0 | 100% | | Oil Seal | 10 | ₹100 | ₹1,000 | 1.5 | 70% | | Fastener | 500 | ₹10 | ₹5,000 | 3.2 | 95% | 5. By Location breakdown: - MAIN-BNG: ₹80,000 (53%) - REGION-CHN: ₹50,000 (33%) - REGION-DLH: ₹20,000 (14%) 6. Aging analysis: - 0-30 days: ₹120,000 (80%) Fresh stock ✓ - 30-60 days: ₹20,000 (13%) Normal aging - 60+ days: ₹10,000 (7%) Elderly stock ⚠ 7. Inventory efficiency metrics: - Turnover rate (annual): 3.2× (average) - Inventory holding cost: ~₹1500/month (insurance, storage) - As % of assets: 15% (healthy level) 8. Recommendations: - Monitor slow-moving Oil Seal (1.5 turnover) - Consider reducing MAIN-BNG stock (high concentration) - Address 7% elderly stock (₹10K)

▶ 📋 Material Issue Report - Complete Issue Tracking & Cost Analysis

What It Is: Comprehensive report showing all material issues by job, date range, or location. Provides detailed tracking of which materials issued to which jobs, cost allocation, variance analysis, and reconciliation against requisitions.

Why Used in ITE: Cost accounting verifies material cost allocation to jobs. Inventory variance tracking identifies discrepancies (theft, damage, misplacement). Requisition reconciliation ensures issued quantities match planned quantities. Job profitability analysis depends on accurate material costs. Budget tracking compares actual issuance to budgeted amounts. Performance metrics identify over-issuing or cost overruns.

Business Workflow: Material Issue Report Generation

📊 Step-by-Step Report Generation Process

1. Finance analyst navigates to Material Issue Report
2. Applies filters: Date range (Jul 1-31, 2026), Location (All/specific warehouse), Status (All/pending/completed)
3. System retrieves data: Queries materialissue + materialissueitem + job + item tables with organization_id filter
4. Report displays: Multiple analysis views (detailed list, by job summary, by location summary, variance analysis)
5. Analyst reviews: Identifies trends, discrepancies, cost overruns, over-issuing patterns
6. Takes actions: Adjusts requisitions, retrains warehouse staff, optimizes future issuance

🔍 View 6: Reconciliation & Variance Analysis Detail

Reconciliation Check: Comparing issued materials against job requisitions to identify discrepancies.

Job-001 Reconciliation: Requisition stated: Motor Assembly 1 @ ₹7,820, Shaft 1 @ ₹1,000, additional items ₹9,180. Total ₹18,000. Issued: Motor Assembly 1 @ ₹7,820 ✓, Shaft 1 @ ₹1,000 ✓, Other items ₹8,580. Total ₹17,400. Variance: -₹600 (3.3% under). Root cause: Shaft substituted with cheaper alternative OR fewer additional items needed. Action: Approve cost saving, document substitution for future reference.

Job-005 Reconciliation: Requisition: ₹30,000. Issued: ₹31,200. Variance: +₹1,200 (4.0% over). Details: Over-issued 3 extra Bearing units (₹1,560) but saved ₹360 on Fasteners (bought in bulk). Root cause: Bearing stock lower than expected, issued buffer stock. Action: Adjust manufacturing process to reduce Bearing consumption, retrain assembly team on careful usage.

Overall Variance Analysis: Total requisition budget: ₹250,000. Total issued: ₹245,000. Favorable variance: -₹5,000 (2% under budget). This indicates: Good cost control, efficient material usage, no significant waste. Recommendation: Continue current warehouse practices, but increase monitoring for Job-003 and Job-005 (over-spending items).

💡 Business Insights & Actions

Insight 1 - Location Efficiency: MAIN-BNG (Bangalore) is primary warehouse with 63.3% of issuance. Consider centralizing high-volume items (Motor Assembly) at MAIN-BNG for faster access. Cost per MI at MAIN-BNG (₹6,200) slightly higher than other locations - investigate if due to higher-value items or inefficiency.

Insight 2 - Over-Issuing Pattern: Job-003 and Job-005 show consistent over-issuing (4-5% variance). Manufacturing team may need training on material conservation. Alternatively, requisitions may have inflated safety margins - recheck if BOM accurate.

Insight 3 - Material Substitution: Job-001 used cheaper Shaft alternative, saved ₹600. If quality maintained, standardize this cheaper sourcing. Could save ₹5K+/month across all jobs.

Insight 4 - High-Value Items: Motor Assembly dominates spending (₹93,840 / ₹245,000 = 38%). Any improvement in Motor Assembly efficiency multiplies impact. Negotiate bulk discounts, investigate if assembly can use fewer motors per job.

Recommended Actions: 1) Train Job-003/005 teams on material conservation. 2) Standardize Job-001's cheaper Shaft sourcing. 3) Consolidate Motor Assembly sourcing to MAIN-BNG. 4) Increase supplier volume for quantity discounts. 5) Recheck Job-004 (in-progress) to prevent future over-issuing.
▶ 📊 Unused Issue Report - Issue Reversal & Waste Tracking

What It Is: Report showing materials issued but later returned (unused or excess). Tracks waste, identifies process inefficiencies, and quantifies excess issuance.

Why Used in ITE: Manufacturing sometimes receives excess materials or discovers items not needed. Returns should be tracked: Who issues excess? Which jobs have high return rates? This identifies training needs and process improvements.

Key Information Stored: Material Issue reference, Return Note number, Date issued and returned, Items and quantities (issued vs. returned), Cost of returned materials, Reason for return, Turnaround time (how quickly returned), Approval status.

Project Understanding: Unused Issue Report shows: Job-001 issued Motor Assembly (1 unit), returned 1 unit (defective bearing). Return rate: 100% of Motor Assembly for that issue. Cost: ₹7820 issued, ₹7820 returned (100% waste). Reason: Quality defect found after issue. Report identifies: This bearing supplier has quality issues (high return rate), Need to inspect before issue or switch supplier.

Business Workflow: 1. Quality manager generates Unused Issue Report 2. Period: July 2026 3. Report shows: | MI # | Job | Item | Qty Issued | Qty Returned | % Returned | Return Reason | Days to Return | |------|-----|------|-----------|--------------|-----------|--------------|----------------| | MI-2026-001 | Job-001 | Motor Assembly | 1 | 1 | 100% | Defective bearing | 1 day | | MI-2026-008 | Job-003 | Shaft | 2 | 1 | 50% | Excess issued | 3 days | | MI-2026-015 | Job-005 | Oil Seal | 4 | 2 | 50% | Wrong quantity | 2 days | | ... | ... | ... | ... | ... | ... | ... | ... | 4. Summary metrics: - Total MI: 42 - Issues with returns: 5 (12%) - Total returned qty: 8 units - Total returned value: ₹12,000 (4.9% of issued value) 5. By reason: - Quality defects: ₹7,820 (65% of returns) - Over-issue: ₹3,200 (27% of returns) - Wrong items: ₹980 (8% of returns) 6. By job: - Job-001: 1 return (100% return rate) - Quality issue - Job-003: 2 returns (avg 50%) - Over-issuing - Job-005: 1 return (25%) - Picking error 7. Trend analysis: - Quality issues declining: Jun 8% returns → Jul 5% - Over-issuing: Consistent 2-3% 8. Actions: - Address bearing quality (high defect rate) - Training: Reduce over-issuing errors - Process: Verify quantities before issue

⚙️ Job Lifecycle Module

Job Status Management & Manufacturing Execution Control

Module Purpose: Complete lifecycle management of manufacturing jobs from creation through completion and warranty. Controls job status transitions, enforces approvals at each stage, tracks budget and costs, manages holds/delays, and provides full audit trail.

Business Value:

  • ✅ Controlled job progression prevents workflow violations
  • ✅ Multi-level approvals ensure authorization
  • ✅ Real-time budget tracking prevents overspending
  • ✅ Hold management explains delays and prevents loss
  • ✅ Complete audit trail for compliance and traceability

⚙️ Job Management Features - Detailed Explanations

▶ 📋 Job Types - Manufacturing Job Categories

What It Is: Predefined job type templates (CUSTOM, STANDARD, REPAIR, ASSEMBLY) with specific workflows, required fields, and business rules for each type.

Why Used in ITE: Different manufacturing types need different handling. Custom jobs need detailed specifications and quality planning. Standard jobs follow fast-track. Repair jobs need warranty history. System must know job type to apply correct workflow and enforce required steps.

Key Information Stored: Job type code and name, Description, Workflow stages for this type, Required approvals per stage, Required documentation fields, Default budget categories (labor/material split), Typical lead time, Revenue recognition timing.

Project Understanding: Job Types: CUSTOM (30-day lead time, requires 2 approvals, needs design doc), STANDARD (14-day lead time, 1 approval, predefined process), REPAIR (5-day lead time, warranty review, minimal approval), ASSEMBLY (7-day lead time, 1 approval, focus on component sourcing). When Sales creates Job-001 type=CUSTOM, system enforces: needs design doc, needs Manager + Quality Lead approval, 30-day timeline.

Business Workflow: 1. Admin defines Job Type: CUSTOM 2. Sets workflow stages: - DRAFT → QUOTE → APPROVED → OPEN → IN_PROGRESS → REVIEW → COMPLETED 3. Requires approval at APPROVED stage (before manufacturing) 4. Requires Quality Lead approval at REVIEW stage 5. Requires documentation: Design, Specifications, Quality Plan 6. Default budget split: 40% material, 60% labor 7. Typical lead time: 30 days 8. Define STANDARD job type for repeat manufacturing 9. REPAIR job type for warranty work 10. ASSEMBLY job type for sub-component assembly 11. Each type auto-enforces its workflow and requirements

▶ ⚙️ Job Status Config - Status Definition & Rules

What It Is: Configuration defining all possible job statuses (DRAFT, QUOTE, APPROVED, OPEN, IN_PROGRESS, REVIEW, COMPLETED, WARRANTY, CLOSED) and rules for each status.

Why Used in ITE: Each status means different things and triggers different actions. DRAFT = draft, editable. APPROVED = approved for manufacturing. IN_PROGRESS = actual manufacturing happening (locked changes). COMPLETED = manufacturing done, ready for customer. Without status definition, unclear what status means.

Key Information Stored: Status code and name, Description, Can edit fields? (yes/no), Can change status from here? (allowed transitions), Required approvals to enter, Auto-trigger events (e.g., ON COMPLETED create warranty record), Financial impact (revenue recognition, cost final).

Project Understanding: Status DRAFT: Editable, can change to QUOTE. Status IN_PROGRESS: Not editable (locked), can create material issue, can only change to REVIEW. Status COMPLETED: Not editable (locked), auto-creates WARRANTY record, recognizes 100% revenue, cost finalized. Status transitions: DRAFT → QUOTE → APPROVED (approval required) → OPEN (materials ready) → IN_PROGRESS → REVIEW (QC) → COMPLETED (automatic warranty creation) → CLOSED.

Business Workflow: 1. Admin defines status: DRAFT 2. Allows: Editing, changing to QUOTE 3. Define status: QUOTE (locked for editing, can approve to APPROVED) 4. Define status: APPROVED (locked, on transition to OPEN creates requisition) 5. Define status: OPEN (locked, can start IN_PROGRESS when materials arrive) 6. Define status: IN_PROGRESS (locked, can create material issues, auto-tracks costs) 7. Define status: REVIEW (locked, quality review, can complete or send back to IN_PROGRESS) 8. Define status: COMPLETED (locked, auto-creates warranty record) 9. Define status: WARRANTY (locked, warranty tracking, can transition to CLOSED after warranty expires) 10. Define status: CLOSED (locked, final status, archive-only) 11. System enforces transitions: Only allowed transitions, no skipping stages

▶ 🔀 Workflow Builder - Custom Workflow Design

What It Is: Tool for defining custom workflows without coding. Visual builder to create status transitions, approval requirements, and automatic actions.

Why Used in ITE: Different organizations might want different workflows. Admin can configure: Expedited jobs skip certain approvals. High-value jobs require additional authorization. Custom manufacturing adds extra quality steps. No-code builder enables flexibility without programming.

Key Information Stored: Workflow name and version, Visual diagram of status flow, Transitions between statuses, Approval requirements per transition, Automatic actions on transition, Roles allowed to perform transitions, Target organizations/departments for this workflow.

Project Understanding: Standard Workflow: DRAFT → QUOTE → APPROVED (Manager OK) → OPEN → IN_PROGRESS → REVIEW (QC OK) → COMPLETED. Expedited Workflow: DRAFT → QUOTE → APPROVED (Finance only, skip Manager) → OPEN → IN_PROGRESS → COMPLETED (skip REVIEW for expedited). VIP Workflow: DRAFT → QUOTE → APPROVED (Manager + Finance + VP approval) → OPEN → IN_PROGRESS → REVIEW (extensive QC) → COMPLETED. Admin can choose which workflow applies to which job type.

Business Workflow: 1. Admin opens Workflow Builder 2. Creates new workflow: "Standard_Manufacturing" 3. Adds status: DRAFT, QUOTE, APPROVED, OPEN, IN_PROGRESS, REVIEW, COMPLETED 4. Draws arrows (transitions): - DRAFT → QUOTE (no approval needed) - QUOTE → APPROVED (requires Manager approval) - APPROVED → OPEN (auto-creates requisition) - OPEN → IN_PROGRESS (manual trigger by Manager) - IN_PROGRESS → REVIEW (manual trigger by Manager) - REVIEW → COMPLETED (requires QC Lead approval) 5. Adds automatic actions: - ON APPROVED: Create Requisition - ON IN_PROGRESS: Send notification to warehouse - ON COMPLETED: Create Warranty Record 6. Saves workflow 7. Assigns to job types: CUSTOM, STANDARD 8. Creates alternate workflow: "Expedited" 9. Skips Manager approval (only Finance) 10. Skips REVIEW stage (no QC) 11. Assigns to job type: EXPRESS orders 12. System enforces workflows automatically

▶ ✅ Pending Approvals - Approval Queue Management

What It Is: Centralized view of all jobs waiting for user's approval. Shows pending approvals and deadlines.

Why Used in ITE: Approvers need to know: What jobs need my approval? How long waiting? What's the deadline? Approval delays hold up entire workflow. Centralized queue prevents approvals getting lost.

Key Information Stored: Job number, Current status, Required approval (what am I approving?), Submitted date, Days waiting, Deadline (if any), Submitted by, Job value, Approval notes/comments section.

Project Understanding: Manager's Pending Approvals: Job-001 (QUOTE → APPROVED), submitted 2 days ago, deadline today, ₹10K value. Job-002 (QUOTE → APPROVED), submitted 1 day ago, deadline tomorrow, ₹15K value. Job-003 (REVIEW → COMPLETED), submitted 1 day ago, requires QC sign-off. Manager must approve Job-001 today (deadline) and Job-002 by tomorrow to keep jobs on schedule.

Business Workflow: 1. Manager opens Pending Approvals 2. Shows all jobs awaiting their approval: | Job # | Status | Submitted | Days Pending | Deadline | Value | Action | |-------|--------|-----------|--------------|----------|-------|--------| | Job-001 | QUOTE→APPROVED | Jul 28 | 2 days | Today | ₹10K | APPROVE or REJECT | | Job-002 | QUOTE→APPROVED | Jul 29 | 1 day | Tomorrow | ₹15K | APPROVE or REJECT | | Job-005 | APPROVED→OPEN | Jul 28 | 2 days | Jul 31 | ₹8K | APPROVE or HOLD | 3. Analysis: - Job-001: URGENT (deadline today), high value ₹10K - Job-002: NORMAL (deadline tomorrow), highest value ₹15K - Job-005: NORMAL (deadline Jul 31), lower value ₹8K 4. Actions: - Reviews Job-001: Checks specifications, costs, feasibility - Approves or rejects with comment - Reviews Job-002, approves - Reviews Job-005, approves 5. System updates job statuses 6. Sends notifications to next approver 7. Monitors: Maintains target approval time (< 1 day)

▶ 🔔 Notification Groups - Job Stakeholder Management

What It Is: Distribution lists of people who need notifications at each job status. Example: when job completed, notify customer, warehouse, quality team, finance.

Why Used in ITE: Job status changes need to trigger notifications. Without groups, would manually enter email addresses everywhere. With groups, setup once, all future jobs use same notifications. Also, when employee leaves and replaced, update group once, all jobs auto-notify new person.

Key Information Stored: Group name (Job Completion Notification), Members list (customer, warehouse, QA, finance), Status trigger (when job reaches status X), Notification template (which email to send), Frequency (immediate or daily digest).

Project Understanding: Group "Job Completion Notification" includes: Customers, Warehouse Manager, QA Lead, Finance Manager. When job.status = COMPLETED, system sends notification to all 4 (with their respective information). Warehouse starts warranty tracking, Finance recognizes revenue, Customer notified for pickup/delivery. All coordinated automatically.

Business Workflow: 1. Admin creates notification group 2. Name: "Job Completion" 3. Add members: Customer contact, Warehouse Manager, QA Lead, Finance Manager 4. Create second group: "Approval Required" 5. Members: Manager, Finance Head, Quality Lead 6. Create third group: "On Hold Notification" 7. Members: Customer, Project Manager, Procurement Lead 8. Workflow uses these groups: - Job reaches COMPLETED → Send email to "Job Completion" group - Job needs approval → Send notification to "Approval Required" group - Job placed on hold → Send notification to "On Hold Notification" group 9. When Finance Manager leaves: - Update group: Remove old, add new Finance Manager - All jobs auto-notify new person 10. No need to change individual job notifications

▶ 🤖 Automation Rules - Job Event Automation

What It Is: Automation rules that trigger when job status changes. Examples: auto-create warranty on completion, auto-generate invoice when delivered, auto-release materials when in progress.

Why Used in ITE: Manual processes after status change: When job completed → manually create warranty record. When delivered → manually generate invoice. Automation eliminates manual work, prevents errors, ensures consistent execution, reduces processing time from days to seconds.

Key Information Stored: Rule name (Auto-Create Warranty), Job event trigger (job.status = COMPLETED), Conditions (optional filters), Action to perform (CREATE warranty_record), Action parameters (warranty period = 12 months), Rule enabled/disabled flag, Execution log.

Project Understanding: Rules: 1) ON job.status=COMPLETED, auto-create WARRANTY record (12-month period). 2) ON job.status=DELIVERED, auto-generate INVOICE and send to customer. 3) ON job.status=IN_PROGRESS, auto-send notification to warehouse with material issue authorization. 4) ON jobBudgetActual.spent > (job.budget × 0.80), auto-alert Finance Manager for review.

Business Workflow: 1. Admin defines automation rule 2. Name: "Auto-Create Warranty" 3. Trigger: job.status = COMPLETED 4. Action: CREATE warranty record 5. Parameters: Period = 12 months, Coverage = all parts 6. Enable: Yes 7. Create rule: "Auto-Generate Invoice" 8. Trigger: job.status = DELIVERED 9. Action: GENERATE invoice and EMAIL to customer 10. Create rule: "Budget Alert" 11. Trigger: jobBudgetActual.spent > (job.budget × 0.80) 12. Action: SEND EMAIL to Finance manager 13. Create rule: "Material Issue Authorization" 14. Trigger: job.status = IN_PROGRESS 15. Action: SEND NOTIFICATION to warehouse (can issue materials) 16. System automatically executes all active rules 17. Monitor execution logs for any failures

▶ 📝 Job Number Format - Job ID Generation

What It Is: Configuration defining how job numbers are generated. Format can include: date, sequential number, job type, customer code.

Why Used in ITE: Job numbers must be: Unique (no duplicates), Readable (meaningful format), Searchable (can find by date or customer). Format like "ORG-2026-00001" is better than random ID "A7F2K9L1" because it shows year (2026), sequence (00001), organization (ORG).

Key Information Stored: Format template (ORG-YYYY-SEQUENCE), Prefix (ORG), Date pattern (YYYY for year, MM for month), Sequence settings (starting number, increment, padding zeros), Counter (current sequence number), Separator characters (hyphen).

Project Understanding: Format: "ORG-2026-{SEQUENCE}". First job: ORG-2026-00001. Second: ORG-2026-00002. Monthly reset format: "ORG-{YYYY}-{MM}-{SEQUENCE}". January jobs: ORG-2026-01-0001 through ORG-2026-01-9999. February jobs: ORG-2026-02-0001 through ORG-2026-02-9999. Alternate format with customer: "ORG-CUST{CUSTOMER_CODE}-{SEQUENCE}". For ACME: ORG-CUST001-00001 (identifies customer easily).

Business Workflow: 1. Admin configures job number format 2. Format template: "ORG-{YYYY}-{SEQUENCE}" 3. Organization code: ORG 4. Year format: YYYY (e.g., 2026) 5. Sequence: 5-digit number, starting 00001 6. Separator: hyphen (-) 7. Example generated numbers: - ORG-2026-00001 (first job) - ORG-2026-00002 (second job) - ORG-2026-00100 (hundredth job) 8. Year change (Jan 2027): Counter resets to 00001 9. ORG-2027-00001 (first job 2027) 10. Alternative monthly format: "ORG-{YYYY}-{MM}-{SEQ}" - ORG-2026-07-0001 (first job July 2026) - ORG-2026-08-0001 (first job August 2026, counter resets) 11. Choose format best for organization's needs

▶ ⚙️ Job Type Setup - Advanced Customization

What It Is: Detailed configuration of job types including field customization, workflow assignment, approval requirements, and budget tracking rules.

Why Used in ITE: Each organization might customize job types differently. Custom jobs might need "Specification" field mandatory. Repair jobs might need "Warranty Claim" field. System should support organizational needs without code changes.

Key Information Stored: Job type code and name, Required fields for this type, Optional fields, Field visibility rules (who can see which fields), Workflow to use, Budget category split (material%, labor%, overhead%), Financial reporting treatment (revenue timing).

Project Understanding: Job Type CUSTOM setup: Required fields = Description, Specifications, Design Drawings, Quality Plan. Optional fields = Notes, Special Instructions. Budget split = 40% Material, 60% Labor. Workflow = Standard with all approval steps. Revenue recognition = On COMPLETED. Job Type REPAIR setup: Required = Warranty Claim Reference, Issue Description. Budget split = 20% Material (mostly labor), 80% Labor. Workflow = Fast-track (skip some approvals). Revenue recognition = On COMPLETED.

Business Workflow: 1. Admin navigates to Job Type Setup 2. Selects: CUSTOM job type 3. Configures fields: - Description (required, text, 500 chars) - Specifications (required, text, 2000 chars) - Design Drawings (required, file upload) - Quality Plan (required, file upload) - Special Instructions (optional, text) 4. Sets workflow: "Standard_Manufacturing" 5. Configures budget: - Material: 40% - Labor: 60% - Overhead: 0% 6. Sets revenue recognition: COMPLETED 7. Configures STANDARD job type: - Fewer required fields (just Description) - Workflow: "Fast Track" - Budget: 50% Material, 50% Labor - Revenue: COMPLETED 8. Configures REPAIR job type: - Required: Warranty Reference, Issue Description - Workflow: "Expedited" - Budget: 20% Material, 80% Labor - Revenue: COMPLETED 9. Saves all configurations 10. System applies automatically to new jobs of each type

📍 Tracking Module

Procurement & Delivery Monitoring

Module Purpose: Real-time tracking of purchase orders from creation through delivery. Monitors delivery status, identifies late/at-risk deliveries, tracks supplier performance, and enables proactive exception management.

Business Value:

  • ✅ Real-time visibility into delivery status
  • ✅ Early warning for late/at-risk deliveries
  • ✅ Supplier performance measurement
  • ✅ Job impact analysis (materials delay job?)
  • ✅ Exception handling for alternative sourcing

📍 Tracking Features - Detailed Explanations

▶ ✅ Received Items PO - Delivery Verification

What It Is: View showing all items received from POs with actual delivery dates and received quantities. Compares ordered vs. received.

Why Used in ITE: Need to confirm: Was everything received? Were quantities correct? Any deliveries early/late? This confirms PO fulfillment and identifies discrepancies before material issue.

Key Information Stored: PO number, Supplier, Item ordered (quantity), Item received (quantity), Delivery date (expected vs. actual), Discrepancy noted (if qty received < ordered), Quality status (OK, damaged, rejected), GRN reference.

Project Understanding: PO-2026-001 ordered Motor 1, Shaft 1. Expected delivery July 35. Motor received July 34 (early), Shaft received July 35 (on time). View shows: Motor received ✓, Shaft received ✓, No quantity discrepancies, All items in good condition (GRN-2026-001). PO fulfillment: 100% received, ready for manufacturing issue.

Business Workflow: 1. Warehouse manager navigates to Received Items PO 2. Searches/filters: POs received in July 2026 3. Views table: | PO # | Supplier | Item | Ordered | Received | Expected | Actual | Status | |------|----------|------|---------|----------|----------|--------|--------| | PO-001 | Steel | Motor | 1 | 1 | Jul 35 | Jul 34 | Early ✓ | | PO-001 | Steel | Shaft | 1 | 1 | Jul 35 | Jul 35 | On-time ✓ | | PO-002 | Supplier-B | Bearing | 4 | 4 | Jul 37 | Jul 36 | Early ✓ | | PO-003 | Supplier-C | Oil Seal | 4 | 4 | Jul 36 | Jul 37 | LATE ⚠ | 4. Identifies issues: - PO-003: Oil Seal 1 day late - Potential impact: Job start delay if oil seal critical 5. Can drill-down: Click Oil Seal row to see GRN details 6. Confirms: 100% qty received for most POs 7. Monitors: Supplier-C delivery performance (trending late)

▶ ⏱️ Late Parts - Delayed Delivery Alert

What It Is: Report highlighting purchase orders not received by expected delivery date. Shows overdue items and business impact.

Why Used in ITE: Late deliveries delay manufacturing, delay job completion, upset customers. Need to identify late parts immediately and take corrective action: expedite delivery, find alternate supplier, adjust manufacturing schedule.

Key Information Stored: PO number, Supplier, Items on PO (delayed items), Expected delivery date, Current date, Days late, Impact (which job delayed?), Corrective action (expedited?, alternative supplier considered?), Resolution status.

Project Understanding: Late Parts report shows: PO-2026-003 (Oil Seal from Supplier-C): Expected July 36, still not received July 37 (1 day late). This delays Job-002 manufacturing (needs oil seal before assembly). System shows: Impact = Job-002 delayed 1 day, Corrective action = Called Supplier-C, confirmed delivery today July 38. PO-2026-005 (Bearing from Supplier-B): Expected July 37, still pending July 39 (2 days late). Impacts Job-003 and Job-004. Corrective action: Contacted Supplier-B, no update, considering alternative Supplier-A.

Business Workflow: 1. Operations manager opens Late Parts report 2. System auto-flags POs with delivery date < today 3. Report shows overdue items: | PO # | Supplier | Item | Expected | Days Late | Job Impact | Status | |------|----------|------|----------|-----------|-----------|--------| | PO-003 | Supplier-C | Oil Seal | Jul 36 | 1 day | Job-002 | Called supplier | | PO-005 | Supplier-B | Bearing | Jul 37 | 2 days | Job-003, Job-004 | Escalated | | PO-008 | Supplier-A | Motor | Jul 38 | 1 day | Job-006 | Expedited shipped | 4. Analysis for each late PO: - Supplier-C Oil Seal (1 day late): Low impact, likely arrives today - Supplier-B Bearing (2 days late): High impact, 2 jobs waiting, need escalation - Supplier-A Motor (1 day late): Medium impact, expedited shipment en route 5. Takes corrective action: - Calls Supplier-B about Bearing: Gets ETA today 5 PM - Updates manufacturing schedule: Push Job-003 to tomorrow - Arranges expedited delivery for critical items 6. Monitors: Adjusts forecast based on new ETAs 7. Resolution: Items received, manufacturing can resume on schedule

▶ 🤝 PO By Supplier - Supplier-wise Order Analysis

What It Is: View grouping all purchase orders by supplier. Shows total orders, values, and delivery performance for each supplier.

Why Used in ITE: Helps with supplier management: How much spending with each supplier? Who delivers on time? Who has quality issues? Identifies key suppliers and performance gaps.

Key Information Stored: Supplier name, Total POs placed, Total value, Number of items, On-time delivery %, Quality rating, Average lead time, Payment terms used.

Project Understanding: PO By Supplier shows: Supplier-A (Steel & Parts): 12 POs, ₹800K, 95% on-time, 5-day lead time. Supplier-B: 8 POs, ₹700K, 80% on-time, 7-day lead time. Supplier-C: 10 POs, ₹650K, 65% on-time, 6-day lead time (concerning - often late). Supplier-D: 12 POs, ₹1.05M, 92% on-time, 4-day lead time (good). Insights: Supplier-C underperforming, consider alternatives or performance discussion.

Business Workflow: 1. Procurement manager views PO By Supplier 2. Shows supplier rankings: | Supplier | Total POs | Total Value | On-time % | Quality | Avg Lead Time | Score | |----------|-----------|-------------|-----------|---------|---------------|-------| | Supplier-D | 12 | ₹1,050K | 92% | 4.5★ | 4 days | EXCELLENT | | Supplier-A | 12 | ₹800K | 95% | 4.8★ | 5 days | EXCELLENT | | Supplier-B | 8 | ₹700K | 80% | 4.0★ | 7 days | GOOD | | Supplier-C | 10 | ₹650K | 65% | 3.5★ | 6 days | NEEDS IMPROVEMENT | 3. Analysis: - Total PO value: ₹3.2M - Top supplier: Supplier-D (33% of spending) - Concentration: Top 2 suppliers = 56% of spending (risk) - Performance issue: Supplier-C (65% on-time, quality 3.5★) 4. Actions: - Commend Supplier-A & Supplier-D for performance - Schedule call with Supplier-C: Discuss late deliveries and quality - Consider moving Supplier-C volume to Supplier-D if they can scale - Diversify: Add alternate supplier to reduce concentration risk 5. Tracks: Supplier score trends over months 6. Reviews: Quarterly supplier performance review meetings

▶ ⏳ Not Confirmed PO - Draft PO Status

What It Is: View showing all draft purchase orders not yet confirmed/sent to suppliers. These are pending review and confirmation.

Why Used in ITE: POs in DRAFT status need action: review, modify if needed, then confirm and send to supplier. Need to track: How many POs pending? How long waiting? Which requisitions still need POs? Prevents POs stuck in draft that delay procurement.

Key Information Stored: PO number, Supplier, Requisition reference, Items and quantities, Total amount, Created date, Days pending, Reason for hold (if any), Approval status.

Project Understanding: Not Confirmed PO report shows: PO-2026-001 (Steel & Parts): DRAFT for 2 days, created from REQ-2026-00042, ₹6000, pending manager review. PO-2026-002 (Supplier-B): DRAFT for 1 day, ₹2080, waiting for Finance approval (exceeds manager limit). PO-2026-003 (Supplier-C): DRAFT for 3 days, ₹400, waiting for price negotiation with supplier. Actionable: Approve PO-001 today, prioritize Finance approval for PO-002, follow up on PO-003 negotiation.

Business Workflow: 1. Procurement manager views Not Confirmed PO 2. Shows draft POs pending action: | PO # | Supplier | Amount | Days Pending | Created | Status | Reason | |------|----------|--------|--------------|---------|--------|--------| | PO-001 | Steel | ₹6,000 | 2 days | Jul 30 | Awaiting Approval | Waiting manager review | | PO-002 | Supplier-B | ₹2,080 | 1 day | Jul 30 | Needs Finance OK | Amount > limit | | PO-003 | Supplier-C | ₹400 | 3 days | Jul 28 | On Hold | Negotiating price | | PO-004 | Supplier-D | ₹250 | 1 day | Jul 30 | Ready | No approval needed | 3. Actions needed: - PO-001: Manager reviews, approves (priority - 2 days old) - PO-002: Send to Finance Director for approval (expedite) - PO-003: Follow up on price negotiation with Supplier-C - PO-004: Confirm immediately (ready to send) 4. Workflow: - Manager approves PO-001 → Status = APPROVED - Finance approves PO-002 → Status = APPROVED - Negotiate PO-003 finalizes price → Approves → Status = APPROVED - PO-004 confirmed → Status = CONFIRMED 5. Sends POs to suppliers 6. All 4 POs now in CONFIRMED status, supplier notification sent 7. Monitors: Ensures no POs stuck > 5 days in DRAFT

▶ 📋 Release PR Status - Requisition Release Progress

What It Is: Status of requisitions through release process: from SUBMITTED awaiting approval, through approval chain, to APPROVED ready for PO generation.

Why Used in ITE: Requisitions must complete approval chain before POs generated. Need to track: Which requisitions stuck in approval? How long waiting? Who needs to approve? Prevents requisitions waiting indefinitely.

Key Information Stored: Requisition number, Job reference, Status (SUBMITTED, APPROVED, PO_CREATED), Approval chain status (who approved, who pending), Current approver (who needs to act now), Days pending at each approval level.

Project Understanding: Release PR Status shows: REQ-2026-00042: Status SUBMITTED, 1 day pending Manager approval (waiting for Rajesh Kumar). REQ-2026-00043: Status SUBMITTED, 2 days pending Finance approval (manager already approved, waiting for Finance Head). REQ-2026-00044: Status APPROVED, 0 days, ready for PO generation (all approvals done). Actionable: Remind Rajesh Kumar about REQ-00042, escalate REQ-00043 to Finance Head (overdue), generate POs for REQ-00044.

Business Workflow: 1. Requisition coordinator views Release PR Status 2. Shows requisition approval progress: | REQ # | Job | Status | Days Pending | Current Approver | Required Approvals | Next Step | |-------|-----|--------|--------------|------------------|-------------------|-----------| | REQ-00042 | Job-001 | SUBMITTED | 1 day | Mgr Rajesh | Mgr→Finance→Proc | Manager approval | | REQ-00043 | Job-002 | SUBMITTED | 2 days | Finance Head | Mgr→Finance→Proc | Finance approval | | REQ-00044 | Job-003 | APPROVED | 0 days | None | All done ✓ | Generate POs | | REQ-00045 | Job-004 | SUBMITTED | 1 day | Mgr Priya | Mgr→Finance→Proc | Manager approval | 3. Analysis: - 3 requisitions pending approval (REQ-00042, 00043, 00045) - 1 requisition approved ready for POs (REQ-00044) - REQ-00043 overdue (2 days at Finance) - escalate - REQ-00042 & 00045 normal (1 day at Manager level) 4. Actions: - Send reminder to Rajesh Kumar: "REQ-00042 awaiting your approval" - Escalate to CFO: "REQ-00043 Finance approval overdue" - Send reminder to Priya: "REQ-00045 awaiting your approval" - Generate POs for REQ-00044 immediately 5. Monitors: Approval cycle targets - Manager approval: Target < 1 day - Finance approval: Target < 2 days - Procurement: Target < 1 day (auto-generate POs) 6. Tracks: Average approval time to identify bottlenecks

▶ 🔄 Alternative Supplier - Backup Sourcing

What It Is: View of alternative suppliers for items when primary supplier unavailable. Shows backup options with pricing and lead time.

Why Used in ITE: Sometimes primary supplier cannot deliver on time or quality issues. Need immediate alternative. System must show: Who else supplies this item? What's their price and lead time? Can we get it in time?

Key Information Stored: Item name, Primary supplier (current), Alternative suppliers (list), Price comparison (primary vs. alternatives), Lead time comparison, Quality rating, Inventory availability (can ship today?).

Project Understanding: Primary supplier (Supplier-B) for Bearing cannot deliver by expected date (late delivery). System shows alternatives: Supplier-A (₹520/unit, 5-day lead time, stock available), Supplier-C (₹540/unit, 4-day lead time, stock available), Supplier-D (₹510/unit, 6-day lead time, low stock). Recommendation: Use Supplier-A (best price ₹520, fast lead time 5 days, ensures on-time delivery). PO modified to use Supplier-A instead of Supplier-B.

Business Workflow: 1. Late delivery discovered for Bearing (Supplier-B delayed) 2. Manufacturing needs Bearing by July 35 (3 days from now) 3. Procurement opens Alternative Supplier view 4. Item: Bearing, Qty: 4 units 5. Searches for alternatives to Supplier-B 6. Results: | Supplier | Unit Price | Lead Time | Delivery by | Quality | Stock | Preference | |----------|-----------|-----------|-----------|---------|-------|-----------| | Supplier-A | ₹520 | 5 days | Jul 35 | 4.8★ | 100+ | ✓ RECOMMENDED | | Supplier-C | ₹540 | 4 days | Jul 34 | 3.5★ | 10 | Earlier but lower quality | | Supplier-D | ₹510 | 6 days | Jul 36 | 4.5★ | 2 | Too late | 7. Decision logic: - Supplier-A: Good price ₹520, meets deadline Jul 35, good quality 4.8★, stock available ✓ - Supplier-C: Earlier (Jul 34) but lower quality 3.5★, price higher ₹540 - Supplier-D: Cheapest ₹510 but delivers Jul 36 (1 day late) 8. Chooses Supplier-A 9. Modifies PO: Supplier-B → Supplier-A 10. Calls Supplier-A: Confirms 5-day lead time 11. PO sent to Supplier-A 12. Manufacturing schedule confirmed: Materials arrive on time

▶ 🎯 PO by Job Number - Job-wise Order Status

What It Is: Purchase orders grouped by job. Shows which orders needed for which jobs and delivery status.

Why Used in ITE: Manufacturing manager needs to know: What materials ordered for my job? Have they arrived? Can I start manufacturing? Grouping by job makes it clear what's needed for specific job.

Key Information Stored: Job number, Requisition reference, All POs for this job, Items in each PO, Total PO value, Delivery status (received, pending, late), Ready to manufacture flag (all materials received?).

Project Understanding: Job-001 materials summary: Requisition REQ-00042, Total materials ₹9870. PO-001 (Steel & Parts): Motor + Shaft, ₹6000, Status RECEIVED ✓. PO-002 (Supplier-B): Bearing, ₹2080, Status IN_TRANSIT (expected Jul 35) ⏳. PO-003 (Supplier-C): Oil Seal, ₹400, Status RECEIVED ✓. PO-004 (Supplier-D): Fasteners, ₹250, Status RECEIVED ✓. Status: 3/4 POs received, 1 PO pending. Recommendation: Wait 1 more day for Bearing, then all materials ready for manufacturing start.

Business Workflow: 1. Manufacturing manager views PO by Job Number 2. Searches: Job-001 3. Shows all materials for Job-001: - Requisition: REQ-00042, ₹9870 total - PO Summary: | PO # | Supplier | Items | Amount | Status | Received | |------|----------|-------|--------|--------|----------| | PO-001 | Steel | Motor, Shaft | ₹6,000 | RECEIVED | ✓ | | PO-002 | Supplier-B | Bearing | ₹2,080 | IN_TRANSIT | Pending (Jul 35) | | PO-003 | Supplier-C | Oil Seal | ₹400 | RECEIVED | ✓ | | PO-004 | Supplier-D | Fasteners | ₹250 | RECEIVED | ✓ | 4. Completion status: - Materials received: 3/4 POs ✓ - Materials pending: 1/4 POs (Bearing, expected Jul 35) - Job ready for manufacturing: NO (waiting for Bearing) - Estimated ready date: Jul 35 5. Can drill-down: Click PO to see detailed delivery status 6. Decision: - Currently received: Motor Assembly + Oil Seal + Fasteners - Could start assembly prep while waiting for Bearing - Will start full production once Bearing arrives Jul 35 7. Monitors: Updates as each PO delivered 8. Final status: All materials received, Manufacturing can start immediately

⚡ Complex Algorithms

Core Business Logic & Calculation Engines

1️⃣ Bill of Materials (BOM) Explosion Algorithm

Purpose: Recursively expand product BOM to calculate all materials needed for manufacturing.

Complexity: O(n log n) where n = total items in hierarchy

Usage: Requisition creation, material planning, cost estimation

Example: Motor Assembly needs: Motor (1), Bearing (4), Shaft (1), Oil Seal (4)
Bearing is sub-assembly that needs: Steel (8), Lubricant (0.5L), Fastener (12)
System expands to all leaf items: Motor (1), Steel (8×4=32), Lubricant (0.5×4=2L), Fastener (12×4=48), Shaft (1), Oil Seal (4)
Result: Single motor assembly requirement = Motor 1 + Steel 32 + Lubricant 2L + Fastener 48 + Shaft 1 + Oil Seal 4

2️⃣ Preferred Supplier Selection Algorithm

Purpose: Intelligently select optimal supplier based on lead time, price, quality, and availability.

Logic: Sort by sequence, filter by delivery feasibility, select primary supplier

Usage: Auto-grouping requisition items for PO creation

Decision Tree:
1. Get item's preferred suppliers (ranked by sequence)
2. Filter by: Can deliver by required date? (lead time check)
3. Filter by: Minimum order quantity met?
4. Filter by: Stock available or can manufacture?
5. Select first in priority order (primary supplier)
6. If primary unavailable, fallback to secondary (backup supplier)
Example: Bearing needed by July 35. Supplier-A (5-day lead time, ready to ship) ✓, Supplier-B (7-day lead time, can't make it) ✗. Auto-select Supplier-A.

3️⃣ Budget Tracking & Alert Algorithm

Purpose: Track job spending in real-time and trigger alerts at budget thresholds.

Formula: Remaining = Budget - (Material Cost + Labor Cost + Overhead)

Alert Triggers: 80%, 95%, 100% (escalating notifications)

Real-Time Tracking:
Job-001 Budget: ₹100,000
Material requisition: ₹40,000 → Committed (spent % = 40%) ⚠️ First alert at 40% (commit impact)
PO confirmed: Amount reserved → Spent = ₹40,000 (40%) ✓ Monitor
Material received (GRN): ₹40,000 → Spent = ₹40,000 (40%) ✓ Same
Material issued: ₹30,000 → Spent = ₹40,000 actual (30% used, 10% pending) ✓ In budget
Labor costs tracked: ₹45,000 → Spent = ₹40K material + ₹45K labor = ₹85,000 (85%) 🔔 Alert triggered!
Additional labor: ₹18,000 → Total = ₹103,000 (103%) 🔴 OVER BUDGET

4️⃣ Job Status Transition Validation Algorithm

Purpose: Enforce workflow rules for job state changes, prevent illegal transitions.

Logic: Check JobTransitionConfig, verify no active holds, validate approval status

Usage: Controlled job lifecycle progression

Validation Steps:
1. User requests: Job transition from OPEN → IN_PROGRESS
2. Check JobTransitionConfig: Is this transition allowed? (OPEN→IN_PROGRESS) ✓ Yes
3. Check job holds: Any active holds? Yes (Materials not ready) ✗ Transition blocked
4. Release hold: Materials received
5. Retry transition: OPEN → IN_PROGRESS ✓ Allowed now
6. Check approvals: Needs approval? (config says yes)
7. Create approval request: Manager must approve before transition
8. Manager approves → Status changes to IN_PROGRESS
Result: Prevents illegal transitions, ensures prerequisites met (materials ready, approvals given)

5️⃣ Multi-Level Approval Routing Algorithm

Purpose: Route approvals through designated hierarchy based on amount and job type.

Logic: Check amount limit, route to appropriate approver, track approval chain

Usage: Requisition approval, job approval, purchase order authorization

Approval Chain Example:
Requisition amount: ₹50,000
Step 1: Route to Department Manager (limit: ₹100K) → Approval received ✓
Step 2: Route to Department Head (limit: ₹500K) → Approval received ✓
Step 3: Route to Finance Manager (limit: ₹1M) → Approval received ✓
Step 4: Route to Procurement (auto-generate POs) ✓
vs. High-value requisition ₹1.5M:
Step 1: Department Manager (limit ₹100K) → Can't approve, route to Head
Step 2: Department Head (limit ₹500K) → Can't approve, route to Finance
Step 3: Finance Manager (limit ₹1M) → Can't approve, route to CFO
Step 4: CFO (limit: unlimited) ✓ Approves

6️⃣ Automatic PO Grouping Algorithm

Purpose: Group requisition items by preferred supplier to minimize POs and shipping costs.

Logic: Group items by supplier, create separate PO per supplier

Usage: Post-requisition approval, auto-generates purchase orders

Grouping Example:
Requisition with 8 items from 4 suppliers:
Motor (Supplier-A), Bearing (Supplier-B), Shaft (Supplier-A), Oil Seal (Supplier-C), Fastener (Supplier-D), Lubricant (Supplier-C), Paint (Supplier-B), Gasket (Supplier-A)
Grouped by supplier:
PO-001 (Supplier-A): Motor, Shaft, Gasket [3 items, 1 PO]
PO-002 (Supplier-B): Bearing, Paint [2 items, 1 PO]
PO-003 (Supplier-C): Oil Seal, Lubricant [2 items, 1 PO]
PO-004 (Supplier-D): Fastener [1 item, 1 PO]
Result: 8 items consolidated into 4 POs (one per supplier), reduces shipping & handling, optimizes costs

7️⃣ Inventory Quantity & Aging Calculation

Purpose: Track inventory levels across locations and calculate aging for slow-moving stock.

Formula: Stock Level = Opening + Received - Issued - Returned - Damaged

Aging: Current Date - Receive Date for each unit

Real-Time Calculation:
Motor Stock (MAIN-BNG location):
Opening: 10 units
Received Jul 1: 5 units (age: 29 days)
Received Jul 15: 8 units (age: 15 days)
Issued Jul 20: 10 units (reducing oldest first)
Current: 13 units
Aging breakdown: 5 old units (29 days) + 8 new units (15 days)
Report shows: 13 units total, 38% old stock (5/13), average age 21 days

8️⃣ Warranty Period & Expiration Tracking

Purpose: Track warranty periods post-delivery and alert before expiration.

Logic: Warranty Start = Delivery Date, End = Start + Warranty Period, Auto-close after expiry

Usage: Warranty claim management, customer support

Example Timeline:
Job-001 Completed: July 30, 2026
Warranty Period: 12 months
Warranty Start: July 30, 2026
Warranty End: July 29, 2027
Days Remaining: 365 days (100%)
Jul 30, 2026 (Day 1): Warranty record created
Jan 30, 2027 (Day 184): Mid-warranty check (6 months in)
Jul 15, 2027 (Day 350): Alert 14 days before expiration
Jul 29, 2027 (Day 365): Warranty expires, auto-closed

🗄️ Database Architecture

PostgreSQL 14+ Schema & Table Relationships

📊 Database Overview

Database Type: PostgreSQL 14+

Migration Tool: Flyway (SQL-based versioning)

Total Tables: 95+

Multi-Tenancy Strategy: Shared schema with organization_id row-level filtering

Auditing: Hibernate Envers with complete change history

📐 Entity Relationship Diagram (Interactive SVG with Zoom)

Zoom: 100%
xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" style="background: white; border-radius: 8px; box-shadow: 0 4px 15px rgba(0,0,0,0.1); display: block; margin: 0 auto; min-height: 600px;"> ITE Database Entity Relationships (95+ Tables) 🏢 ORGANIZATION (Tenant Root) PK: org_id | org_name | tax_id | subscription_level | currency 👤 USERS PK: user_id | org_id(FK) email | department_id designation_id 🔐 ROLES PK: role_id | role_name ADMIN, MANAGER FINANCE, WORKER 🏪 DEPT PK: dept_id | org_id dept_name manager_id(FK) 🚚 SUPPLIER PK: supplier_id org_id(FK) | payment_terms credit_limit | rating 📦 ITEM PK: item_id org_id(FK) | item_type_id unit_id | manuf_id 👥 CUSTOMER PK: customer_id org_id(FK) | company credit_limit 🎯 JOB PK: job_id | org_id customer_id | status budget, created_date 📋 REQUISITION PK: req_id | org_id job_id | status total_amount 🛒 PO PK: po_id | org_id req_id | supplier_id status | total_amount 📦 GRN PK: grn_id | org_id po_id | received_date status (OK/REJECT) 🏭 MI PK: mi_id | org_id job_id | issued_date issued_by | status 📊 STOCK PK: stock_id | org_id item_id | location_id qty_available 💰 BUDGET PK: budget_id job_id(FK) | spent remaining 🔓 HOLD PK: hold_id job_id(FK) hold_reason ✅ APPROVAL PK: approval_id job_id | approver_id status 1:M 1:M 1:M 1:M 1:1 1:M M:1 M:1 1:M 1:M 1:M 1:1 1:M 📋 Table Categories: ■ User Management (7 tables) ■ Sales/Requisition (4 tables) ■ Masters/Reference (15 tables) ■ Warehouse/Inventory (6 tables) ■ Job Lifecycle (8 tables) → Multi-tenancy relationships → Primary business flows → Reference data links

🎯 Entity Relationship Summary

Root Entity: ORGANIZATION table serves as multi-tenancy root for all 95+ tables with org_id foreign key

User Management: USERS → ROLES (M:M via ROLEACCESS) → DEPARTMENT creates complete organizational hierarchy

Primary Sales Flow: CUSTOMER → JOB → REQUISITION → PURCHASE_ORDER → GRN → MATERIAL_ISSUE → STOCK tracks order lifecycle

Master Data: SUPPLIER and ITEM act as reference catalogs; MANUFACTURER provides product information; UNIT standardizes measurements

Job Governance: JOB_BUDGET_ACTUAL tracks spending, JOB_HOLD manages blockers, APPROVAL_REQUEST enforces multi-level approvals, JOB_WARRANTY tracks post-delivery

Data Isolation: Every table includes org_id for automatic row-level filtering; Hibernate Envers audits all changes with REVINFO and entity_AUD tables

📝 SQL Schema: Key Table Definitions

User Management Tables

-- ORGANIZATION (Multi-tenancy root) CREATE TABLE organization ( org_id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY, org_code VARCHAR(50) UNIQUE NOT NULL, org_name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL, tax_id VARCHAR(50) UNIQUE NOT NULL, country VARCHAR(100), currency_code VARCHAR(3) DEFAULT 'INR', fiscal_year_start INT DEFAULT 1, is_active BOOLEAN DEFAULT TRUE, created_date TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP ); -- USERS (all rows have org_id for multi-tenancy) CREATE TABLE users ( user_id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY, org_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES organization(org_id), email VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE NOT NULL, first_name VARCHAR(100), last_name VARCHAR(100), department_id BIGINT, designation_id BIGINT, is_active BOOLEAN DEFAULT TRUE, last_login_date TIMESTAMP, created_date TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, created_by BIGINT REFERENCES users(user_id) ); CREATE INDEX idx_users_org_id ON users(org_id); CREATE INDEX idx_users_email ON users(email); -- CREDENTIAL (Passwords - NOT audited for security) CREATE TABLE credential ( credential_id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY, user_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(user_id), password_hash VARCHAR(500) NOT NULL, password_updated_date TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, failed_login_attempts INT DEFAULT 0, locked_until TIMESTAMP ); -- ROLES (Predefined permission groups) CREATE TABLE roles ( role_id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY, role_code VARCHAR(50) UNIQUE NOT NULL, role_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL, description TEXT, approval_limit DECIMAL(15,2), is_active BOOLEAN DEFAULT TRUE ); -- ROLEACCESS (M:M junction - Users to Roles) CREATE TABLE roleaccess ( roleaccess_id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY, user_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(user_id), role_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES roles(role_id), assigned_date TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, assigned_by BIGINT REFERENCES users(user_id), UNIQUE(user_id, role_id) ); CREATE INDEX idx_roleaccess_user_id ON roleaccess(user_id);

Masters & Procurement Tables

-- ITEM (Product master) CREATE TABLE item ( item_id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY, org_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES organization(org_id), item_code VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL, item_name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL, item_type_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES itemtype(item_type_id), manufacturer_id BIGINT, unit_id BIGINT NOT NULL, reorder_level INT, reorder_quantity INT, unit_price DECIMAL(15,2), is_active BOOLEAN DEFAULT TRUE, UNIQUE(org_id, item_code) ); CREATE INDEX idx_item_org_id ON item(org_id); -- SUPPLIER (Vendor master - multi-tenant) CREATE TABLE supplier ( supplier_id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY, org_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES organization(org_id), supplier_code VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL, company_name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL, tax_id VARCHAR(50), payment_terms_days INT DEFAULT 30, credit_limit DECIMAL(15,2), on_time_delivery_percent DECIMAL(5,2), quality_rating DECIMAL(3,2), is_active BOOLEAN DEFAULT TRUE, created_date TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, UNIQUE(org_id, supplier_code) ); CREATE INDEX idx_supplier_org_id ON supplier(org_id); -- PURCHASE_ORDER CREATE TABLE purchase_order ( po_id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY, org_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES organization(org_id), req_id BIGINT REFERENCES requisition(req_id), po_number VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL, supplier_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES supplier(supplier_id), po_date DATE NOT NULL, delivery_date DATE NOT NULL, total_amount DECIMAL(15,2) NOT NULL, status VARCHAR(50) DEFAULT 'DRAFT', is_active BOOLEAN DEFAULT TRUE, UNIQUE(org_id, po_number) ); CREATE INDEX idx_po_org_id ON purchase_order(org_id); CREATE INDEX idx_po_status ON purchase_order(status);

Requisitions & Job Tables

-- REQUISITION (Material request from jobs) CREATE TABLE requisition ( req_id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY, org_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES organization(org_id), job_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES job(job_id), req_number VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL, status VARCHAR(50) DEFAULT 'DRAFT', total_amount DECIMAL(15,2), submitted_date TIMESTAMP, submitted_by BIGINT REFERENCES users(user_id), UNIQUE(org_id, req_number) ); CREATE INDEX idx_req_org_id ON requisition(org_id); CREATE INDEX idx_req_job_id ON requisition(job_id); -- REQUISITION_ITEM CREATE TABLE requisition_item ( req_item_id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY, req_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES requisition(req_id), item_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES item(item_id), qty_required INT NOT NULL, unit_price DECIMAL(15,2), line_total DECIMAL(15,2) ); -- JOB (Sales Order / Manufacturing Job) CREATE TABLE job ( job_id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY, org_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES organization(org_id), job_number VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL, customer_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES customer(customer_id), job_type_id BIGINT, status VARCHAR(50) DEFAULT 'DRAFT', description TEXT, quantity INT, material_budget DECIMAL(15,2), labor_budget DECIMAL(15,2), overhead_budget DECIMAL(15,2), total_budget DECIMAL(15,2), delivery_date DATE, created_date TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, created_by BIGINT REFERENCES users(user_id), UNIQUE(org_id, job_number) ); CREATE INDEX idx_job_org_id ON job(org_id); CREATE INDEX idx_job_status ON job(status); CREATE INDEX idx_job_customer_id ON job(customer_id);

Warehouse & Inventory Tables

-- GRN (Goods Receipt Note) CREATE TABLE grn ( grn_id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY, org_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES organization(org_id), po_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES purchase_order(po_id), grn_number VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL, received_date DATE NOT NULL, received_by BIGINT REFERENCES users(user_id), status VARCHAR(50) DEFAULT 'DRAFT', UNIQUE(org_id, grn_number) ); CREATE INDEX idx_grn_org_id ON grn(org_id); -- MATERIAL_ISSUE (Materials allocated to jobs) CREATE TABLE material_issue ( mi_id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY, org_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES organization(org_id), job_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES job(job_id), issue_number VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL, issued_date DATE NOT NULL, issued_by BIGINT REFERENCES users(user_id), received_by BIGINT REFERENCES users(user_id), status VARCHAR(50) DEFAULT 'DRAFT', UNIQUE(org_id, issue_number) ); CREATE INDEX idx_mi_org_id ON material_issue(org_id); CREATE INDEX idx_mi_job_id ON material_issue(job_id); -- STOCK (Current inventory levels) CREATE TABLE stock ( stock_id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY, org_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES organization(org_id), item_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES item(item_id), location_id BIGINT NOT NULL, qty_available INT DEFAULT 0, received_date TIMESTAMP, last_issued_date TIMESTAMP, UNIQUE(org_id, item_id, location_id) ); CREATE INDEX idx_stock_org_id ON stock(org_id); CREATE INDEX idx_stock_item_id ON stock(item_id);

Table Purpose Records Key Relationship
item Product master (all items) ~500-5000 item_id → item_type_id, manufacturer_id
itemtype Item classification ~10-20 RAW_MATERIAL, COMPONENT, CONSUMABLE, FINISHED_GOOD
manufacturer Item manufacturers ~50-200 manufacturer_id ← item (M:M via junction table)
supplier Material vendors ~100-500 supplier_id ← po (supplier)
unit Measurement units ~20-30 unit_code (KG, PCS, LTR, MTR, DZN, BOX)
currency Supported currencies ~15-20 currency_code (INR, USD, EUR, GBP), exchange_rate
location Warehouse locations ~5-20 location_id → grn (receive location)
customer Customer master ~100-1000 customer_id ← job (customer)
customerlocation Multi-location customers ~200-2000 customer_id (FK) → job (ship_to_location)

📋 Procurement (15 tables)

Table Purpose Key Fields Typical Rows
requisition Material requisitions req_id (PK), job_id (FK), status, total_amount, created_date ~50-500/month
requisitionitem Requisition line items req_item_id (PK), req_id (FK), item_id (FK), qty, unit_price ~200-2000/month
purchaseorder Purchase orders po_id (PK), requisition_id (FK), supplier_id (FK), status, total_amount ~50-200/month
purchaseorderitem PO line items po_item_id (PK), po_id (FK), item_id (FK), qty_ordered, unit_price, qty_received ~200-1000/month
purchaseorderstatus PO status history po_status_id (PK), po_id (FK), status, changed_date, changed_by ~150-600/month

📦 Warehouse/Stores (10 tables)

Table Purpose Rows/Updates Audit
grn Goods Receipt Notes ~100-500/month ✅ Full audit trail
grnitem GRN line items ~500-2000/month ✅ Audited
materialissue Material issues to jobs ~200-1000/month ✅ Audited
materialissueitem Issue line items ~1000-5000/month ✅ Audited
materialreturn Material returns ~50-200/month ✅ Audited
