⚙️ Job Lifecycle (12 tables)

Table Purpose Relationships
job Core job records job_id (PK), customer_id (FK), job_type_id (FK), status, budget
jobstatus Predefined statuses DRAFT, QUOTE, APPROVED, OPEN, IN_PROGRESS, REVIEW, COMPLETED, WARRANTY, CLOSED
jobstatusconfig Status workflow config Defines allowed transitions, required approvals per status
jobtransitionconfig Transition rules From_status → To_status validation rules
jobhold Job holds/delays job_id (FK), hold_type_id (FK), reason, created_date, released_date
jobbudgetactual Real-time cost tracking job_id (FK), material_cost, labor_cost, total_spent, budget_remaining
jobrevision Scope change history job_id (FK), revision_num, description, approved, revised_budget
jobwarranty Warranty tracking job_id (FK), start_date, end_date, claim_count, total_claim_amount
approvalrequest Approval routing job_id (FK), approval_level, approver_id (FK), status, approved_date

🔑 Key Relationships & Constraints

Customer → Shipping Address: One customer can have multiple shipping addresses (1:M)
Item → Manufacturer: One item can have multiple manufacturers (M:M via junction)
Item → Supplier: One item sourced from multiple suppliers (M:M via preferred_supplier)
Job → Requisition: One job triggers one requisition (1:1)
Requisition → PO: One requisition generates multiple POs (1:M by supplier grouping)
PO → GRN: PO compared with GRN for receipt verification (1:M as partial deliveries)
GRN → Material Issue: Received materials issued to jobs (M:M)
Job → Job Hold: Job can have multiple holds at different times (1:M)
Job → Warranty: Completed job creates one warranty record (1:1)

🗃️ Audit & Compliance Tables

Table Purpose Contains
revinfo Hibernate Envers revision information revision_id (PK), timestamp, username (who made change)
{table}_AUD Audit table for each entity Copy of all columns + revision_id, revtype (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE)
jobauditlog Job-specific audit job_id, status_change, changed_by, changed_date, old_value, new_value

🔐 Multi-Tenancy Implementation

Strategy: Shared schema with organization_id column in all tables

Isolation: Row-level filtering ensures data isolation per tenant

Implementation: TenantContext interceptor adds organization_id to all queries automatically

Security: Impossible to access data from other organizations (database-level enforcement)

📈 Performance Indexes

Indexes created on:
- organization_id (every table - multi-tenancy)
- job_id, requisition_id, po_id (frequent lookups)
- customer_id, supplier_id (many joins)
- status, created_date (filtering/sorting)
- item_id, location_id (stock queries)
Result: Query performance < 100ms typical, even with millions of historical records

📄 Complete Project Summary & Understanding

15 Key Points to Understand ITE Project

🎯 What is ITE?

ITE is an integrated ERP system that automates and unifies all business operations for manufacturing organizations. It eliminates manual processes, ensures compliance, prevents errors, and provides real-time visibility into business performance.

📌 15 Key Points to Understand ITE Project

1. Multi-Tenant Architecture: Multiple organizations use same system but data completely isolated. Organization A cannot see Organization B's data even with admin privileges. Achieved via organization_id column on every table.
2. Complete Order-to-Cash Automation: Customer order enters system → Requisition auto-created → Multi-level approval → PO auto-generated → Goods received → Material issued → Manufacturing → QA → Delivery → Warranty tracking. Zero manual data entry between steps.
3. Multi-Level Approval Workflow: Large requisitions routed through hierarchy: Manager (₹10K limit) → Head (₹50K limit) → Finance (₹100K limit) → Procurement (unlimited). Prevents unauthorized spending and ensures financial control.
4. Role-Based Access Control (RBAC): 7 predefined roles with specific permissions. User can have multiple roles. Permissions are additive (union of all role permissions). Ensures security and audit compliance.
5. Real-Time Budget Tracking: Job allocated ₹500,000 budget. System tracks: Committed (POs created), Actual (goods received/used). Alerts at 80%, 95%, 100% utilization. Prevents budget overruns which impact profitability.
6. Automatic Supplier Grouping: When requisition has items from multiple suppliers, system automatically groups by preferred supplier and creates separate POs. Example: 100 items grouped by 5 suppliers = 5 POs. Saves procurement time.
7. Complete Audit Trail (Hibernate Envers): Every change to any entity logged with user, timestamp, before/after values. Cannot be modified or deleted. Compliance requirement for manufacturing industry.
8. BOM Explosion Algorithm: Hierarchical Bill of Materials recursively expanded. Example: Product has Sub-Assembly A (qty=2) which contains Item X (qty=5). For 10 units: System calculates 10×2×5 = 100 units of Item X. Prevents manual calculation errors.
9. Preferred Supplier Auto-Selection: Each item has list of suppliers ranked by preference. System checks: delivery date within timeline? Yes. Quantity ≥ minimum buy? Yes. Selects first feasible supplier. Reduces procurement manual work.
10. Status Transition Validation: Job cannot skip states (cannot jump DRAFT directly to COMPLETED). Workflow rules enforce: DRAFT → QUOTE → OPEN → IN_PROGRESS etc. If hold placed, status transition blocked. Prevents data corruption.
11. Job Holds with Reason Tracking: Manufacturing paused due to material shortage (reason: MATERIAL_SHORTAGE). System tracks pause date and reason. QA issues (reason: QUALITY_ISSUE) puts on hold. Prevents jobs from progressing in wrong state.
12. Warranty Post-Delivery Tracking: After job completion, warranty automatically created for 12 months. Any customer issues tracked against warranty. Post-warranty support charged. Improves customer relationships and prevents warranty disputes.
13. Real-Time Inventory Tracking: GRN (goods receipt) increases stock. Material Issue decreases stock. System knows exactly what's available at each warehouse location. Prevents stockouts and enables just-in-time ordering.
14. Automation Rules Engine: Events trigger automatic actions. Job Completed → Create Warranty. Budget 80% → Alert Finance. Material Received → Notify Warehouse. Reduces manual notifications and ensures timely responses.
15. Performance Dashboards & Reports: Executive sees real-time: Job status distribution, supplier on-time delivery %, budget variance, late materials impacting schedules. Data-driven decision making replaces gut feel guessing.

Complete End-to-End Workflow

CUSTOMER ORDER ↓ Sales creates Job (DRAFT) ↓ Job approved, status → OPEN ↓ System auto-creates Requisition ↓ Requisition routed for Multi-Level Approval (Manager → Head → Finance → Procurement) ↓ System auto-creates Purchase Orders (grouped by supplier) ↓ Supplier delivers materials ↓ Warehouse receives, creates GRN, verifies quantities, inspects quality ↓ Manufacturing requests materials, warehouse issues from stock ↓ Workers execute job, update status, log time ↓ QA inspects finished goods ↓ Job completed, Warranty tracking begins ↓ Warranty period ends, Job fully closed

Business Benefits

Benefit Impact
Efficiency Eliminates manual data entry, automates approvals, reduces processing time from days to hours
Cost Control Real-time budget monitoring prevents overruns, tracks spending, identifies savings
Visibility Dashboards show real-time job status, delivery status, budget position, supplier performance
Compliance Complete audit trail for regulatory requirements, fraud prevention, accountability
Quality Built-in quality checkpoints ensure standards compliance

System Statistics

  • ✅ 12 Modules covering complete business processes
  • ✅ 7 Built-In Roles with customizable permissions
  • ✅ Multi-Tenant Architecture supporting multiple organizations
  • ✅ Complete Audit Trail for compliance and accountability
  • ✅ Real-Time Dashboards for executive visibility
  • ✅ Automated Workflows reducing manual processes

✓ TC-001: Organization Profile - Create
Database Table: organization

📋 Test Case Description

Create a new organization with unique code and validate all master data for the organization.

🗄️ Database Schema & Fields

Field Name Data Type Status Constraint/Validation Database Constraint
org_id INT Required * Auto-increment PRIMARY KEY, AUTO_INCREMENT
org_name VARCHAR(255) Required * Unique, Length 1-255 UNIQUE, NOT NULL
org_code VARCHAR(50) Required * Unique, Alphanumeric UNIQUE, NOT NULL, INDEX
business_type VARCHAR(100) Required * Enum (Manufacturing/Trading/Services) NOT NULL, INDEX
country VARCHAR(100) Optional Length 0-100 -
currency VARCHAR(10) Required * Enum (USD, INR, GBP, EUR) NOT NULL
created_by VARCHAR(100) Required * Valid User ID FK -> users(user_id), NOT NULL
created_at TIMESTAMP Required * Auto-set on creation DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
updated_at TIMESTAMP Required * Auto-update on modification ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP

⚡ Event Triggers

TRIGGER on_organization_create
TRIGGER validate_unique_org_code
TRIGGER audit_log_organization
TRIGGER initialize_org_settings

✅ Validation Rules

Organization name must be unique across system
Organization code must follow pattern: [A-Z]{3,10}
Business type must be from predefined enum list
Currency must be valid ISO 4217 code
Creator user must exist and have admin privileges

🧪 Test Steps

Create organization with valid data
Verify org_id auto-increments correctly
Attempt duplicate org_name - should FAIL
Attempt duplicate org_code - should FAIL
Verify created_at timestamp is auto-set
Verify audit log entry is created

📊 Expected Results

Success Case: Organization created with all fields populated, ID auto-generated, timestamps set, audit log created

Failure Cases: Duplicate code/name rejected, invalid enum rejected, missing required fields rejected

✏️ UPDATE Operation

API Endpoint: PUT /api/organization/{org_id}

Request Body:

{
									"org_name": "ABC Manufacturing Ltd",
									"country": "Canada",
									"currency": "CAD"
								}

Success Response (HTTP 200):

{
									"status": "SUCCESS",

									"audit_log_id": 5002
								}

Database Impact: UPDATE organization table, update org_name/country/currency fields, set updated_at timestamp, create audit log entry

🗑️ DELETE Operation

API Endpoint: DELETE /api/organization/{org_id}

Constraints: Cannot delete if users/roles/departments exist | Soft delete: is_deleted=true

Success Response (HTTP 204): No Content

Database Impact: UPDATE organization SET is_deleted=true, deleted_at=NOW()

On Failure (HTTP 400/409):

{
								"status": "FAILED",
								"error_code": "CANNOT_DELETE_ORGANIZATION_WITH_USERS",
								"message": "Organization has 5 users. Cannot delete.",
								"details": {
									"user_count": 5,
									"role_count": 3
								}
							}

✅ VALIDATE Operation

Validation Rules:

  • org_name must be UNIQUE across system, max 255 chars, required
  • org_code must be UNIQUE, match pattern [A-Z]{3,10}, required
  • business_type must be from ENUM: Manufacturing, Trading, Services
  • currency must be valid ISO 4217 code (USD, INR, GBP, EUR, etc.)
  • country must be valid country name or code if provided
  • created_by must reference existing user with admin privileges

Error Codes & HTTP Status:

  • HTTP 409 CONFLICT: DUPLICATE_ORG_NAME | DUPLICATE_ORG_CODE
  • HTTP 400 BAD_REQUEST: INVALID_ENUM_VALUE | INVALID_CURRENCY_CODE | MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD | INVALID_ORG_CODE_FORMAT
  • HTTP 404 NOT_FOUND: USER_NOT_FOUND | INVALID_COUNTRY

⏮️ ROLLBACK Operation

Transaction Rollback Scenarios:

  • org_name validation fails → ROLLBACK entire INSERT transaction
  • org_code UNIQUE constraint violated → ROLLBACK and return 409 DUPLICATE_ORG_CODE
  • business_type enum validation fails → ROLLBACK, return 400 INVALID_ENUM_VALUE
  • currency validation fails → ROLLBACK, return 400 INVALID_CURRENCY_CODE
  • created_by user validation fails → ROLLBACK, return 404 USER_NOT_FOUND
  • audit_log creation fails → ROLLBACK entire transaction, send alert to admin

✨ SUCCESS RESPONSE Details

HTTP Status Codes: CREATE: 201 Created | UPDATE: 200 OK | DELETE: 204 No Content

Response JSON Structure:

  • status: "SUCCESS" (on success) or "FAILED" (on error)
  • org_id: Generated auto-increment integer
  • org_name: Organization name as sent/stored
  • org_code: Auto-generated unique code
  • business_type: Business type enum value
  • currency: ISO 4217 currency code
  • created_at/updated_at: ISO 8601 timestamp format
  • deleted_at: ISO 8601 timestamp (only on delete)
  • audit_log_id: Reference to audit log entry for tracking

Timing Requirements: Response should be returned within 500ms for normal operations

Validation Rules:

  • role_name must be UNIQUE per organization (composite key with org_id)
  • role_name required, max 100 chars
  • permissions must be valid JSON array with approved permission names
  • org_id must reference existing organization
  • Cannot assign permissions higher than creator's role level
  • System roles (Admin, User, Guest) cannot be deleted

Error Codes & HTTP Status:

  • HTTP 404 NOT_FOUND: ORGANIZATION_NOT_FOUND
  • HTTP 403 FORBIDDEN: CANNOT_DELETE_SYSTEM_ROLE

⏮️ ROLLBACK Operation

  • role_name already exists in org → ROLLBACK, return 409 DUPLICATE_ROLE_NAME_IN_ORG
  • permissions JSON invalid → ROLLBACK entire transaction, return 400 INVALID_JSON_PERMISSIONS
  • permission not in approved list → ROLLBACK, return 400 INVALID_PERMISSION_NAME
  • creator lacks permission to assign this level → ROLLBACK, return 403 PERMISSION_LEVEL_EXCEEDED
  • org_id invalid → ROLLBACK, return 404 ORGANIZATION_NOT_FOUND
  • role_permissions insert fails → ROLLBACK entire transaction, send alert

HTTP Status Codes: CREATE: 201 Created | UPDATE: 200 OK | DELETE: 204 No Content

Response JSON Structure:

  • role_id: Generated auto-increment ID
  • role_name: Role name as stored
  • org_id: Organization reference
  • permissions: Array of permission strings
  • is_active: Boolean active status
  • created_at/updated_at: ISO 8601 timestamps
  • permission_cache_invalidated: Boolean (on UPDATE)
  • audit_log_id: Reference to audit log entry

  • password fails complexity check → ROLLBACK, return 400 WEAK_PASSWORD
  • password hashing fails → ROLLBACK entire transaction, send alert to admin
  • role validation fails → ROLLBACK, return 404/403 error
  • welcome email send fails → ROLLBACK transaction, queue retry
  • user_settings creation fails → ROLLBACK entire transaction

✨ SUCCESS RESPONSE Details

HTTP Status Codes: CREATE: 201 Created | UPDATE: 200 OK | DELETE: 204 No Content

Response JSON Structure:

  • status: "SUCCESS" or "FAILED"
  • user_id: Generated auto-increment ID
  • email: User email as stored
  • username: Username as stored
  • first_name/last_name: Names as provided
  • role_id: Assigned role ID
  • is_active: Boolean active status
  • created_at/updated_at: ISO 8601 timestamps
  • welcome_email_sent: Boolean (on CREATE only)
  • permissions_updated: Boolean (on UPDATE if role changed)
  • audit_log_id: Reference to audit log entry

Password Note: Password field NEVER returned in response. Password hash is never exposed via API.

							"customer_name": "ABC Trading Company Ltd",

🗑️ DELETE Operation

API Endpoint: DELETE /api/customer/{customer_id}

Constraints: Cannot delete if active orders exist | Cannot delete if ledger balance > 0 | Soft delete: is_deleted=true

Success Response (HTTP 204): No Content

On Failure (HTTP 400/409):

{

Validation Rules:

  • Email must be UNIQUE across system, valid email format (RFC 5322)

  • Customer_name required, max 255 chars
  • Credit_limit numeric, >= 0, max 999999999.99

  • Payment_terms must be from ENUM: NET30, NET45, NET60, COD, ADVANCE

Error Codes & HTTP Status:

⏮️ ROLLBACK Operation

Transaction Rollback Scenarios:

  • Email validation fails → ROLLBACK customer insert + ledger account creation
  • Phone format invalid → ROLLBACK entire transaction
  • Country validation fails → ROLLBACK and return error
  • Customer_code generation fails → ROLLBACK and retry with different sequence
  • Ledger account creation fails → ROLLBACK customer insert, send alert to admin
  • Payment_terms enum validation fails → ROLLBACK, return error

✨ SUCCESS RESPONSE Details

HTTP Status Codes: CREATE: 201 Created | UPDATE: 200 OK | DELETE: 204 No Content

Response JSON Structure:

  • status: "SUCCESS" or "FAILED"

  • customer_code: Auto-generated unique code (CUST-YYYY-XXX format)
  • customer_name: Customer name as stored
  • email: Customer email
  • phone: Customer phone number
  • credit_limit: Credit limit amount
  • payment_terms: Payment terms enum value
  • ledger_account_created: Boolean flag (on CREATE)
  • created_at/updated_at: ISO 8601 timestamps
  • audit_log_id: Reference to audit log entry

API Endpoint: DELETE /api/job-number/{job_id}

Constraints: Cannot delete if status is Active or Completed | Only Draft or Cancelled jobs can be deleted | Soft delete: is_deleted=true

On Failure (HTTP 400/409):

{

			"recommendation": "Cancel the job before deletion"
		}

✅ VALIDATE Operation

Validation Rules:

  • Job_number format: JO-YYYY-XXXXXX (auto-generated, must be unique)
  • Customer_id must exist and be active in system
  • Job_type_id must exist and be valid for organization
  • Status must be from ENUM: Draft, Active, Completed, Cancelled, On-Hold
  • Priority must be from ENUM: Low, Medium, High, Urgent
  • Allocated_to user must exist, have permission 'handle_jobs', belong to same organization
  • Description max 1000 chars, optional
  • Job_number sequence must be contiguous and unique per organization per year

Error Codes & HTTP Status:

  • HTTP 409 CONFLICT: DUPLICATE_JOB_NUMBER | INVALID_STATUS_TRANSITION
  • HTTP 400 BAD_REQUEST: INVALID_ENUM_VALUE | MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD | INVALID_PRIORITY | INVALID_STATUS
  • HTTP 403 FORBIDDEN: USER_LACKS_PERMISSION | CANNOT_ALLOCATE_OUTSIDE_ORG
  • HTTP 404 NOT_FOUND: CUSTOMER_NOT_FOUND | JOB_TYPE_NOT_FOUND | USER_NOT_FOUND

⏮️ ROLLBACK Operation

Transaction Rollback Scenarios:

  • Customer validation fails → ROLLBACK job insert, return CUSTOMER_NOT_FOUND
  • Job_type validation fails → ROLLBACK transaction
  • Allocated user lacks permission → ROLLBACK and return PERMISSION_DENIED
  • Job_number generation fails → ROLLBACK entire creation, retry sequence
  • Status transition invalid → ROLLBACK update, return INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION
  • Notification service fails → ROLLBACK allocation, retry notification queue
  • Workflow initialization fails → ROLLBACK entire transaction

✨ SUCCESS RESPONSE Details

HTTP Status Codes: CREATE: 201 Created | UPDATE: 200 OK | DELETE: 204 No Content

Response JSON Structure:

  • status: "SUCCESS" or "FAILED"
  • job_id: Generated auto-increment integer
  • job_number: Auto-generated JO-YYYY-XXXXXX format
  • customer_id: Reference to customer
  • customer_name: Customer name for display
  • job_type_id: Reference to job type
  • current_status: Current workflow state
  • priority: Priority level from enum
  • allocated_to: User ID of assignee
  • previous_allocated_to: Previous user (on UPDATE)
  • workflow_state_updated: Boolean for status change confirmation
  • notification_sent: Boolean for user notification
  • created_at/updated_at: ISO 8601 timestamps
  • audit_log_id: Reference to audit log entry

⚙️ MASTERS MODULE

System Masters: Manufacturers, Suppliers, Units, Items, Currency

📊 Master Data Hierarchy & Relationships

🏛️ Complete Master Data Structure

ORGANIZATION (Parent Root)
				│
				├── 📦 MANUFACTURERS (1:Many)
				│   └── Products (Many reference manufacturer)
				│
				├── 🏭 SUPPLIERS (1:Many)
				│   ├── Purchase Orders
				│   └── Goods Received Notes
				│
				├── 📏 UNITS (1:Many)
				│   ├── Products (reference unit for quantities)
				│   ├── Pricing Tiers (priced per unit)
				│   └── Material Issues (measured in units)
				│
				├── 📂 ITEM TYPES (1:Many)
				│   └── Products (classified by item type)
				│
				├── 📍 LOCATIONS (1:Many)
				│   ├── Inventory Stock (stored at locations)
				│   ├── Material Issues (issued from locations)
				│   └── Goods Receipts (received at locations)
				│
				├── 💰 CURRENCIES (1:Many)
				│   ├── Organization Default Currency
				│   ├── Pricing (quoted in currencies)
				│   └── Financial Reports (converted to base currency)
				│
				├── 👥 DEPARTMENTS (1:Many)
				│   └── Users (assigned to departments)
				│
				├── 💼 DESIGNATIONS (1:Many)
				│   └── Users (assigned designations)
				│
				├── 📧 EMAIL TEMPLATES (1:Many)
				│   ├── Notifications
				│   ├── Order Confirmations
				│   └── Workflows (reference templates)
				│
				├── 🏠 SHIPPING ADDRESSES (1:Many → Customers)
				│   └── Customer → Shipping Address (delivery locations)
				│
				├── 💼 JOB BELONGS TO (1:Many)
				│   └── Jobs (classified as belongs to)
				│
				└── ⏸️ HOLD TYPES (1:Many)
						└── Job Holds (reason for hold)

🔗 Key Relationships & Dependencies

Master Type References Referenced By Delete Constraint
Manufacturers Organization Products ❌ Cannot delete if products exist
Suppliers Organization Purchase Orders, GRN ❌ Cannot delete if active POs exist
Units Organization Products, Pricing, Stock ❌ Cannot delete if products/pricing use it
Item Types Organization Products ❌ Cannot delete if products use it
Locations Organization Inventory, Stock, GRN ❌ Cannot delete if inventory exists
Currencies Organization Default Pricing, Transactions ❌ Cannot delete if base currency or active transactions
Departments Organization Users ❌ Cannot delete if users assigned
Designations Organization Users ❌ Cannot delete if users have this designation

✅ Master Data Validation Rules (All Masters)

  • Uniqueness: Code must be unique within organization (composite key: org_id + code)
  • Format: Code alphanumeric with hyphens allowed, no spaces or special chars
  • Name/Description: Required, max 255 chars for names, max 1000 for descriptions
  • Active Flag: Boolean (true/false), defaults to true on creation
  • Multi-tenancy: All masters scoped to organization (org_id foreign key)
  • Delete Constraint: Soft delete (is_deleted=true) if referenced, hard delete only if no references
  • Audit Trail: All changes logged with created_by, created_at, updated_by, updated_at timestamps
  • Cascading Updates: Changes to masters trigger updates in dependent records (e.g., currency rate changes affect pricing)
✓ TC-006: Manufacturers - Create & Manage
Database Table: manufacturers

📋 Test Case Description

Manufacturers are master data records representing companies that manufacture products. Each manufacturer is uniquely identified within an organization by a manufacturer code. Manufacturers maintain contact information (email, phone), location details (country), and performance ratings. This master data is referenced when creating products to identify their source manufacturer. Manufacturers can have multiple products linked to them, and cannot be deleted if products still reference them.

📊 Hierarchy & Relationships

Organization (Parent)
				↓
				Manufacturers (Child)
						↓
						Products (References manufacturer_id)

		Relationship: One Organization → Many Manufacturers (1 to Many)
								 One Manufacturer → Many Products (1 to Many)
		Cross-Reference: Manufacturers.manufacturer_id ← Products.manufacturer_id

CREATE: POST /api/manufacturer | {org_id, manufacturer_code, manufacturer_name, email, phone, country, contact_person, rating} | (201) {manufacturer_id, code, name, created_at}

UPDATE: PUT /api/manufacturer/{id} | Update: email, phone, contact_person, rating, is_active | (200) Success

DELETE: DELETE /api/manufacturer/{id} | Constraint: Cannot delete if products reference it | Soft delete: is_deleted=true | (204) No Content

VALIDATE: Code unique per org, email valid format, phone international format, country from master list, rating 0-5 | Errors: 409 DUPLICATE_CODE | 400 INVALID_EMAIL | 404 INVALID_COUNTRY

ROLLBACK: Email validation fails → ROLLBACK | Phone format invalid → ROLLBACK | Country validation fails → return error | Product reference check fails → return error

SUCCESS RESPONSE (201|200|204): {manufacturer_id, code, name, email, phone, country, rating, created_at, updated_at, audit_log_id}

✓ TC-007: Suppliers - Create & Manage
Database Table: suppliers

📋 Test Case Description

Suppliers are master data records representing vendors from whom the organization sources materials and products. Each supplier is uniquely identified by a supplier code within an organization. Suppliers include payment terms (NET30, NET45, etc.), lead time information (how many days for delivery), and performance ratings (0-5 stars). Suppliers are referenced in Purchase Orders and cannot be deleted if active POs exist against them. Supplier master data helps track vendor performance, manage procurement costs, and optimize supply chain operations.

				↓
				Suppliers (Child)
						↓
						Purchase Orders (References supplier_id)
						↓
						Received Goods/GRN (References supplier via PO)

		Relationship: One Organization → Many Suppliers (1 to Many)
								 One Supplier → Many Purchase Orders (1 to Many)
		Cross-Reference: Suppliers.supplier_id ← PurchaseOrders.supplier_id

CREATE: POST /api/supplier | {org_id, supplier_code, supplier_name, email, phone, payment_terms, lead_time_days, rating, is_active} | (201) {supplier_id, code, name, created_at}

UPDATE: PUT /api/supplier/{id} | Update: supplier_name, email, phone, payment_terms, lead_time_days, rating, is_active | (200)

DELETE: DELETE /api/supplier/{id} | Constraint: Cannot delete if active POs exist | Soft delete | (204)

VALIDATE: Code unique per org, payment_terms enum (NET30|NET45|NET60|COD|ADVANCE), lead_time_days > 0, rating 0-5 | Errors: 409 DUPLICATE_CODE | 400 INVALID_PAYMENT_TERMS

ROLLBACK: Payment terms validation fails → ROLLBACK | Lead time validation fails → return error | PO reference check fails → return error with count

SUCCESS RESPONSE (201|200|204): {supplier_id, code, name, payment_terms, lead_time_days, rating, audit_log_id}

✓ TC-008: Units - Create & Define
Database Table: units

📋 Test Case Description

Units are master data representing measurement units (KG, LTR, PCS, MTR, etc.) used throughout the system for measuring quantities, pricing, and stock movements. Each unit belongs to a unit type (Weight, Volume, Quantity, Length, Area) and can have conversion factors for converting between different units of the same type (e.g., 1000 grams = 1 kg). Units are referenced in products, pricing tiers, material issues, and stock management. Cannot be deleted if products or pricing still use them, or if they are base units for other units (circular dependency prevention).

📊 Hierarchy & Relationships

Organization (Parent)
				↓
				Units (Child)
						├── Products (reference unit_id for quantities)
						├── Pricing Tiers (quantity and pricing based on units)
						├── Stock Movements (material issue/receipt measured in units)
						└── Conversion Rules (units can reference other units as base_unit_id)

		Relationship: One Organization → Many Units (1 to Many)
								 One Unit → Many Products/Pricing/Stock (1 to Many)
		Conversion: Units.base_unit_id → Units.unit_id (self-reference, prevents circular)

CREATE: POST /api/unit | {org_id, unit_code, unit_name, unit_type, conversion_factor, base_unit_id} | (201) {unit_id, code, name, type, created_at}

UPDATE: PUT /api/unit/{id} | Update: unit_name, conversion_factor, base_unit_id, is_active | (200)

DELETE: DELETE /api/unit/{id} | Constraint: Cannot delete if products use it or it's base unit for others | Soft delete | (204)

VALIDATE: Code unique per org, unit_type enum (Weight|Length|Quantity|Volume|Area), conversion_factor > 0, no circular references | Errors: 409 DUPLICATE_CODE | 400 CIRCULAR_UNIT_REFERENCE

ROLLBACK: Conversion factor validation fails → ROLLBACK | Circular reference detected → ROLLBACK | Base unit not found → return 404

SUCCESS RESPONSE (201|200|204): {unit_id, code, name, type, conversion_factor, base_unit_id, audit_log_id}

ROLLBACK: HSN validation fails → ROLLBACK | Item type in use → return error | Description too long → validate and return error

🔧 CONFIGURATORS MODULE

Product Configuration: Products, Models, Items, Pricing, Assembly

📊 Product Configuration Hierarchy & Relationships

🏛️ Product Configuration Structure

PRODUCT (Base Configuration)
				├── Linked Masters
				│   ├── Manufacturer (FK to manufacturers)
				│   ├── Item Type (FK to item_types)
				│   └── Unit (FK to units)
				│
				├── MODELS (Product Variants)
				│   ├── Model Specifications (JSON)
				│   └── ITEMS (Model Line Items)
				│       ├── Item Details
				│       └── Component Reference
				│
				├── PRICING (Quantity-based Tiers)
				│   ├── Price Tier 1: 0-100 units @ $10
				│   ├── Price Tier 2: 101-500 units @ $9.50
				│   └── Price Tier 3: 500+ units @ $9.00
				│       (with effective_from/effective_to dates)
				│
				├── ASSEMBLY (Bill of Materials)
				│   ├── Component 1 (qty: 5 units)
				│   ├── Component 2 (qty: 3 units)
				│   └── Component 3 (qty: 1 unit)
				│
				└── ASSEMBLY RELEASE (Version Control)
						├── Release Version 1.0
						├── Release Version 2.0 (with change log)
						└── Release Version 3.0 (current)

		Relationship: Product (1) → Models (Many) → Items (Many)
								 Product (1) → Pricing (Many)
								 Product (1) → Assembly (Many) → Assembly Release (Many)
✓ TC-018: Products - Create & Configure
Database Table: products

📋 Test Case Description

Products are the primary master records representing items that can be bought, sold, or manufactured. Each product links to a manufacturer, item type, and measurement unit. Products are the base for all downstream configurations including models, pricing, inventory, and assembly. Creating a product automatically initializes an inventory ledger account. Products cannot be deleted if models, pricing, assembly, or inventory records exist.

CREATE: POST /api/product | {org_id, product_code, product_name, manufacturer_id, item_type_id, unit_id, description} | (201) {product_id, code, name, inventory_ledger_created, created_at}

UPDATE: PUT /api/product/{id} | Update: product_name, description, manufacturer_id, is_active | (200)

DELETE: DELETE /api/product/{id} | Constraint: Cannot delete if models/pricing/assembly/inventory exist | Soft delete | (204)

VALIDATE: Code unique per org, manufacturer exists, item_type exists, unit exists | Errors: 409 DUPLICATE_CODE | 404 MANUFACTURER_NOT_FOUND | 404 ITEM_TYPE_NOT_FOUND

ROLLBACK: FK validation fails → ROLLBACK | Inventory ledger creation fails → ROLLBACK | Code duplication → return 409

SUCCESS RESPONSE (201|200|204): {product_id, code, name, manufacturer_id, item_type_id, unit_id, inventory_ledger_id, audit_log_id}

✓ TC-019: Models - Create & Link
Database Table: product_models

📋 Test Case Description

Models represent product variants or SKUs (Stock Keeping Units). Each product can have multiple models with different specifications, colors, sizes, or configurations. Models store specifications as JSON for flexibility. Models cannot be deleted if pricing or items are configured for them.

CREATE: POST /api/model | {product_id, model_code, model_name, specifications_json} | (201) {model_id, code, name, created_at}

UPDATE: PUT /api/model/{id} | Update: model_name, specifications_json, is_active | (200)

DELETE: DELETE /api/model/{id} | Constraint: Cannot delete if pricing/items reference it | Soft delete | (204)

VALIDATE: Code unique per product, specifications valid JSON, product exists | Errors: 409 DUPLICATE_MODEL_CODE | 400 INVALID_JSON_SPECS | 404 PRODUCT_NOT_FOUND

ROLLBACK: JSON validation fails → ROLLBACK | Product FK check fails → return 404 | Pricing reference check fails → return error

SUCCESS RESPONSE (201|200|204): {model_id, product_id, code, name, specifications, created_at, audit_log_id}

✓ TC-020: Items - Create & Configure
Database Table: product_items

📋 Test Case Description

Items are the line items within a model, representing individual components or sub-items that make up a model configuration. Each item has a quantity and unit price within the context of that model. Items help break down product configurations into manageable pieces for requisitioning and purchasing.

CREATE: POST /api/item | {model_id, item_code, item_name, quantity, unit_price} | (201) {item_id, code, name, quantity, unit_price, created_at}

UPDATE: PUT /api/item/{id} | Update: item_name, quantity, unit_price, is_active | (200)

DELETE: DELETE /api/item/{id} | Constraint: Cannot delete if requisitions reference it | Soft delete | (204)

VALIDATE: Code unique per model, quantity > 0, unit_price >= 0, model exists | Errors: 409 DUPLICATE_ITEM_CODE | 400 INVALID_QUANTITY | 404 MODEL_NOT_FOUND

ROLLBACK: Quantity validation fails → ROLLBACK | Price validation fails → ROLLBACK | Model FK check fails → return 404

SUCCESS RESPONSE (201|200|204): {item_id, model_id, code, name, quantity, unit_price, total_price, audit_log_id}

✓ TC-021: Pricing - Create & Manage Tiers
Database Table: pricing_tiers

📋 Test Case Description

Pricing Tiers define quantity-based pricing for products. Different price points apply based on order quantity (e.g., 0-100 units @ $10, 101-500 @ $9.50, 500+ @ $9.00). Pricing tiers have effective date ranges for temporal pricing strategies. Old pricing is archived when new tiers are created. Quantity ranges must not overlap.

CREATE: POST /api/pricing | {product_id, qty_from, qty_to, price, effective_from, effective_to} | (201) {pricing_id, qty_from, qty_to, price, created_at}

UPDATE: PUT /api/pricing/{id} | Update: qty_from, qty_to, price, effective_dates | (200)

DELETE: DELETE /api/pricing/{id} | Archive and soft delete old pricing | (204)

VALIDATE: qty_from < qty_to, no overlapping ranges, effective_from < effective_to, price >= 0 | Errors: 409 OVERLAPPING_QTY_RANGE | 400 INVALID_DATE_RANGE

ROLLBACK: Overlap detected → ROLLBACK | Date validation fails → ROLLBACK | Price validation fails → return error

SUCCESS RESPONSE (201|200|204): {pricing_id, product_id, qty_from, qty_to, price, effective_dates, archived_count, audit_log_id}

✓ TC-022: Assembly - Create & Link
Database Table: assemblies

📋 Test Case Description

Assemblies define Bill of Materials (BoM) - the list of components needed to assemble/manufacture a product. Each assembly specifies which components are needed and in what quantities. Assemblies prevent circular dependencies (a component cannot be its own assembly). Assemblies are versioned through Assembly Releases.

CREATE: POST /api/assembly | {product_id, assembly_code, assembly_name, components_json} | (201) {assembly_id, code, name, component_count, created_at}

UPDATE: PUT /api/assembly/{id} | Update: assembly_name, components_json, is_active | (200)

DELETE: DELETE /api/assembly/{id} | Constraint: Cannot delete if assembly releases exist | Soft delete | (204)

VALIDATE: Code unique per product, components valid JSON, no circular references, product exists | Errors: 409 DUPLICATE_ASSEMBLY_CODE | 400 CIRCULAR_ASSEMBLY_REF | 400 INVALID_JSON

ROLLBACK: Circular reference detected → ROLLBACK | JSON validation fails → ROLLBACK | Product FK check fails → return 404

SUCCESS RESPONSE (201|200|204): {assembly_id, product_id, code, name, components, component_count, audit_log_id}

✓ TC-023: Assembly Release - Create & Track
Database Table: assembly_releases

📋 Test Case Description

Assembly Releases version control assemblies (BoM). Each time an assembly's components change significantly, a new release is created (v1.0, v2.0, v3.0). Only one release can be active at a time. Assembly releases track which version is in use for production, purchasing, and manufacturing. Older releases are retained for historical/audit purposes.

CREATE: POST /api/assembly-release | {assembly_id, release_version, release_date, status, change_notes} | (201) {release_id, version, status, created_at}

UPDATE: PUT /api/assembly-release/{id} | Update: status, change_notes, is_active | (200)

DELETE: DELETE /api/assembly-release/{id} | Constraint: Cannot delete active/released versions | Archive only | (204)

VALIDATE: Version unique per assembly, release_date valid, status enum (Draft|Released|Archived), assembly exists | Errors: 409 DUPLICATE_VERSION | 400 INVALID_STATUS

ROLLBACK: Status validation fails → ROLLBACK | Date validation fails → ROLLBACK | Assembly FK check fails → return 404

SUCCESS RESPONSE (201|200|204): {release_id, assembly_id, version, status, release_date, change_notes, active_version, audit_log_id}

🎯 Testing Strategies

Comprehensive strategies for system testing and quality assurance.

Strategy Components

  • Black Box Testing: Test without internal code knowledge
  • White Box Testing: Test internal code logic and paths
  • Regression Testing: Verify fixes don't break existing functionality
  • Smoke Testing: Quick verification of critical paths
  • Load Testing: Performance under concurrent users
  • Security Testing: Penetration testing and vulnerability scanning

✅ QA Process

Quality assurance procedures and testing workflows.

QA Phases

  • Phase 1 - Planning: Define test scope and strategy
  • Phase 2 - Design: Create test cases and scenarios
  • Phase 3 - Execution: Run tests and log results
  • Phase 4 - Reporting: Document findings and defects
  • Phase 5 - Closure: Verify fixes and sign off
